原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A6_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md)。SHA-256：`914f70385c2808f2e3fbb16fde140a34c662b7fa4e4560706970ff7109f2240c`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json), [A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json), [A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json), [EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### Q5 A6 by four-dimensional transfers and a zero-imbalance exception

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft. Status: a complete proposed
proof relative to the listed imported results and explicit finite positive
certificates; independent proof-checker review PENDING. This is not a
claim that full Q6 P6, or even all eight-hole P6, has been proved.

##### Claim and notation

**A6.** Let $F$ be any matching of the complete graph $K(Q_5)$ with
exactly six uncovered vertices (holes), two of one parity and four of
the other. For each specified hole $v$ in the larger class, there is a
cycle on exactly $Q_5-v$ containing $F$, all of whose edges outside $F$
are edges of $Q_5$ (short edges).

Call the two-hole parity $E$ and the four-hole parity $O$. These names
may be interchanged by translation. Required edges of $F$ may be long
or join vertices of the same parity. No argument assumes otherwise.

In a coordinate cut let $A$ contain $v$, and let $B$ be the other face.
Use global parity labels on both faces. Let $H_A,H_B$ be the original
holes, $F_A,F_B$ the internal required edges, $C$ the crossing required
edges, $c=|C|$, and $X_A,X_B$ their endpoint sets. A crossing edge need
not be short. For a vertex $t$ let $\bar t$ denote its short neighbor
across the cut, not its required partner. Write
$\delta=|H_A\cap O|-|H_A\cap E|$.

##### Dependencies and proof map

1. Full Q5 A4: [CANONICAL_A4_CLOSURE.md](#proof-canonical-a4-closure), audited in
   [CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.md](#review-canonical-completion-review).
2. Q4 N14 (two same-parity holes, avoid one), A4_4, NC_4, and the
   general GQ4-avoid/GQ4-cycle consequences in
   [Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md](#proof-q4-core-and-a4-split) and [Q4_GENERAL_AUGMENTATION.md](#proof-q4-general-augmentation).
3. Q4 T44 (four same-parity holes, avoid any two),
   [Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_TRANSFER.md](#proof-q4-two-avoided-transfer), reviewed in [Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_REVIEW.md](#review-q4-two-avoided-review).
4. Previously audited two-hole optional-short-edge union bounds L15/L18,
   and the four-hole extensions in Section 2 below.
5. The new alternate-endpoint positive certificates in Section 3.
6. The complete residual hole geometry census in Section 4, followed by
   explicit transfer proofs for every cut and the exceptional geometry.

All circle/path extension inputs preserve required edges and add only
short edges. Artificial edges used to encode paths may be arbitrary;
each such edge is removed or expanded in the final construction.

##### 1. Preprocessing and transfer conventions

If any minority hole is adjacent to a majority hole other than $v$,
add that short edge and invoke Q5 A4, avoiding $v$. Henceforth assume
there is no edge between the two minority holes and the three other
majority holes. In particular a mirror of a minority hole cannot be
an original nonforbidden majority hole, and a mirror of a nonforbidden
majority hole cannot be a minority hole.

Deleting a nonempty matching $D$ from a cycle leaves disjoint paths
whose endpoints are the endpoints of $D$. If two endpoints of a removed
edge are rejoined while at least one other gap remains, this does not
create a closed component. More generally, restoring any proper subset
of the removed edges by internally disjoint paths still leaves a path
forest. Attaching original crossings at distinct free ports and a short
bridge at a distinct chosen hole preserves this property, except for
explicit duplicated B-side bridge vertices treated below.

Compressing the resulting disjoint paths means replacing each path by
an artificial edge on its two endpoints. After a single B-side cycle
containing these artificial edges has been obtained, replacing each edge
by its path gives one cycle. Its internal vertices are pairwise disjoint
and outside the B-side cycle. This is the expansion used below.

##### 2. Four-hole optional-edge bounds

For a matching $L$ of $K(Q_4)$ let its optional-edge union be the set of
short edges outside $L$ occurring in at least one extending cycle of the
specified vertex set. No simultaneous prescription of these edges is
asserted.

**O15.** With one minority and three majority holes, avoiding any specified
majority hole, the optional-edge union has at least 15 elements.
If a short pair of free vertices can be added without using the forbidden
hole, add it and apply the already audited same-parity two-hole L15
bound. Its optional edges are still outside the original matching.
Otherwise translate the minority hole to 0. The two nonforbidden odd
holes have weight three. By a coordinate permutation they are 7 and 11.
The forbidden odd hole has three orbits under their stabilizer, represented
by 1,4,13. The three `q4_four_spectrum_A_*.bin` files give all $10395$
matchings for each representative with cycles certifying a union of size
at least 15.

**O18.** With two holes of each parity, the full-cycle optional-edge union
has at least 18 elements. If there is a short free pair, add it and use
the opposite-parity two-hole L18 bound. Otherwise normalize even holes
to $0,z$, where $z=3$ or 15. If $z=15$, their neighbors exhaust all odd
vertices, impossible. If $z=3$, the only two odd vertices nonadjacent to
both are 13,14. The file [q4_four_spectrum_balanced.bin](research/six_directions/q4_four_spectrum_balanced.bin) covers all
$10395$ matchings with holes $0,3,13,14$.

Producer [q4_four_hole_spectrum.cpp](research/six_directions/q4_four_hole_spectrum.cpp) stores a mate array, a cycle count,
and explicit cycles. Checker [verify_q4_four_hole_spectrum.py](research/six_directions/verify_q4_four_hole_spectrum.py) checks
all 41580 records and 160549 cycles, matching rank coverage, vertex sets,
required edges and every new edge. The two-hole bounds cover the cases
with respectively two same-parity or two opposite-parity holes.

##### 3. Alternate endpoint lemma B4

Let $L$ be an arbitrary matching of $K(Q_4)$ with holes $v,b,z,d$, where
$v,b$ have one parity and $z,d$ the other. Suppose $z$ is not adjacent
to $b$. There is a path on exactly $Q_4-v$, starting at $d$, ending at
some vertex of the parity of $d$ other than $z$, containing $L$ and
using only short new edges.

Translate $v$ to 0. Normalize the ordered triple $(b,z,d)$ by all 24
coordinate permutations. There are exactly 196 ordered configurations
and 13 orbits, listed in [q4_balanced_avoid_path_orbits.json](research/six_directions/q4_balanced_avoid_path_orbits.json). Each has
$11!!=10395$ matchings of the other twelve vertices. The files
`q4_balanced_avoid_path_b_z_d.bin` have one 31-byte record for every
matching: sixteen mate bytes (255 for holes), followed by the fifteen
path vertices. All 135135 rows are positive.

[verify_q4_balanced_avoid_path.py](research/six_directions/verify_q4_balanced_avoid_path.py) independently regenerates the full
196-configuration orbit cover, verifies a bijective matching rank cover
in every file, and checks every path, both endpoints, every required
edge, and shortness of all remaining edges. Thus search completeness is
not needed: exhaustive explicit positive witnesses prove B4.

##### 4. Complete geometry cover

Translate one minority hole to 0. The other has weight 2 or 4, so a
coordinate permutation sends it to 3 or 15. The three nonforbidden
majority holes are any three odd vertices nonadjacent to both minorities;
$v$ is any remaining odd vertex. This lists 728 configurations for $z=3$
and 260 for $z=15$, totaling 988. It is a complete cover, not a minimal
orbit list.

[a6_cut_cover.py](research/six_directions/a6_cut_cover.py) enumerates precisely these choices and the five values
of $\delta$. Choosing a cut with $\delta=2,3,4,1$, in that preference
order, leaves exactly two configurations with no such cut:

$$H_E=\{0,3\},\quad (v,H_O\setminus\{v\})=
(1,\{14,22,26\})\text{ or }(2,\{13,21,25\}).$$

Swapping coordinates 0 and 1 interchanges these exceptions. In each,
all five values of $\delta$ are zero. Sections 5--8 cover the selected
cuts; Section 9 covers the exception. Only 988 hole sets are enumerated:
the transfer proofs apply to every arbitrary matching with those holes.

##### 5. A cut with delta two

Then $A$ has imbalance two and $B$ is balanced. The number $c$ is even,
because each face has an even number of original holes.
If $c>0$, pair $X_A$ into $D$. GQ4-avoid gives an A-side cycle avoiding
$v$ and containing $F_A+D$. Delete $D$, attach all crossings, and
compress to $R$ on $X_B$. The matching $F_B+R$ has exactly $H_B$ as
holes, hence GQ4-cycle gives its full B-side cycle. Expand $R$.

If $c=0$, write $|H_A\cap E|=k$. Here $k=0$ or 1. The only alternative
$k=2$ would put two minority and all four majority holes in one Q4;
two minority vertices have at least six odd neighbors, so three odd
nonforbidden holes cannot all avoid them. This contradicts preprocessing.
Thus the A holes have counts $(0,2)$ or $(1,3)$ and the B holes have
counts $(2,2)$ or $(1,1)$. The A optional union has size at least 15,
the B union at least 18. Identify both faces with Q4; its 32 edges force
these unions to intersect. Choose corresponding optional edges in one
A cycle avoiding $v$ and one full B cycle, delete them, and add the two
short crossing edges between corresponding endpoints. The result is a
single cycle on $Q_5-v$, preserving all required edges.

##### 6. A cut with delta three

Here $A$ has either three majority holes and no minority, or four
majority holes and one minority. There are at least two nonforbidden
majority holes in $A$. Their B mirrors are distinct minority-parity
vertices covered by $F$. The count $c$ is odd, hence positive.
If $c=1$, choose a hole $t$ whose mirror $w$ is not the unique B port.
If $c\ge3$, choose any such $t$.

Pair $X_A\cup\{t\}$ into $D$. The holes of $F_A+D$ have imbalance two;
GQ4-avoid supplies a cycle avoiding $v$.
If $w$ is internal to $F_B$, delete $D$, attach $C$ and bridge $tw$,
and compress to $R$ on $X_B\cup\{w\}$. With $k=F_B(w)$ and $q=R(w)$,
replace $wk,wq$ by $kq$. This is a matching with holes $H_B\cup\{w\}$,
whose minority-parity excess is two. GQ4-avoid on B avoids $w$.
Expand $kq$ via $kw$ and the transfer path, and expand the other R edges.

If $w\in X_B$, choose $D$ to contain $tx$, where $x$ is its original
crossing partner. Since $c\ge3$, there is another edge of $D$. Deleting
$D$ separates $t$ and $x$ into different paths. Attaching $tw,xw$ rejoins
those paths through $w$, and creates no circle. The compressed matching
$R$ has endpoints $X_B-\{w\}$ and interiors $A-v$ together with $w$.
Now $F_B+R$ has holes $H_B\cup\{w\}$. Apply GQ4-avoid avoiding $w$
and expand. Both cases give the required 31-cycle.

##### 7. Double-bridge transfer and delta four

Suppose two distinct original holes $t,s$ in A, neither $v$, have the
same parity, and their mirrors $w=\bar t,z=\bar s$ in B are covered.
Suppose the remaining A holes are exactly two same-parity vertices,
including $v$, and the original B holes are exactly two vertices of the
parity of $w,z$. In particular $c$ is even. The following conditions
each suffice for A6:

1. Both $w,z$ are internal to $F_B$, and either $wz\notin F_B$ or $c\ge2$.
2. Exactly one of $w,z$ is a crossing port (necessarily $c\ge2$).
3. Both are ports and $c\ge4$.

Pair $X_A\cup\{t,s\}$ into $D$, choosing it as follows. For each bridge
whose B endpoint is a port, include the edge joining its A hole to the
original A partner of that port. These prescribed edges are disjoint.
For case 1 with $wz\in F_B$, instead prescribe $ts\in D$. Complete the
remaining pairs arbitrarily. N14_4 gives an A cycle avoiding $v$.

Let $p\in\{0,1,2\}$ be the number of bridge endpoints that are ports.
Delete $D$, attach all original crossings and the bridges $tw,sz$.
At each port bridge vertex two segments join. This restores a prescribed
D edge by a two-edge path; since $|D|=(c+2)/2>p$, at least one gap remains
and the transferred graph is a path forest. Its interiors partition
$A-v$ and the $p$ port bridge vertices. Its endpoints are the other
B ports and the $2-p$ internal bridge vertices. Compress to $R$.

In $F_B+R$, the only vertices of degree two are the internal bridge
vertices. Suppress them along their components to get a matching $L_B$.
There is no closed component: the only possible one would require both
bridge vertices to be internal and $wz$ to be an edge of BOTH $F_B$ and
$R$. When $wz\notin F_B$ this cannot occur. When $wz\in F_B$, the chosen
$ts\in D$ and $|D|\ge2$ place $t,s$ in different path components after
deletion, so $wz\notin R$ as well. With zero or one internal bridge
vertex a cycle cannot occur, since every other vertex has degree at most
one. The holes of $L_B$ are exactly $H_B\cup\{w,z\}$, four vertices of
one parity. T44 gives a B cycle avoiding $w,z$. Undo all suppressions and
expansions. Each avoided bridge vertex is restored exactly once, together
with all of $A-v$, and every original edge is retained.

For $\delta=4$, all four majority holes lie in A and both minority holes
in B. The three nonforbidden majority holes offer three covered mirror
vertices. Choose two for this transfer. If at least two are ports and
$c\ge4$, use case 3. If there is a port and an internal vertex, use case 2.
If all three are internal, at most one pair is an edge of $F_B$, so
choose an unpaired pair and use case 1. The only remaining possibility
is that all three are ports, which implies even $c\ge4$. Thus every
delta-four input is covered.

##### 8. A cut with delta one

Write $k=|H_A\cap E|$, so $|H_A\cap O|=k+1$. The value $k=0$ is
impossible: B would have two minority and three majority holes, all
nonforbidden, contrary to the Q4 neighbor bound and preprocessing.
Thus $k=1$ or 2. The crossing count $c$ is odd and positive.

For any minority hole $y\in A$, any root port $d\in X_A$, and any pairing
$D$ of $X_A-\{d\}$, add the auxiliary edge $dy$ to $F_A+D$. Its holes
have majority excess two and include $v$. GQ4-avoid gives a cycle on
$A-v$ containing $dy$. Deleting $dy$ gives a spanning $d$--$y$ path
containing $F_A+D$ with only short new edges. This holds for EVERY root
port and EVERY pairing D.

The mirror $w=\bar y$ has majority parity and is covered in B. If it is
internal, delete D, attach crossings and $yw$, compress to R, and repair
the unique overlap at $w$ as in Section 6. The resulting matching has
holes $H_B\cup\{w\}$ of majority excess two. GQ4-avoid avoiding $w$
and expansion finish the construction.

If $w$ is a port and $c\ge3$, choose $d$ to be its original partner.
Now D is nonempty. Deleting D separates the two ends $d,y$ of the A path;
attaching $dw,yw$ joins different path components at $w$. Compress on
$X_B-\{w\}$ and apply GQ4-avoid to $F_B+R$ avoiding $w$. Its holes are
again $H_B\cup\{w\}$.

When $k=2,c=1$, choose a minority hole whose mirror is not the unique
port, and use the internal case. The only remaining case has $k=c=1$
and the unique minority hole $y$ mirrored at the unique port $w$.
Let $d$ be the unique A port; the holes of $F_A$ are $v,b,y,d$, where
$v,b$ have majority parity. Preprocessing says $y$ is not adjacent to b.

If $d$ has majority parity, A4_4 gives a cycle on $A-v$ containing $F_A$.
At its free vertex $d$ both incident cycle edges are short. Their two
neighbors have minority parity; choose a neighbor $z\ne y$ and delete
$dz$. This gives an A path from $d$ to $z$ avoiding $v$.
If $d$ has minority parity, B4 gives exactly such a path, with endpoint
$z$ of minority parity and $z\ne y$. In both cases $z\ne d$ as well.

Attach the original crossing $dw$ and the new bridge $z\bar z$ to this
path. Because $z\ne y$, its mirror $q=\bar z$ is not the unique B port w.
It has majority parity and hence is either an original majority hole
or internally covered. Compress to the edge $wq$.
If q is a hole, $F_B+wq$ has balanced holes, so GQ4-cycle applies.
If q is internally covered, suppress q through its $F_B$ edge and $wq$;
the resulting matching has holes $H_B\cup\{q\}$ of majority excess two.
GQ4-avoid avoids q. Expanding restores the A path and q and completes
the construction in all delta-one cases.

##### 9. The all-zero exceptional geometry

It suffices by the stated coordinate swap to handle

$$H_E=\{0,3\},\quad H_O=\{1,14,22,26\},\quad v=1.$$

For each coordinate $j\in\{2,3,4\}$, put its zero face in A. It contains
the minority holes $t=0,s=3$, the forbidden hole 1, and exactly one other
majority hole. B contains exactly two majority holes. The two bridges
from $0,3$ have endpoints $w_j=2^j,z_j=2^j+3$. These have majority parity
and are covered. Consequently Section 7 applies unless the cut has one
of these two exceptional forms:

- $c_j=0$ and $w_jz_j\in F_B$;
- $c_j=2$ and its B port set is exactly $\{w_j,z_j\}$.

Indeed even $c_j$ and the three cases in Section 7 exhaust all other
possibilities, including an internal required edge $w_jz_j$ when $c_j>0$.

Suppose all three cuts have one of these exceptional forms. Let S be the
vertices whose last three bits (coordinates 2,3,4) have weight at most
one. Then $|S|=4(1+3)=16$. Its original holes are exactly $0,1,3$;
the other three holes $14,22,26$ each have two of those bits set.
No edge of F can leave S. To see this, take an edge from $x\in S$ to
$r\notin S$. At some coordinate $j\in\{2,3,4\}$ the outside endpoint r
has bit 1 and x has bit 0. If $c_j=0$ the edge is impossible. Otherwise
the B port r must equal $w_j$ or $z_j$, each of which has only ONE set
bit among those three coordinates, contradicting $r\notin S$.
Thus F would match the 13 covered vertices of S entirely within S,
which is impossible for a matching. At least one of the three cuts is
therefore nonexceptional, and its double-bridge transfer proves A6.

##### Conclusion and remaining scope

Preprocessing and the complete 988-configuration cover reduce every A6
input to Sections 5--9. These sections give cycles through exactly
$Q_5-v$, preserving arbitrary original edges and adding only short ones.
Subject to independent audit of this argument and the new finite inputs,
the A6 proof is complete relative to the declared prior results.

[EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md](#proof-eight-hole-conditional-reduction-draft) separately explains the
consequence for all free-target eight-hole Q6 inputs and some covered
targets. Its covered residual R8-covered remains a genuine obligation.
Neither A6 nor that conditional reduction alone closes full eight-hole
P6, and the higher 10--18-hole levels also remain open.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-delta4-first-orbit" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT.md — A8: delta-four transfer with one minority hole in the target face</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT.md)。SHA-256：`296d483e95fa6b5d07b5d35f9562fce0a798b1b0876898ea4bc5a5013d947a3f`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json), [TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json)。

#### A8: delta-four transfer with one minority hole in the target face

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft. Independent review pending.

##### Claim

Let $F$ be an arbitrary matching of $K(Q_5)$ with three minority and five
majority holes, and let $v$ be a specified majority hole. Assume no minority
hole is short-adjacent to any other majority hole. If a coordinate face
$A$ containing $v$ contains all five majority holes and exactly one minority
hole, then $F$ extends to a simple cycle on exactly $Q_5-v$ using only short
new edges.

##### Status

**PROVABLE AS STATED**, relative to GQ4-avoid and Q4 T44. This closes the
first residual orbit of [A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md](#proof-a8-partial-proof-package); it does not close
the four other residual orbits or full A8.

##### Assumptions, notation, and dependency map

Use the global majority/minority parity labels on both faces. Write $B$
for the other face, $C$ for the original crossing matching, $c=|C|$, and
$X_A,X_B$ for its endpoint sets. The internal matchings are $F_A,F_B$.
For $t\in A$ its short mirror in $B$ is $\bar t$.

The imported results are GQ4-avoid in [Q4_GENERAL_AUGMENTATION.md](#proof-q4-general-augmentation) and
T44 in [Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_TRANSFER.md](#proof-q4-two-avoided-transfer), with their prior audit packages.
GQ4-avoid supplies the $A-v$ cycle after two bridges are prepared.
T44 supplies the cycle on $B$ avoiding the two bridge vertices after
compression. The path-forest argument below justifies all compression.

##### Proof strategy

Two of the four available majority holes in $A$ provide short bridges.
They are chosen so that an artificial matching can encode every forced
joining at a bridge vertex while leaving at least one unfilled gap in the
$A$ cycle. The remaining $A$ holes have imbalance two; the remaining $B$
matching has four same-parity holes and two prescribed avoided holes.

##### Proof

###### Step 1. Choice of the two bridges

There are four candidate majority holes in $A$ other than $v$. Their
mirrors are distinct minority-parity vertices in $B$. None is an original
hole: the only original $B$ holes are two minority holes, and a minority
hole cannot be adjacent to a nonforbidden majority hole under the stated
nonadjacency assumption. Thus all four mirrors are covered. Also $c$ is
even because $A$ has six original holes and
$2|F_A|+c=16-6=10$.

Choose candidates $t,s$ with mirrors $w=\bar t,z=\bar s$ as follows.

* If both internal vertices and ports occur among the four mirrors,
  choose one of each. Then $c\ge2$ and exactly one selected mirror is a port.
* If all four mirrors are internal to $F_B$, choose two not paired by
  $F_B$. Such a choice exists because a matching on four vertices has
  at most two edges, whereas there are six pairs.
* If all four mirrors are ports, then $c\ge4$. Choose any two of them.

These three alternatives exhaust the possibilities. In particular the
case of two mirror ports with $c=2$ belongs to the first alternative,
where a port and an internal vertex are chosen.

###### Step 2. An artificial matching in the target face

Let $T=X_A\cup\{t,s\}$. For each chosen mirror that is a port, prescribe
in a matching $D$ the edge joining its hole $t$ or $s$ to that port's
original crossing partner in $X_A$. These prescriptions are disjoint.
Complete them to a perfect matching $D$ on $T$, which has even size
$c+2$. Put $d=|D|=(c+2)/2$, and let $p$ be the number of selected mirrors
that are ports. In the three alternatives of Step 1, respectively,

$$ (p,d)=(1,d\ge2),\quad(0,d\ge1),\quad(2,d\ge3). $$

In every alternative $d>p$. The holes of $F_A\cup D$ are the original
six $A$ holes with $t,s$ removed, namely one minority hole and three
majority holes including $v$. GQ4-avoid gives an $A-v$ cycle $K$
containing $F_A\cup D$.

###### Step 3. Compression and the absence of a closed component

Delete $D$ from $K$, attach all original crossings, and attach the short
bridges $tw,sz$. At each selected port mirror the two incident edges
join the endpoints of its prescribed edge of $D$ by a two-edge path.
This restores exactly $p$ of the $d$ removed gaps. Since $p<d$, the
result is a path forest. Its interiors include $A-v$ and each selected
mirror that is a port. Its endpoints consist of all other $B$ ports
and the selected mirrors that are internal to $F_B$.

Compress this forest to an endpoint matching $R$. Consider $F_B\cup R$.
The only vertices where these two matchings overlap are the selected
internal mirrors, at most two vertices. If exactly one mirror is
internal, a closed component cannot exist: every other vertex has degree
at most one. If neither is internal, the union is already a matching.
If both are internal, a closed component would have to alternate
between $F_B$ and $R$ using only the two degree-two vertices $w,z$.
It would require $wz\in F_B$ and $wz\in R$. Step 1 chose
$wz\notin F_B$, so this is impossible.

Suppress every selected internal mirror along its path component in
$F_B\cup R$. The resulting graph $L$ is therefore a matching of $K(B)$.
Its holes are exactly the two original $B$ holes together with $w,z$.
All four have minority parity.

###### Step 4. Completion in the other face

T44 supplies a simple cycle on exactly $B\setminus\{w,z\}$ containing
$L$, with all other edges short. Undo all suppressions and compressed
paths. The two avoided mirror vertices are restored exactly once: an
internal mirror lies on its suppressed path, and a port mirror lies in
the transferred path forest. All vertices of $A-v$ are also restored
exactly once. The expanded cycle has vertex set $Q_5-v$, contains every
edge of $F_A,F_B,C$, and its new edges are short. This proves the claim.

###### Step 5. Application to the first residual orbit

The first representative in [A8_geometry_census.json](research/six_directions/A8_geometry_census.json) has

$$v=0,\quad Z=\{3,5,6,15\},\quad W=\{8,25,26\}.$$

Here majority parity is numerical even parity. Cut at coordinate $4$
(the bit of value $16$) and take its zero face as $A$. All five majority
holes lie in $A$, and the only minority hole in $A$ is $8$; the other
minority holes $25,26$ lie in $B$. This is exactly the proved condition.
Coordinate permutations preserve the condition and transfer the whole
arbitrary matching, so all 60 geometries in this orbit are covered.

##### Corrections or missing assumptions

None for the stated claim. The nonadjacency hypothesis is the residual
hypothesis after short-edge augmentation to A6; it is explicitly assumed
here and guarantees the bridges end at covered vertices.

##### Open risks

This is a new proof awaiting independent review. Combined with the three
cut branches, it leaves four residual orbits of sizes $20,30,30,20$,
totaling 100 normalized hole geometries. It asserts no closure of their
matching instances, of full A8, or of any full higher-hole P6 layer.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-double-bridge-sufficient" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_SUFFICIENT.md — A8: a sufficient double-bridge criterion controlling the T15 obstruction</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_SUFFICIENT.md)。SHA-256：`a42004652fb586ec3971b02c7f932ce337f3bd8476cea0da5755a3b4d2b287f3`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json), [A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json), [A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### A8: a sufficient double-bridge criterion controlling the T15 obstruction

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft; independent review pending.

##### Claim

Let $F$ have the original A8 hole counts and satisfy the residual
nonadjacency condition of [A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md](#proof-a8-partial-proof-package). Take a coordinate
face $A$ containing the forbidden majority hole $v$ and two distinct holes
$t,s\ne v$. Let $B$ be the other face and put $w=\bar t,z=\bar s$.
Assume:

1. The vertices $w,z$ are covered by $F$.
2. Removing $t,s$ from the original $A$ holes leaves majority excess two.
3. The original $B$ holes together with $w,z$ consist of one singleton
   parity hole $a$ and five holes of the other parity; $w,z$ belong to
   that five-hole class.

The graph criterion in Step 2 below suffices for the A8 conclusion.

##### Status

**PROVABLE AS STATED**, relative to GQ4-avoid and the Q4 T15 classification.
This is a sufficient criterion, with no claim that all remaining matching
instances satisfy it. In particular, a fixed original edge between the
two remaining neighbors of $a$ may prevent its use.

##### Notation, assumptions, and dependency map

Use $F_A,F_B,C,c,X_A,X_B$ as in the partial package. Put
$T=X_A\cup\{t,s\}$ and $d=|T|/2$. Assumption 2 implies $|T|$ is even.
GQ4-avoid is used on $A-v$. The exact Q4 T15 classification in
[Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md](#proof-q4-t15-classification) is used on $B$ avoiding $w,z$. The argument
does not assume T15 is universally positive.

##### Proof strategy and proof

###### Step 1. A graph recording the part outside the target face

Define $G$ with edges

$$F_B\cup C\cup\{tw,sz\}$$

and include its isolated original $B$ holes. The $A$ vertices of $G$
are exactly $T$, each of degree one. Every covered $B$ vertex except
$w,z$ has degree one; $w,z$ each have degree two. Thus every nontrivial
component is a path: a cycle could use only degree-two vertices $w,z$,
but $G$ is simple and has no cycle on two vertices. There are no repeated
edges here, since $t,s$ are original holes and the original matching has
no edge incident to them.

Each component with both endpoints in $T$ gives an artificial edge on
its two endpoints. These edges form a matching $P$ on $T$. There are at
most two such components. Indeed each must contain $w$ or $z$, because
all other $B$ vertices have degree one. Each other component meeting $T$
has a unique endpoint in $B\setminus\{w,z\}$; call that endpoint a
terminal, and call its unique corresponding vertex of $T$ its root.

###### Step 2. The sufficient criterion

If at least one of $w,z$ is not adjacent to $a$ in $B$, set $J=P$.
Otherwise let $p,q$ be the two neighbors of $a$ in the $Q_4$ face $B$
other than $w,z$. Require

$$pq\notin F_B.\tag{1}$$

If both $p,q$ are terminals of components meeting $T$, let their roots
be $u,r$ and set $J=P\cup\{ur\}$. Otherwise set $J=P$.
The roots of terminal components are disjoint from all endpoints of
$P$, so $J$ is a matching in all cases. The sufficient criterion is

$$d>|J|.\tag{2}$$

This criterion is inspectable from $F$ and the selected bridges without
searching for any $A$-face cycle. In the case where (1) is needed,
$c\ge6$ implies (2), because $d=(c+2)/2\ge4$ and $|J|\le3$;
the condition (1) is still required even for such large $c$.

###### Step 3. Choice of the target-face cycle

Complete $J$ to a perfect matching $D$ on $T$. By assumption 2 the
matching $F_A\cup D$ has hole excess two, with $v$ in its larger class.
GQ4-avoid gives a cycle $K$ on $A-v$ containing $F_A\cup D$.
Delete $D$. The resulting path forest pairs the vertices of $T$ by a
matching $S$, where an edge of $S$ stands for an entire remaining path
of $K$. As a multigraph, $S\cup D$ is one cycle: it is obtained by
contracting those paths in the original cycle. This remains true when
$d=1$, in which case its two edges are parallel.

Since $P\subseteq J\subset D$ and $|J|<d$, the multigraph
$S\cup P$ contains no cycle. Otherwise it would already contain the
unique cycle of $S\cup D$, forcing every edge of $D$ to belong to $P$.
Consequently attaching $G$ to the uncompressed $A$ paths produces no
closed component. Its nontrivial components are paths with endpoints
in $B\setminus\{w,z\}$ and interiors containing all of $A-v$ and both
$w,z$. Compress them, retaining isolated original $B$ holes, to a matching
$L$ on $B$ with hole set exactly $H_B\cup\{w,z\}$.

###### Step 4. Excluding the T15 obstruction

If at least one of $w,z$ is not a neighbor of $a$, the T15 obstruction
does not hold, independent of $L$, so proceed to Step 5.

In the other case, the T15 obstruction is exactly $pq\in L$.
The vertices $p,q$ are original covered vertices: they cannot be original
$B$ holes because every original hole of their parity is nonadjacent to
the singleton opposite-parity original hole $a$, by residual
nonadjacency. They are not $w,z$, so each has degree one in $G$.

A component of $G$ with both endpoints in $B$ is a single edge of $F_B$:
any longer such path would require traversing $w$ or $z$, whose other
incident bridge leads to an endpoint in $T$. Thus, if $p$ or $q$ belongs
to a component not meeting $T$, it remains paired with its original
partner in $L$. Condition (1) then prevents $pq\in L$.

It remains to consider the case where $p,q$ are both terminals with
roots $u,r$. Here $ur\in J\subset D$. If expansion and compression
produced an edge $pq\in L$, the portions between roots would give an
$u$--$r$ path in $S\cup P$. Adding the edge $ur$ gives a cycle in
$S\cup P\cup\{ur\}$. But $P\cup\{ur\}=J$ is a proper subset of $D$
by (2), so this multigraph is a proper subgraph of the single cycle
$S\cup D$ and cannot contain a cycle. This contradiction proves
$pq\notin L$.

###### Step 5. Completion

Assumption 3 gives exactly the hole pattern of Q4 T15, with avoided
holes $w,z$. Step 4 excludes its necessary and sufficient obstruction,
so T15 gives a simple cycle on $B\setminus\{w,z\}$ containing $L$.
Expand all its compressed edges. The expanded paths restore every
vertex of $A-v$, both bridge vertices, and every original edge of $F$,
and all other edges used are short. The result is the desired cycle on
$Q_5-v$.

##### Corrections or missing assumptions

The criterion is not necessary. Its failure is not a counterexample to
A8 or to other choices of bridges or cuts. In particular $d=|J|$ only
blocks this method of keeping a spare gap; it does not rule out a more
flexible target-face construction.

##### Open risks

This proof is unreviewed. It has not been used to count or close the
remaining four A8 residual orbits. Universal coverage would require an
additional argument over all arbitrary matchings, or a complete finite
positive certificate package for the cases left by this criterion.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-orbit4-full-closure" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_ORBIT4_FULL_CLOSURE.md — A8: full closure of the fourth residual geometry orbit</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT4_FULL_CLOSURE.md)。SHA-256：`8dfb5f3ccd45dadcc4cc3467369616bce05eab94b0c91a132c4ddc4442ed6387`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT4_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### A8: full closure of the fourth residual geometry orbit

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Complete proposed orbit proof relative to
explicit imports and positive finite certificates; fresh review pending.
Full A8 and full P6 remain open.

##### Exact theorem

Let F be any matching of K(Q5) with holes exactly

$$H=\{0,1,2,4,15,23,27,29\}.$$

Then there is a cycle on exactly Q5 minus {0}, containing F, with every
edge outside F short. All twelve required matching edges may be arbitrary,
including long and same-parity edges. Coordinate permutations transport
this theorem to all30 marked geometries in the fourth row of
A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md (zero-based orbit index3). This statement is
about that exact orbit, not all A8 inputs.

##### Imports

Use GQ4-avoid, the complete Q4 T15 and T63 classifications, and the two-
and three-bridge sufficient criteria, with accepted scopes in
A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.md/.json. The proof below derives the needed
four-cut restrictions explicitly; the unreviewed diagnostic typed spectrum
is not a premise. No full A8, A10, or higher-hole P6 conclusion is imported.

##### 1. Four valid cut templates

For bit b let A have coordinate zero and B coordinate one. A contains the
forbidden hole0. In each row choose the A bridge holes whose B mirrors are Y.

| b | Y in B | possible fixed obstruction edge pq | B local theorem |
|---:|---|---|---|
|2|3,6|10--18|T15|
|4|5,6|12--20|T15|
|8|9,10,12|8--24|T63|
|16|17,18,20|16--24|T63|

The first two A faces have two minority and two majority original holes;
consuming the two minority bridge sources leaves two majority holes.
The B compression has one minority and five majority holes, omitting Y.
The last two A faces have three minority and two majority holes; consuming
three minority bridge sources again leaves two majority holes. Their B
compression has six same-parity holes, omitting the three members of Y.
All bridge vertices are originally covered. Direct coordinate deletion
and minority translation give exactly the obstruction edges displayed.
These facts can also be verified directly from H and the cut bits.

##### 2. A sufficient condition outside a restricted-edge family

Fix one row, put S=Y union {p,q}, and suppose pq is not an original edge
of F. The restricted-edge family for this row consists of matchings with:

1. every original crossing edge having its B endpoint in S;
2. every internally matched member of Y having its mate in S.

If a matching violates either condition, its audited bridge criterion
succeeds. Indeed form G=F_B union C union the bridges. Its A endpoints T
are the crossing ports and the bridge sources. Pair its T-to-T components
into P. Every other G component meeting T has one B terminal.
Violation of condition1 or2 gives a terminal outside {p,q}: respectively
a nonbridge crossing port outside S, or the outside mate of an internal
bridge. Let e=1 when both p,q are terminals rooted in T, and e=0 otherwise.
The total number of rooted terminals is even, and the outside terminal
ensures it is strictly greater than2e. Since that number is |T|-2|P|,

$$ |T|/2>|P|+e. $$

This is exactly the strict inequality in the accepted bridge criterion,
with pq absent as required. It gives the desired31-cycle. Thus an input
not covered by any of these four constructions must, for each row,
either contain its fixed edge pq or belong to its restricted-edge family.
This necessary condition for remaining inputs is all that is needed;
no assertion that a failed template disproves the original theorem is used.

##### 3. Disjoint complete description of the remaining inputs

Partition by the four-bit mask recording which displayed fixed edges
belong to F, in table order. For a bit set to1 require that edge. For a
bit set to0 exclude that edge and impose its restricted-edge conditions.
The required edges must be pairwise disjoint. Each restricted condition
is precisely an allowed-edge graph on the24 covered vertices: crossing
edges may enter B only at S, and an internal B edge meeting Y may not
leave S. All other original edges are allowed.

Intersect these graphs for the unset bits, remove the vertices covered
by the required edges, and enumerate all perfect matchings of the remaining
graph. This is a disjoint, exhaustive partition of every input left by
Section2. It places no shortness restriction on the original matching.

The nonempty masks and exact counts are:

| mask | required fixed edges | matching count |
|---:|---|---:|
|3|10--18,12--20|2025|
|7|10--18,12--20,8--24|99225|
|11|10--18,12--20,16--24|99225|

The total is200475. Masks containing both final fixed edges are impossible
because these edges share24. Every other empty branch has an odd connected
component in its allowed graph, preventing a perfect matching; actual
components are recorded in the independent verification output.

The producer A8_orbit4_joint_bad_enumerate.py generates the full inputs
and branch graphs. The separate verify_A8_orbit4_joint_bad.py reconstructs
the graphs from the cut definitions, verifies odd-component obstructions,
and enumerates the remaining perfect matchings in reverse vertex order,
without importing producer code or using its memoized counts. It checks
exact set equality, uniqueness, all required fixed edges, and all unset
fixed-edge absences against the24-byte input records.

##### 4. Complete positive certificates for the finite remainder

A8_orbit4_joint_bad_certificates.bin contains exactly200475 records of55
bytes: the twelve original matching edges (24 bytes), followed by a31-
vertex cycle. The independent verifier checks each input is precisely the
corresponding member of the complete input domain; all31 listed vertices
are distinct and equal to {1,...,31}; every original edge appears; and
every other cycle edge, including the closing edge, has Hamming distance1.
The vertex sequence itself proves connectedness and excludes extra cycles.

All200475 records pass. The search producer reports no unknown or exhausted
input, but search exhaustiveness is not a proof premise: the complete
positive certificates and independently checked domain are sufficient.
There are no unchecked residual inputs in this finite remainder.

##### 5. Conclusion and remaining scope

Every matching with holes H either satisfies one audited cut construction
or is one of the completely verified positive finite inputs. This proves
the exact theorem. Coordinate permutations preserve the omitted vertex0,
short edges, and the arbitrary matching domain, so the30-member orbit is
covered. The other A8 residual orbits and full P6 remain separate obligations.
Semantic acceptance remains same-family/provisional relative to explicit
imports, pending fresh review of this complete assembly.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-orbit5-full-closure" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_ORBIT5_FULL_CLOSURE.md — A8: final residual orbit, complete finite-completion obligation</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT5_FULL_CLOSURE.md)。SHA-256：`847f42aec33dac489169aa49be300ac673adb98eb564712440ade600a7451dde`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_ORBIT5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### A8: final residual orbit, complete finite-completion obligation

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Proposed complete assembly; the positive
certificate run and fresh independent review must finish before acceptance.
Full A8 and P6 are not declared proved by this draft.

##### Exact claim

Every arbitrary matching F of K(Q5) with holes exactly

$$H=\{0,2,4,8,15,23,27,29\}$$

has an extending cycle on exactly Q5 minus {0}, with only short new edges.
The twelve required edges may be long or join equal parities. The fifth
row of A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md has20 coordinate-permutation images
of this marked geometry. No other residual orbit is claimed here.

##### 1. Imported constructions and four actual cuts

Import the accepted GQ4-avoid, Q4 T15/T63, and bridge criteria from
A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.md/.json. For each cut bit b take A's bit zero
face, containing forbidden0, and B's bit one face. Select the bridge holes
in A that mirror to Y below.

| b | Y in B | fixed obstruction edge pq | B theorem |
|---:|---|---|---|
|2|6,10|3--18|T15|
|4|6,12|5--20|T15|
|8|10,12|9--24|T15|
|16|18,20,24|16--17|T63|

Each of the first three A faces has two minority and two majority holes.
The two bridges consume its minority holes; the A completion has two
majority holes and the compressed B input has1:5 holes, omitting Y.
The last A face has three minority and two majority holes; three bridges
leave its two majority holes, and B has six same-parity holes omitting Y.
Every bridge mirror is covered. Deleting the cut coordinate and normalizing
the singleton where required gives precisely the displayed local OB edges.

##### 2. Exhaustive sufficient-condition partition

For any row let S=Y union {p,q}. If pq is absent from F and either a
crossing edge enters B outside S, or an internally matched bridge vertex
has its original mate outside S, the accepted bridge criterion succeeds.
Here is the complete reason, independent of any A-cycle search.

In G=F_B union C union the short bridges, all A vertices are degree-one
endpoints T. Let P pair T-to-T components and let e indicate whether
both p,q are B terminals of components rooted at T. The violated restriction
produces another B terminal outside {p,q}. The number |T|-2|P| of rooted
terminals is even and exceeds2e. Hence |T|/2>|P|+e. Prescribe P and the
OB-root pair when present as a proper subset of D, apply GQ4-avoid in A,
and use the audited bridge criterion. It guarantees an acyclic transfer,
no compressed OB, and a positive T15/T63 B completion. Expansion gives
the required31-cycle preserving all of F.

Thus every input not already solved must, for each row, either contain pq
or obey both restricted-edge conditions. Partition such inputs by the
four-bit mask of which actual fixed edges occur, in table order. For an
unset bit explicitly exclude its fixed edge and impose its restrictions.
This partitions all remaining matchings into16 disjoint finite graph
matching domains. The original graph is the complete graph on the24
covered vertices; no restriction to short original matching edges is made.

##### 3. Exact finite domains

Require the set-bit fixed edges, delete their covered vertices, and
intersect the allowed-edge graphs for the unset bits. In a restricted
graph, crossings may enter B only at S, and internal B edges meeting Y
must remain in S. Enumerate all perfect matchings of the remaining graph.
The counts computed by A8_orbit5_joint_bad_enumerate.py are:

| fixed-edge mask | matching count |
|---:|---:|
|7|176400|
|11|176400|
|13|176400|
|14|176400|
|15|2027025|

All other masks have zero inputs. Total:2732625. These counts and the
empty branches require independent reconstruction; the producer's dynamic
programming alone is not the final acceptance gate. The input file stores
each original matching as24 endpoint bytes, with both endpoints within
each edge sorted and the twelve edges lexicographically sorted.

##### 4. Positive finite completion and mandatory acceptance gate

The running producer a8_full_cycle_certifier.cpp seeks one31-cycle for
each complete input and writes55-byte records:24 original-matching bytes
followed by31 cycle vertices. Acceptance requires all2732625 inputs to
have such a record, with no missing or duplicate input. Every record must
independently satisfy:

* its required matching is exactly the corresponding complete-domain input;
* its cycle lists each vertex1,...,31 exactly once and never lists0;
* all twelve original required edges occur;
* every other cycle edge, including the closing edge, is a cube short edge.

These positive checks suffice regardless of the search algorithm. A timeout
or exhausted search would leave an explicit open obligation, not establish
a counterexample. The cycle order supplies connectedness as well as degrees.

##### 5. Conclusion conditional on the gate, and scope

Once the independent domain reconstruction and all positive certificate
checks pass, every F either has a constructed cycle from Section2 or is one
of the certified finite inputs. This proves the exact claim and its20
coordinate images. A separate whole-A8 assembly audit must combine this
orbit with the other accepted cases before full A8 is marked closed.
No Q6 covered-target layer or full P6 conclusion follows solely from this file.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-orbits2-3-analytic-closure" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_ORBITS2_3_ANALYTIC_CLOSURE.md — A8 residual orbits 2 and 3: analytic closure by closed matching sets</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_ORBITS2_3_ANALYTIC_CLOSURE.md)。SHA-256：`c273b767a2ee10303c768b48d5d35a23da330cd4128af62b08547d51bc542764`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_ORBITS2_3_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_ORBITS2_3_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### A8 residual orbits 2 and 3: analytic closure by closed matching sets

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer package; fresh independent review pending.

##### Claim

Write $V(Q_5)=\{0,\ldots,31\}$ in binary coordinates. Let $F$ be an
arbitrary matching of the complete graph on these vertices whose hole
set is one of

$$H_2=\{0,3,5,6,15,25,26,28\},$$
$$H_3=\{0,3,5,15,23,25,26,28\}.$$

There is a simple cycle on exactly $V(Q_5)\setminus\{0\}$ containing
every edge of $F$ and using only short edges outside $F$. The same
conclusion holds under every coordinate permutation of either marked
hole geometry. These are the second and third residual orbits in
[A8_geometry_census.json](research/six_directions/A8_geometry_census.json), of respective sizes 20 and 30.

##### Status

**PROVABLE AS STATED**, relative to the previously certified Q4 inputs
listed below. This package proves the two specified orbits and makes
no claim that the remaining A8 orbits or full A8 are closed. Independent
proof-checker review of this new argument is pending.

##### Assumptions, notation, and dependency map

No required edge is assumed short or bipartite. The five numerical even
holes are called majority holes, the three odd holes minority holes.
The forbidden hole is $v=0$. In both cases put $W=\{25,26,28\}$,
and write $Z=H_j\setminus(W\cup\{0\})$ for the four available majority
holes. Direct bit geometry shows no vertex of $Z$ is short-adjacent
to a vertex of $W$; this is a property of these particular geometries,
not an extra condition on the arbitrary matching.

For a cut bit $b\in\{1,2,4,8,16\}$, let $A$ be its zero face and
$B$ its one face. The internal matching edges are $F_A,F_B$, the
crossing matching is $C$, its size is $c$, and its endpoint sets are
$X_A,X_B$. A short mirror across the cut is denoted $\bar t=t\oplus b$.

The imported inputs are:

1. GQ4-avoid in [Q4_GENERAL_AUGMENTATION.md](#proof-q4-general-augmentation): arbitrary hole counts
   of imbalance two permit a face cycle avoiding a specified majority hole.
2. The exact Q4 T15 classification in [Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md](#proof-q4-t15-classification).
3. The exact Q4 T63 classification in [A8_Q4_T63_CLASSIFICATION.md](#proof-a8-q4-t63-classification).

The latter input and the double/three-bridge path construction were
independently accepted in [A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.md](#review-a8-bridge-inputs-review). We reproduce
the needed construction in Step 1, including its extension to the
delta-five cut, so it is not being invoked outside its former delta-minus-one
statement. The small checker [A8_orbits2_3_geometry_check.py](research/six_directions/A8_orbits2_3_geometry_check.py) verifies
the bit identities and orbit sizes used below; it enumerates no matching
instances and is not a substitute for the analytic matching argument.

##### Proof strategy

Assume no required cycle exists. If all bridge choices at a suitable
cut fail, their fixed obstructions and nonfixed endpoint restrictions
force an eight-vertex covered set to be closed under the matching.
Applying this at bits 8 and 16 yields three disjoint closed four-vertex
sets. The remaining covered set is then closed too. Other cuts forbid
its matching from changing selected low bits, leaving vertex 1 with
no possible distinct partner. This contradicts the original matching.

##### Proof

###### Step 1. A common sufficient bridge construction

Select $k$ original holes $t_1,\ldots,t_k\ne0$ in $A$, where $k=2$
or $3$, and put $Y=\{\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_k\}$. In each application
below these mirrors are original covered vertices, and removing the
selected holes leaves original $A$ hole excess two in the majority class.
Consequently $T=X_A\cup\{t_1,\ldots,t_k\}$ has even size. Write
$d=|T|/2$.

Define the graph

$$G=F_B\cup C\cup\{t_i\bar t_i:1\le i\le k\}.$$

Every vertex of $T$ has degree one. Only the vertices of $Y$ have
degree two in $B$; each such vertex is incident to a bridge leading
to a degree-one endpoint in $T$. Hence $G$ is a path forest, not a
graph with a closed component. Pair the two $T$ endpoints of every
$T$--$T$ component to get a matching $P$ on $T$. Every other component
meeting $T$ has a terminal in $B$ and a root in $T$.

Suppose the chosen local completion theorem on $B$ has exactly one
possible obstruction edge $pq$, with $p,q$ original covered vertices
outside $Y$. Suppose $pq\notin F_B$. If both $p,q$ are rooted terminals,
add to $P$ the edge between their roots, obtaining $J$; otherwise put
$J=P$. This is a matching, because roots of terminal components do
not occur in $P$. Write $e=|J|-|P|\in\{0,1\}$.

If there is a terminal outside $\{p,q\}$, the number of terminal roots,
$2d-2|P|$, is even and strictly larger than $2e$. Thus $d>|J|$.
Complete $J$ to a perfect matching $D$ on $T$. GQ4-avoid applies to
$F_A\cup D$, giving a cycle $K$ on $A\setminus\{0\}$. Delete $D$.
The resulting path forest pairs $T$ by a matching $Q$ after each path
is contracted; the multigraph $Q\cup D$ is one cycle. Since $J$ is
a proper subset of $D$, the graph $Q\cup J$ has no cycle.

Attach $G$ to the uncontracted paths. A closed component would give
a cycle in $Q\cup P\subseteq Q\cup J$, and is therefore impossible.
The result compresses to a matching $L$ on $B$ whose holes are exactly
the original $B$ holes together with $Y$. Its suppressed interiors
contain every vertex of $A\setminus\{0\}$ and every vertex of $Y$.

The edge $pq$ does not belong to $L$. If either endpoint belongs to
a component of $G$ not meeting $T$, that component is an original
edge of $F_B$, and $pq\notin F_B$ excludes it. Such a component cannot
be a longer $B$--$B$ path because traversing a bridge vertex leads
to a degree-one endpoint in $T$. In the other case both endpoints
are rooted terminals. A compressed $pq$ edge would give a path
between their roots in $Q\cup P$; together with the prescribed extra
edge of $J$, this would be a cycle in $Q\cup J$, a contradiction.

The local T15 or T63 theorem therefore supplies a cycle on $B\setminus Y$
containing $L$. Expanding the compressed paths restores every suppressed
vertex exactly once and gives the required cycle on $Q_5\setminus\{0\}$.
All original edges survive, and all other edges are short: the only
additional original-face edges come from GQ4-avoid and the local theorem,
and every selected bridge is short.

We have proved: if the required global cycle does not exist and
$pq\notin F_B$, there is no rooted terminal outside $\{p,q\}$.
Equivalently, with $S=Y\cup\{p,q\}$,

$$X_B\subseteq S,\qquad
F_B(y)\in S\text{ for every }y\in Y\text{ internally covered in }B.\tag{R}$$

For this equivalence, a port outside $S$ is itself an impermissible
terminal, and an internally matched bridge with partner outside $S$
produces that partner as an impermissible terminal. These exhaust all
components leading from $T$ to a nonbridge $B$ terminal. This reasoning
handles all mixtures of port and internal bridge vertices, with no
restriction on the crossing count.

###### Step 2. How failure of every choice forces a closed set

We use (R) in three kinds of cut, summarized next. Here $M$ is the
complete candidate set of covered bridge mirrors, $k$ are selected,
and $S$ is independent of which $k$ are selected.

| geometry | cut bit | $M$ | $k$ | $S$ | distinguished vertex |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| $H_2$ | 8 | $11,13,14$ | 2 | $11,13,14,31$ | 31 |
| $H_2$ | 16 | $19,21,22,31$ | 3 | $19,21,22,23,31$ | 23 |
| $H_3$ | 8 | $11,13,31$ | 2 | $11,13,14,31$ | 14 |
| $H_3$ | 16 | $19,21,31$ | 2 | $19,21,22,31$ | 22 |

We verify the local theorem conditions in Steps 3--4. In every row,
$S=M\cup\{r\}$ where $r$ is the distinguished vertex. For each
choice of selected bridge vertices $Y\subset M$, its possible obstruction
edge is $r u$, where $u$ is the unique unselected member of $M$.
These obstruction edges all meet $r$, so at most one can belong to
the matching $F$. There are three choices when $|M|=3$ and four when
$|M|=4$. After discarding the at most one fixed-obstruction choice,
the remaining choices still cover every member of $M$: two distinct
two-subsets of a three-set cover it, and three distinct three-subsets
of a four-set cover it.

Assume the global cycle does not exist. Apply (R) to every nonfixed
choice. We get $X_B\subseteq S$ and, by the preceding choice coverage,
every internally matched vertex of $M$ has its partner in $S$. The
only vertex of $S$ that could still be internally matched to $B\setminus S$
is $r$.

All vertices of $S$ are covered. For the three rows with $|S|=4$,
the face $A$ has four original holes, so $c$ is even. For the row
with $|S|=5$, $A$ has five original holes, so $c$ is odd. Hence
$|S|-c$ is even in every row. Exactly $c$ vertices of $S$ are ports,
because all $B$ ports lie in $S$. If $r$ were matched to $B\setminus S$,
the remaining internally matched vertices of $S$ would number
$|S|-c-1$, which is odd. They cannot all be paired within $S$; yet
no other vertex of $S$ is allowed an external partner. This contradiction
shows that $r$ does not escape either.

Every covered vertex of $B\setminus S$ therefore has its partner in
$B\setminus S$: it is not a port and cannot be paired to $S$. Thus

$$C_b=(B\setminus S)\setminus H_j$$

is closed under the original matching. Notice that this parity argument
also covers zero crossings and every port/internal mixture. It does
not assume that the distinguished vertex was selected as a bridge.

###### Step 3. Verification of the two-bridge local inputs

In each two-bridge row of the table, $A$ has four majority holes and
no minority holes; $B$ has the one remaining majority hole $a$ and
all three minority holes. The candidates $M$ are mirrors of the three
available majority holes in $A$ other than $0$. Selecting two candidates
consumes two majority holes in $A$, leaving exactly two majority holes,
so GQ4-avoid applies in Step 1.

For $H_2$ at bit 8 and for $H_3$ at bit 8 the singleton hole is
$a=15$, with its four neighbors in the face $B$ equal to
$\{11,13,14,31\}=S$. For $H_3$ at bit 16 the singleton is $a=23$,
whose four neighbors in $B$ are $\{19,21,22,31\}=S$.
After compression, the holes of $L$ are the singleton majority hole
$a$ and five minority holes (the original three plus the two selected
bridge vertices). T15 is therefore exactly applicable with those
two selected vertices avoided. Since they both neighbor $a$, its sole
possible obstruction is the matching edge on the two remaining members
of $S$, namely $r u$ as in Step 2. All vertices of $S$ are originally
covered, as can also be read directly from $H_2,H_3$.

###### Step 4. Full three-bridge verification for the delta-five cut

For $H_2$ at bit 16, all five majority holes $0,3,5,6,15$ lie in $A$,
and all three minority holes lie in $B$. The mirrors of the four
available majority holes are

$$M=\{19,21,22,31\}.$$

These are covered vertices and are exactly the four neighbors of
$a=23$ within $B$. Choose any three of the four original available
majority holes for the bridges. Pairing their endpoints and all ports
in $D$ removes three majority holes from $A$, leaving exactly two
majority holes, one of which is $0$. Thus the target-face cycle required
in Step 1 follows from GQ4-avoid for every pairing $D$.

The compressed $B$ matching has six minority holes: the original
three odd holes and the three odd bridge vertices. Avoid precisely
the bridge vertices and apply T63. The three chosen vertices have
unique common neighbor $a=23$ in the face $B$. Its only remaining
neighbor is the unselected candidate $u\in M$. Thus the unique possible
T63 obstruction is $23\,u$. This is precisely the edge $r u$ in Step 2,
with $S=M\cup\{23\}$ of size five.

The graph argument in Step 1 is valid for these majority-to-minority
bridges as well as for minority-to-majority bridges. It uses the
post-consumption imbalance in $A$, the hole pattern of $L$, distinct
covered mirror vertices, and path compression; every one of these
conditions has just been checked. No assumption that $A$ originally
contains minority holes, or that $c$ exceeds a threshold, occurs.

###### Step 5. Two closed eight-sets yield three closed four-sets

Steps 2--4, under the supposition that there is no global cycle, give
for both geometries the same closed sets

$$C_8=\{8,9,10,12,24,27,29,30\},$$
$$C_{16}=\{16,17,18,20,24,27,29,30\}.$$

The intersection of two closed matching sets is closed, since the
partner of each point must lie in both. Their differences are also
closed: if a point of $C_8\setminus C_{16}$ had its partner in the
intersection, that partner would have its unique partner outside the
closed set $C_{16}$, a contradiction. The same reasoning applies to
$C_{16}\setminus C_8$. Therefore the following disjoint four-sets are
all closed:

$$I=\{24,27,29,30\},\quad D_8=\{8,9,10,12\},\quad
D_{16}=\{16,17,18,20\}.$$

Put $U=I\cup D_8\cup D_{16}$. The other twelve covered vertices
$R_j=Q_5\setminus(H_j\cup U)$ are closed as well, since their partners
cannot enter any of the three closed four-sets or the original holes.

###### Step 6. Delta-zero cuts restrict the matching on the remaining set

The needed cuts and local data are:

| geometry | cut bit | selected bridge mirrors $Y$ | singleton $a$ | remaining neighbor edge $pq$ | $S=Y\cup\{p,q\}$ |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| $H_2$ | 1 | $27,29$ | 25 | $9\,17$ | $9,17,27,29$ |
| both | 2 | $27,30$ | 26 | $10\,18$ | $10,18,27,30$ |
| both | 4 | $29,30$ | 28 | $12\,20$ | $12,20,29,30$ |

For each listed cut, $A$ has two majority holes, including $0$, and
two minority holes. Select both minority holes as the bridges. Their
mirrors in the table are covered. After consumption $A$ has two majority
holes, so GQ4-avoid applies. The original $B$ holes have three majority
holes and one minority singleton $a$; the bridge mirrors have majority
parity. Thus the compressed matching has the T15 pattern, and the
four neighbors of $a$ in $B$ are exactly the listed set $S$. T15's
possible obstruction is the listed remaining neighbor edge $pq$.

Every listed $pq$ joins a member of $D_8$ to a member of $D_{16}$.
These sets are disjoint and closed, so $pq\notin F$. Step 1 therefore
applies to each cut. The assumed absence of a global cycle forces
$X_B\subseteq S\subseteq U$.

Now suppose an original matching edge with both endpoints in $R_j$
crossed that cut. Its $B$ endpoint would be a port in $R_j$, contrary
to $X_B\subseteq U$ and $R_j\cap U=\varnothing$. Consequently every
matching edge within $R_j$ preserves every listed cut bit.

###### Step 7. Contradiction at vertex 1

For the second residual orbit the closed remaining set is

$$R_2=\{1,2,4,7,11,13,14,19,21,22,23,31\}.$$

By Step 6 every matching edge in $R_2$ preserves bits 1, 2, and 4.
The only vertex of $R_2$ with the same three low bits as vertex 1 is
vertex 1 itself. A matching has no loop, so 1 has no possible partner.

For the third residual orbit the closed remaining set is

$$R_3=\{1,2,4,6,7,11,13,14,19,21,22,31\}.$$

Here bits 2 and 4 are preserved. Vertex 1 is the only member of $R_3$
having both those bits zero. It again has no distinct possible partner.

Both contradictions refute the supposition that a global cycle does
not exist. The asserted cycle therefore exists for every arbitrary
matching with hole set $H_2$ or $H_3$.

###### Step 8. Orbit coverage

A coordinate permutation fixes $0$ and preserves short edges, matching
edges, parity, and the cycle condition. The respective marked geometries
have 20 and 30 distinct coordinate images; these sizes are checked by
directly generating all 120 permutations in the accompanying checker.
Hence the two analytic arguments cover all 50 normalized geometries
in those two residual orbits.

##### Verification and remaining scope

Run `D:\anaconda\python.exe A8_orbits2_3_geometry_check.py` in this
directory. Its output [A8_orbits2_3_geometry_check.json](research/six_directions/A8_orbits2_3_geometry_check.json) checks every
candidate set, local hole count, local obstruction edge, nonfixed-choice
coverage after any possible single fixed obstruction, parity identity,
closed-set identity, and final isolated vertex class. It performs zero
matching-instance enumerations. The mathematical matching argument is
the proof above and still requires fresh independent semantic review.

The original A8 statement is not weakened for these two orbits. This
package by itself establishes no result for the other residual orbits
or for the entire P6 problem. No previously frozen proof or main
ledger was modified.


</details>

<summary>A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md — Q5 A8 proof package: three complete transfer branches and five residual orbits</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_PARTIAL_PROOF_PACKAGE.md)。SHA-256：`3133642eb22daa30c48253dcd97a3a808e8f3169a4c3256af8240ae0f8bd2a5f`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_BRIDGE_INPUTS_REVIEW.json), [A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_DELTA4_FIRST_ORBIT_REVIEW.json), [A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q5_K8_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_K8_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json), [TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json)。

#### Q5 A8 proof package: three complete transfer branches and five residual orbits

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer output; independent review pending.

##### Claim

Let $F$ be any matching of the complete graph on $V(Q_5)$ with exactly
eight holes, three of one parity and five of the other. For every specified
hole $v$ in the larger class, there is a simple cycle on exactly
$V(Q_5)\setminus\{v\}$ containing $F$, with every edge outside $F$ short.
Required edges may be arbitrary long edges and may join equal parities.

##### Status

**NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED.** The original statement is unchanged. This
package proves the augmentation branch and every instance admitting a
coordinate cut of imbalance $1,2,$ or $3$. A complete census reduces the
remaining hole geometries to five explicitly listed orbits; their arbitrary
matching instances remain open. No failed search is presented as a
counterexample, and no sampled success is used to assert a universal claim.

##### Assumptions and dependency map

1. Q5 A6, established in [A6_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md](#proof-a6-closure-draft) and its closure reviews.
2. GQ4-avoid and GQ4-cycle in [Q4_GENERAL_AUGMENTATION.md](#proof-q4-general-augmentation), for arbitrary
   hole counts of imbalance two and zero, respectively.
3. The four-hole optional edge bounds O15 and O18 in Section 2 of
   [A6_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md](#proof-a6-closure-draft), with their certified finite inputs.
4. The residual geometry census is the new independent deterministic
   program [A8_geometry_census.py](research/six_directions/A8_geometry_census.py). It enumerates hole sets only, never
   matching instances. Its output is [A8_geometry_census.json](research/six_directions/A8_geometry_census.json).

Items 1--3 are imported results, not new assumptions on $F$. The partial
proof below uses no Q5 A8/A10, higher-hole P6 claim, or Q5 T15 result.

##### Notation and proof strategy

Call majority parity $O$ and minority parity $E$; these are labels, not
fixed numerical parities. For a coordinate cut let $A$ contain $v$ and
$B$ be the other face. Write $F_A,F_B$ for the internal matching edges,
$C$ for the crossing matching, $c=|C|$, and $X_A,X_B$ for its endpoint
sets. Let $H_A,H_B$ be the original holes, and set
$\delta=|H_A\cap O|-|H_A\cap E|$. For $t\in A$, write $\bar t$ for its
short mirror in $B$, which need not be its required partner.

We add short edges between opposite-parity holes when possible. Otherwise
we use a face cycle or a face path, remove an artificial matching, attach
the original crossings and selected short bridges, and compress the resulting
paths into a matching on the opposite face.

##### Proof

###### Step 1. Augmentation and a local geometric fact

If a minority hole is short-adjacent to a majority hole other than $v$,
add that short edge. The augmented matching has two minority and four
majority holes and still has $v$ free. Q5 A6 gives the desired cycle;
the added edge is short relative to the original matching. Hence we may
assume

$$E\cap H\text{ has no short edge to }(O\cap H)\setminus\{v\}.\tag{I}$$

In $Q_4$, any two distinct same-parity vertices have at least six distinct
neighbors: at distance two they have two common neighbors, and at distance
four none. Therefore two such vertices cannot simultaneously avoid three
vertices of the other parity. We use this fact in each face with its
global parity labels.

The identity $2|F_A|+c=16-|H_A|$ determines the parity of $c$.

###### Step 2. Transfer conventions

If a cycle contains a nonempty matching $D$, deleting $D$ leaves a path
forest with endpoint set $V(D)$. Restoring any proper subset of these
removed edges, possibly as internally disjoint paths, leaves a path
forest: otherwise the restored subset and the undeleted part of the
original cycle would contain a cycle while an edge of the original
cycle remained missing. Thus no component closes prematurely in the
constructions below.

Compressing disjoint paths to edges gives a matching on their endpoints.
If a cycle on the other face contains this matching and avoids its
internal vertices, expansion gives one simple cycle. This preserves all
required edges, and the only newly added edges outside artificial paths
are short edges. Any artificial edge is deleted or expanded.

###### Step 3. All cuts with $\delta=2$

Here $c$ is even. If $c>0$, choose any perfect matching $D$ on $X_A$.
The holes of $F_A\cup D$ are exactly $H_A$, of majority excess two.
GQ4-avoid gives an $A-v$ cycle containing it. Delete $D$, attach every
edge of $C$, and compress to $R$ on $X_B$. The matching $F_B\cup R$
has holes exactly $H_B$, which are balanced because the total excess
is two. GQ4-cycle gives its full $B$ cycle, and expansion finishes.

Suppose $c=0$, and put $k=|H_A\cap E|$. The hole counts in $A$ are
$(k,k+2)$ and in $B$ are $(3-k,3-k)$. If $k=0$, the $B$ face has three
minority and three nonforbidden majority holes, contradicting (I) and
the two-versus-three geometric fact. If $k\ge2$, $A$ has two minority
holes and at least three majority holes other than $v$, with the same
contradiction. Consequently $k=1$. The $A$ holes have counts $(1,3)$,
and the $B$ holes $(2,2)$. O15 supplies at least 15 short optional
edges among the extending $A-v$ cycles; O18 supplies at least 18 among
the full extending $B$ cycles. Under the mirror identification both
unions lie in the 32 edges of $Q_4$. Their intersection is nonempty,
since $15+18>32$. Choose corresponding optional edges in two witnessing
cycles, delete these two edges, and join their corresponding endpoints
by two short edges across the cut. The result is the required single
cycle. The optional edge union argument asserts the existence of
separate witnessing cycles for the chosen edge; it does not prescribe
many optional edges simultaneously.

###### Step 4. All cuts with $\delta=3$

The crossing number $c$ is odd and positive. There are at least two
nonforbidden majority holes in $A$. Choose one, $t$, whose mirror
$w=\bar t$ is not the unique $B$ port when $c=1$; two candidates ensure
this choice exists. For $c\ge3$ choose any such hole. By (I), $w$ is
covered in the original matching, and has minority parity.

Choose a perfect matching $D$ on $X_A\cup\{t\}$. Adding $D$ reduces
the majority excess in the remaining $A$ holes from three to two, so
GQ4-avoid gives an $A-v$ cycle. If $w$ is a port, prescribe $tx\in D$,
where $x$ is the original $A$ partner of $w$; this is possible because
$t$ is a hole and $x$ is a port.

If $w$ is internal to $F_B$, delete $D$, attach $C$ and the bridge $tw$,
and compress to $R$ on $X_B\cup\{w\}$. Let $wk\in F_B$ and $wq\in R$.
Suppress these two edges into $kq$. All other edges remain disjoint,
and the holes of the resulting matching are $H_B\cup\{w\}$. The original
$B$ majority excess is $2-3=-1$; adding the minority hole $w$ gives
excess $-2$. GQ4-avoid therefore applies with minority parity as the
larger class and avoids $w$. Expand $kq$ via $kw$ and the transferred
path; expand every other compressed edge.

If $w$ is a port, then $c\ge3$ by the choice for $c=1$, and $|D|\ge2$.
Delete $D$. The endpoints $t,x$ of its prescribed edge lie in different
path components. Attaching $tw,xw$ restores just that gap through $w$;
at least one other gap remains. Attach all other crossings. Compress
the resulting forest onto $X_B\setminus\{w\}$; its interiors contain
$A-v$ and $w$. Together with $F_B$ this is a matching whose holes are
$H_B\cup\{w\}$, again of excess $-2$. Apply GQ4-avoid avoiding $w$
and expand. This also gives the required cycle.

###### Step 5. All cuts with $\delta=1$

Put $k=|H_A\cap E|$, so $|H_A\cap O|=k+1$. If $k=0$ or $1$, the
$B$ hole counts are $(3-k,4-k)$, containing two minority and three
majority holes, none equal to $v$. This contradicts (I). Hence $k\ge2$.
The crossing number $c$ is odd and positive.

Choose a minority hole $y\in A$. When $c=1$, choose $y$ whose mirror
$w=\bar y$ is not the unique $B$ port; at least two choices of $y$ exist.
For $c\ge3$ any $y$ may be used. By (I), $w$ is covered and has
majority parity. Select a root port $d\in X_A$ and a perfect matching
$D$ on $X_A\setminus\{d\}$. The matching

$$F_A\cup D\cup\{dy\}$$

has original holes $H_A\setminus\{y\}$ of majority excess two and
contains the free forbidden hole $v$. GQ4-avoid supplies an $A-v$
cycle containing $dy$; deleting $dy$ gives an $A-v$ path from $d$ to $y$.

If $w$ is internal to $F_B$, delete $D$ from the path, attach all
crossings and $yw$, compress, and suppress the unique overlap $w$ as
in Step 4. The resulting matching has holes $H_B\cup\{w\}$. The original
$B$ excess is one; adding majority hole $w$ gives excess two.
GQ4-avoid avoiding $w$ and expansion complete the cycle.

If $w$ is a port, $c\ge3$. Choose $d$ to be its original crossing
partner. Then $D$ is nonempty. Deleting $D$ from the $d$--$y$ path
separates its endpoints into different components, since at least one
edge of that path was removed. Attach $dw,yw$ and the other crossings;
the two endpoint components join through $w$ without closing a cycle.
Compress onto $X_B\setminus\{w\}$ and apply GQ4-avoid to the matching
with holes $H_B\cup\{w\}$, avoiding $w$. Expansion finishes.

In particular the exceptional $k=c=1$ endpoint lemma required in the
A6 proof never arises in A8. No new finite endpoint input is needed.

###### Step 6. Exact remaining geometric obligation

Translate $v$ to $0$; this makes the majority parity the numerical even
parity. Let $Z$ be the four other even holes and $W$ the three odd holes.
Condition (I) says every $z\in Z$ is nonadjacent to every $w\in W$.
There are only $\binom{15}{4}$ possibilities for $Z$. For each one the
program lists all odd vertices nonadjacent to $Z$ and all their triples
$W$. This gives exactly 2700 configurations. For coordinate $i$, the
face containing $0$ is its zero face, and the program directly computes

$$\delta_i=1+|\{z\in Z:z_i=0\}|-|\{w\in W:w_i=0\}|.$$

Exactly 2540 configurations have some $\delta_i\in\{1,2,3\}$ and are
proved by Steps 3--5. For every other configuration the program takes
the lexicographically smallest pair $(\pi Z,\pi W)$ over all 120
coordinate permutations. The remaining 160 configurations have exactly
the following five representatives:

| $Z$ | $W$ | orbit size | ordered $(\delta_0,\ldots,\delta_4)$ at this representative |
|---|---|---:|---|
| $3,5,6,15$ | $8,25,26$ | 60 | $0,0,-1,4,4$ |
| $3,5,6,15$ | $25,26,28$ | 20 | $0,0,0,4,5$ |
| $3,5,15,23$ | $25,26,28$ | 30 | $-1,0,0,4,4$ |
| $15,23,27,29$ | $1,2,4$ | 30 | $-1,0,0,-1,-1$ |
| $15,23,27,29$ | $2,4,8$ | 20 | $-2,0,0,0,-1$ |

The census output includes every residual member and its computed
deltas, so both coverage and orbit membership are inspectable. Orbit
sizes sum to 160. The normalization preserves arbitrary matching edges,
the specified forbidden hole, and shortness. The enumerated domain is
therefore a complete geometry reduction, not a finite test of selected
matching instances.

##### Corrections or missing assumptions

To prove the original A8 claim it suffices to prove it for every arbitrary
matching on the 24 covered vertices in each of the five rows. No matching
condition may be silently imposed in that residual theorem.

##### Open risks

The five residual rows remain open. Delta-zero and delta-four double-bridge
transfers can leave a Q4 T15 instance with its genuine triangle obstruction;
the existence of Q4 T15 positive cases does not remove this obstruction.
The separate [A8_DOUBLE_BRIDGE_SUFFICIENT.md](#proof-a8-double-bridge-sufficient) proves a sufficient mechanism
to avoid it in many matching instances, without asserting complete coverage.
No full A8 or full higher-hole P6 closure is claimed by this package.


</details>


<details id="proof-a8-q4-t63-classification" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>A8_Q4_T63_CLASSIFICATION.md — Q4 T63: six same-parity holes with three prescribed avoided holes</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/A8_Q4_T63_CLASSIFICATION.md)。SHA-256：`6d99eb27dd3a1c7396a6ae930959871f9124dd27c12d00ace8a999d0cf09c597`。
