<details id="proof-higher-forced-cherry-transfer" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_TRANSFER.md — Uniform transfer through one or several forced cherries</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_TRANSFER.md)。SHA-256：`a5030f66772259eeb32402c25f92a77761acb454e70696b2d370c652037fbea4`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOURTEEN_FINAL25_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_FINAL25_REVIEW.json), [FOURTEEN_FORCED_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_FORCED_REVIEW.json), [FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json), [SIXTEEN_LOCAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIXTEEN_LOCAL_REVIEW.json), [SIXTEEN_SMALLCUT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIXTEEN_SMALLCUT_REVIEW.json), [SIXTEEN_STAR_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIXTEEN_STAR_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_EXTRA_FORCED_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_EXTRA_FORCED_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_NEW_FORCED_HALL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_NEW_FORCED_HALL_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_STAR_B_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_STAR_B_REVIEW.json)。

#### Uniform transfer through one or several forced cherries

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer candidate. Status: **PROVABLE AS STATED
relative to the explicit local inputs below**; fresh independent review is
required. This is a sufficient-route theorem, not a closure of any higher
hole layer or unrestricted local geometry.

##### Claim and assumptions

Let $M$ be any short matching in $Q_6$ with holes
$H=\{u\}\cup Z\cup W$, where $u$ is even and free,
$|Z|=k-1$, $|W|=k$, $Z$ is even, $W$ is odd, and $Z\cup W$ is independent.
Let $v$ be any odd target, covered or free. Choose a coordinate cut $A,B$
with $v\in A$; put $a=|Z\cap A|$, $b=|W\cap A|$,
$\delta=\mathbf1[u\in A]$. Let $C$ be the original crossing matching,
$c=|C|$, and $X_A,X_B$ its port sets.

Consider either of the following branches with $s\ge3$:

* **Even consumption:** $b\ge1$, $s=a+1-b$, and choose any
  $S\subset Z\cap A$ of size $s$.
* **Odd consumption:** $s=b-a-1$, and choose
  $S\subset(W\cap A)\setminus\{v,\bar u\}$ of size $s$.
  The exclusion of $v$ matters only when $v$ is free, and that of $\bar u$
  only when $u\in B$. Existence of this precise $S$ is a hypothesis.

Here $\bar x$ means the mirror across the cut and $Y=\{\bar x:x\in S\}$.
The intended B matching has hole set
$H_*=(H\cap B)\setminus\{u\}\ \cup Y$ and covered set $K=B\setminus H_*$.
In even consumption its hole counts (global even,odd) are
$(k-a-1,k-b+s)$; in odd consumption they are
$(k-a-1+s,k-b)$. It must admit a local cycle on precisely $B\setminus Y$.

**Single-cherry hypothesis.** Suppose $p,q\in K$ are distinct, have the
same global parity as $Y$, and $u\notin\{p,q\}$. Suppose the actual marked
B geometry has the local classification: for every arbitrary perfect
matching $F$ on $K$, it has a cycle on $B\setminus Y$ containing $F$,
with only short new edges, if and only if $pq\notin F$.
Then $M$ has a Hamilton $u$--$v$ extension with only short new edges.

This statement holds for every feasible $k$, in particular $k=6,7,8,9$
(twelve through eighteen holes); it does not supply the assumed marked
local classification or the existence of a useful cut.

The multi-cherry version and a precise rank criterion supplying its local
classification are proved in Sections5--6. All graph unions retain edge
labels: a common matching pair is a two-edge cycle, not a single edge.

##### Imports and strategy

Import the accepted balanced-hole Q5 endpoint theorem for arbitrary
complete-graph matching edges and every feasible balanced hole count:
any free root and opposite-parity covered or free target have a Hamilton
path through that matching, with only short new edges. The full A10
assembly and [Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW.json) accept the consequences of
[Q5_HIGHER_HOLE_REDUCTION.md](#proof-q5-higher-hole-reduction), together with full A8 and the named earlier
inputs. Thus the old uniform transfer's small balanced-hole range need
not restrict $a,b$ here. Global parity is restricted to a face; choosing
face coordinates may reverse both parity names, which the import allows.

Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem for
$c=0$, exactly as in [HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER.md](#proof-higher-hole-unified-transfer).
For $c>0$ we prove the forest construction directly. Its degree accounting,
tag and simultaneous suppression agree with that accepted uniform
transfer. The single-cherry avoidance extends the accepted
[Q5_T17_RANK_ROOT_NOT_OB_TRANSFER.md](#proof-q5-t17-rank-root-not-ob-transfer); that frozen text is not modified.

Dependency map: all-balanced Q5 endpoints -> A Hamilton path -> controlled
deletion forest -> actual compressed B matching avoids the local obstruction
-> assumed B classification -> expansion. In Section5 the optional local
input is obtained from independently verified forest ranks and the generic
complete-graph matching-connectivity rank upper bound. No Q6 higher layer
is an input to this proof.

##### 1. Legal completions and uniform gap lower bounds

If $c=0$, invoke the explicit five-direction import and finish. Assume
$c>0$. Shortness of the internal matching $M_A$ gives

$$|X_A\cap E|-|X_A\cap O|=b-a-\delta,
\qquad c\equiv a+b+\delta\pmod2.$$

Choose root $r$ and the set $V_D$ to be paired as follows:

| Branch | Root face | $r$ | $V_D$ | A holes after completion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|even|$\delta=1$|$u$|$X_A\cup S$|$(b,b)$|
|even|$\delta=0$|any member of $S$|$X_A\cup(S\setminus\{r\})$|$(b,b)$|
|odd|$\delta=1$|$u$|$X_A\cup S$|$(a+1,a+1)$|
|odd|$\delta=0$|any even port|$(X_A\setminus\{r\})\cup S$|$(a+1,a+1)$|

For the last row the even-port surplus is $b-a=s+1$, so such a port
exists and $c\ge s+1$. Every $V_D$ has even cardinality by the congruence
above. Its vertices are free for $M_A$, distinct from $r$, and do not
include a free target $v$ by the source exclusions. A covered target can
belong to $V_D$ only when it is a crossing port.

Let $D$ be any perfect pairing of $V_D$ for now, and write $d=|D|$.
When $\delta=1$, $d=(c+s)/2\ge2$ since $c\ge1$, $s\ge3$.
When $\delta=0$, $d=(c+s-1)/2$. In even consumption $c+s-1\ge3$ and is
even, hence $d\ge2$. In odd consumption $c\ge s+1$ gives $d\ge s\ge3$.

The A matching $M_A+D$ has exactly the balanced hole counts in the table,
with $r$ free and even and $v$ an odd legal target. Apply the all-balanced
endpoint import to obtain a simple Hamilton $r$--$v$ path $P_A$ containing
every edge of $M_A+D$. Artificial $D$ edges may be long or same-parity;
all other new local edges are short.

##### 2. Actual transfer and suppression

Each $y\in Y$ is originally internally matched in B. Indeed its source
mirror is originally free, so it cannot be a crossing port; independence
of $Z\cup W$ excludes any original nonroot hole at $y$; and $y\ne u$ by
parity in even consumption and the explicit root-mirror exclusion in odd
consumption. Put $h_y=M_B(y)$. These mates are distinct and have parity
opposite to $Y$. Being internally covered, they are not ports or the
root; their parity also puts them outside $Y$.

Delete $D$ from $P_A$, attach every original crossing and all short bridges
$x\bar x$ for $x\in S$, and add tagged edge $uv$. If $u\in A$, one can
equivalently first add $uv$ to $P_A$, obtaining one simple32-cycle, then
delete $D$. Its endpoint edge was not already on $P_A$. Since $d\ge2$,
at least one cycle edge was removed and the result is a forest. If $u\in B$,
start with a path forest; all attachments, including the previously free
root at $v$, are distinct B leaves and create no cycle.

Degree accounting leaves all A vertices with degree two: the missing
degree at $r$ is supplied by its source bridge or crossing when $r\ne u$;
the tag supplies the true endpoint degree at $v$ and at $u$ when $u\in A$.
Each deleted D endpoint receives one attachment. If a covered target is a
port and loses its only A path edge, its crossing and tag restore degree
two. A free target is not in $D$ and keeps its A path edge plus the tag.
Thus compression gives a perfect matching $T$ on
$X_B\cup Y\cup(\{u\}\cap B)$, with exactly one tag-carrying path.

The only degree conflicts in $T+M_B$ are at $Y$, with the distinct pendant
mates $h_y$ described above. A conflict component contains one T edge and
at most one pendant original edge at each endpoint. It cannot be a cycle.
Suppress $Y$ in every such component and carry along the actual paths and
tag. The result is a perfect matching $L$ on $K$, with hole set exactly
$H_*$, including $Y$ as omitted holes. It may have arbitrary long or
same-parity edges; its precise edges, not just $M_B$, must satisfy the B
input.

##### 3. One cherry: preventing the actual compressed pair

Both $p,q$ are originally covered: they are outside $H_*$ and $Y$, and
the only original hole removed from $H\cap B$ was $u$, which is excluded.
They have $Y$'s parity. Consequently $pq\notin M_B$ by shortness.

If an obstruction endpoint is not a port, it is not a T endpoint either:
it is outside $Y$ and the root. Its original internal matching edge stays
unchanged. Its opposite-parity mate is not in $Y$, cannot be a port or free
root, and is not the other obstruction endpoint. If a T edge ends in $Y$,
suppression moves that end to $h_y$ of opposite parity, and a Y--Y edge
becomes an edge between two such mates. An edge to $u$ remains incident
with that distinct root. These cases prove

$$pq\in L\ \Longrightarrow\ p,q\in X_B\text{ and }pq\in T.$$

If either vertex is not a port, any legal $D$ therefore works. Otherwise
let $p',q'$ be their actual original A crossing partners and prescribe
$p'q'\in D$. This is legal: in even consumption $r$ is the originally
free root or a source hole, never a port. In odd consumption with
$\delta=0$, the B obstruction endpoints are even, their crossing partners
are odd, and $r$ was chosen even. For $\delta=1$, $r=u$ is originally free.
The prescribed endpoints are distinct from all source holes, so the
remaining even number of vertices in $V_D$ can be paired arbitrarily.

For $\delta=1$, the tagged A cycle loses $p'q'$ and at least one other
D edge. Its direct $p'$--$q'$ arc and its complementary arc are both cut.
Hence $p',q'$ lie in different remaining A components. B leaf attachments
cannot merge those components, so $p,q$ are not one T pair.
For $\delta=0$, deleting $p'q'$ from a simple A path already separates
its endpoints. Further deletions and distinct B leaf attachments cannot
reconnect them. Thus again $pq\notin T$, and hence $pq\notin L$.

The covered target-port boundary is included: if $v$ is incident with the
prescribed D edge, deletion may isolate $v$ in the A path. For $\delta=1$
the retained tag is part of the tagged-cycle proof. For $\delta=0$ the
segment is $u-v-\bar v$, which cannot have endpoints $p,q$ because the
root is excluded. For a free target this degeneracy cannot occur because
$v\notin V_D$.

Apply the assumed B classification to the actual $L$. Expand its cycle
through the suppressed mirrors $Y$ and transferred A paths. These paths
are disjoint except for their prescribed cycle endpoints; no physical edge
is reused. Expansion gives a tagged spanning64-cycle containing all
original M edges. Delete the tag. All D edges had been deleted, all
compressed edges were expanded, and every remaining new edge is a local
cube edge or selected short bridge. This proves the single-cherry theorem.

##### 4. Source existence for free targets

In even consumption $b\ge1$ implies $s=a+1-b\le a$; sources exist and
cannot be the odd target. In odd consumption the exact existence condition is

$$b-|(W\cap A)\cap\{v,\bar u\}|\ge s=b-a-1.$$

For covered targets at most the root mirror is excluded, so this always
holds. For free targets with $a\ge1$ at most two holes are excluded and
it also holds. With a free target and $a=0$, two distinct excluded holes
can leave too few sources; $Z\cup W$ independence alone does not remove
this possibility. No route is claimed without legal sources.

If the full original hole set $H=\{u\}\cup Z\cup W$ is independent, then
$\bar u\notin W$, so at most $v$ is excluded; the odd source set exists
even when $a=0$. This is a useful free-target corollary under a declared
stronger geometry hypothesis. It is not silently inferred from
$Z\cup W$ independence, nor from an unproved predecessor hole layer.

##### 5. Several cherries: exact local rank criterion

This section is a general local lemma on one Q5 face. Let $H_*$ be its
holes, $Y\subset H_*$ its specified omissions, and $K$ its $2n$ covered
terminals. Assume $n\ge2$. A legal short-complement forest has degree zero
on $Y$, two on $H_*\setminus Y$, one on $K$, and consists of paths whose
endpoints partition $K$. Write $P$ for its endpoint perfect matching.

Let $R$ be a fixed matching of $r$ pairs on $K$, with $1\le r<n$.
Suppose every legal short-complement forest has endpoint pairing containing
$R$. To prove the positive direction it suffices to supply a selected
family of such forests whose reduced pairings $P^-=P\setminus R$,
on $K^-=K\setminus V(R)$, have rank $2^{n-r-1}$ against any supplied
perfect-matching columns in the connectivity matrix on these $2(n-r)$
labels. The generic upper bound for that matrix is the only rank import.

Then, for every arbitrary perfect matching $F$ on $K$,

$$\text{a required local cycle exists}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F+R\text{ has no labeled cycle}.$$

**Necessity.** Any local cycle through $F$, after deleting $F$, gives one
of the legal complement forests and hence a pairing containing $R$.
A cycle in $F+R$ is a full component of $F+P$, because all its vertices
already have one F and one R edge. It misses the nonempty set $K^-$,
so $F+P$ cannot be a single alternating cycle. This contradiction proves
necessity; a common pair $F\cap R$ is included as a two-edge obstruction.

**Sufficiency.** If $F+R$ has no cycle, it is a disjoint union of paths.
Every vertex of $V(R)$ has degree two and every other vertex of $K$ has
degree one, so its path endpoints are exactly $K^-$. Suppressing all
internal $V(R)$ vertices produces an arbitrary perfect matching $F^-$ on
$K^-$. For any selected $P=R\cup P^-$, replacing those internally
disjoint F/R paths by single edges preserves connectedness of the labeled
unions:

$$F+P\text{ is one alternating cycle}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F^-+P^-\text{ is one alternating cycle}.$$

The verified reduced rank and upper bound make the selected rows span
the full connectivity row space. The column of every $F^-$ is nonzero:
cyclically join consecutive F-minus edges; for two residual terminals
use the labeled double-edge cycle convention. Some selected row connects
it. Undo the suppressions and expand the selected short forest to obtain
the required local cycle. Since the original full terminal domain has
at least four vertices, a shared physical F/forest edge would form a
proper two-edge component and could not have passed connectedness.

For $r=1$, acyclicity of $F+R$ is exactly absence of that one pair in F.
For $r\ge2$, absence of the individual R edges is insufficient. For
example $R=\{01,23\}$ and $F=\{12,30,45\}$ have no common pair but contain
the alternating cycle $0-1-2-3-0$. The other endpoints ensure it is a
proper component. The case $r=n$ is deliberately excluded: there are no
residual endpoints, $F+R$ always has cycles, and the stated necessity
argument would not exclude one Hamilton alternating component.

##### 6. Multi-cherry transfer: the extra gap is automatic

Return to the global setup, with the same legal sources and $s\ge3$.
Let $R$ be a matching of local covered B vertices, all of whose endpoints
have the parity of $Y$, lie outside $Y$, and exclude $u$.
Assume the actual marked B geometry has the local classification

$$\text{cycle on }B\setminus Y\text{ through arbitrary }F
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F+R\text{ is acyclic}.$$

Section5 is one sufficient way to establish this input; a fresh audited
alternative proof is also allowed. Let

$$J_B=\{pq\in R:p,q\in X_B\},\qquad j=|J_B|,$$

and let $J_A$ be the matching of their actual crossing partners in A.
These j edges are pairwise disjoint and are all legal completion pairs
by the same parity/root argument as in Section3. Prescribe $J_A\subset D$
and pair the rest of $V_D$ arbitrarily.

Under precisely the stated hypotheses a Hamilton $u$--$v$ extension
exists. No additional bound on $|R|$ and no matching-dependent extra-gap
hypothesis are needed. Because R is a matching, every edge of $J_B$
consumes two distinct ports, and therefore

$$j\le\lfloor c/2\rfloor.$$

For $\delta=1$, $d=(c+s)/2>\lfloor c/2\rfloor$; for $\delta=0$,
$d=(c+s-1)/2>\lfloor c/2\rfloor$. Both strict inequalities follow from
$s\ge3$. Thus $d>j$ holds automatically in both root faces, and at least
one D edge remains outside the prescribed set $J_A$. The actual bound is
on both-port obstruction pairs, not on the total number of cherries.

To prove the claim, every cycle in $L+R$ would alternate L and R edges,
and all its vertices would belong to $V(R)$, which has Y's parity.
Section3's suppression analysis now applies to each possible L edge
within $V(R)$: such an edge can only be an unchanged direct T pairing
between two ports. Original internal edges and suppressed bridge-mate
edges end outside this parity class. An edge to the root cannot belong
to the cycle because $u\notin V(R)$. Thus the putative cycle lies in
$T+J_B$.

Lift every T edge of that cycle to its actual transferred A path and
the crossing attachments at its port endpoints. Replace every J-B edge
by its prescribed A pair in $J_A$, deleting the now-superfluous B port
leaves and crossings along this cycle. This gives a cycle in the graph
obtained from the tagged A graph by deleting $D$ and restoring $J_A$.
The lifted paths are internally disjoint, so this operation does not
create a merely closed walk with repeated interior vertices.

If $\delta=1$, write $Q=P_A+uv$, a simple cycle. The graph in question is

$$Q-(D\setminus J_A).$$

Since $d>j$, it is a proper edge-deleted subgraph of a simple cycle,
and therefore a forest. If $\delta=0$, ignore the tag's root leaf, which
cannot participate in the putative cycle. The graph in question is

$$P_A-(D\setminus J_A),$$

a subgraph of a simple path, hence a forest even when $D=J_A$.
Both conclusions contradict the lifted cycle. Consequently $L+R$ is
acyclic and the assumed local classification and tagged expansion finish.
The argument includes a covered target port isolated after deleting D;
the tag either belongs to Q or has the excluded root as a leaf.

The extra-gap distinction is real for the abstract graph argument. If
$\delta=1$ and
$D=J_A$, restoring all prescribed pairs restores the entire tagged A
cycle. Upon path compression this can produce a full alternating
$T+J_B$ cycle even though no individual R pair is a T edge. This is a
failure of this prescription argument, not a counterexample to the
global endpoint theorem. The port count excludes this event under the
present hypotheses. Outside those hypotheses no claim is made that a
different D or cut cannot work. In the $\delta=0$ path case restoration
of all D edges would still be acyclic, providing a stronger abstract fact
than the uniform extra-gap bound used here.

##### Boundaries and outstanding work

The new results are complete conditional proofs, submitted for fresh
review. Higher marked local rank certificates, actual useful cut/source
coverage, and whole twelve-to-eighteen-hole closure are not provided.
Root-in-obstruction cases, mixed-parity obstruction endpoints, and
transfers outside the declared source/consumption hypotheses are not
covered. In particular, general tagged-cycle prescriptions without any
unprescribed gap are not justified by this argument; the present port
bound guarantees that gap. Source shortage for a free target under only
nonroot independence
must be handled by another route or an explicit stronger hypothesis.
No unconditional predecessor induction is introduced. The proposed
single-cherry result specializes to the accepted ten-hole two-row lemma,
and the multi-cherry result strictly tracks cycles of the whole F+R
union, not just membership of individual pairs.

##### Author sanity evidence, not independent acceptance

[HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_author_check.py](research/six_directions/HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_author_check.py) exhausts all perfect F matchings
on four, six, eight and ten terminals for every nonempty fixed partial R
with at least two residual terminals. It compares119238 full/reduced
connectivity instances and checks both directions of the contraction
criterion. It also checks8640 integer port/gap parameter cases and the
two explicit alternating-cycle boundary examples above. All pass.
These finite checks support the argument but do not prove its universal
quantifiers or replace the requested fresh proof review.


</details>

<summary>HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER.md — A uniform cut transfer for the remaining P6 layers</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER.md)。SHA-256：`75f481593ecff17f888102e687c0c669f8dd96cdd5ce953434fb93de644df0ed`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOURTEEN_FORCED_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_FORCED_REVIEW.json), [FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_FORCED_CHERRY_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json), [Q5_A8_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_A8_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json), [Q5_T15_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_T15_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json), [Q5_T17_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_T17_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json), [Q5_T26_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_T26_RANK_BATCH_REVIEW.json), [Q5_T63_RANK_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_T63_RANK_REVIEW.json), [SIXTEEN_LOCAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIXTEEN_LOCAL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_T63_SPLIT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_T63_SPLIT_REVIEW.json), [TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json), [TEN_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json), [TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_EXTRA_TYPES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_EXTRA_TYPES_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_NEW_TYPES_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_NEW_TYPES_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json)。

#### A uniform cut transfer for the remaining P6 layers

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. Proposed proof relative to explicit imports;
independent review pending. Full P6 and the 10--18-hole layers remain open.

##### Claim, assumptions, and notation

Let $M$ be a short matching in $Q_6$ with $2k$ holes, let $u$ be a free
even root, and let $v$ be any odd target, covered or free. Write the holes
as $\{u\}\cup Z\cup W$, where $|Z|=k-1$, $|W|=k$, all members of $Z$
are even and all members of $W$ are odd. Assume $Z\cup W$ is independent.
This assumption is a legitimate induction reduction only after the
$(2k-2)$-hole theorem is available; it is not currently a proof of that
predecessor theorem for $k\ge6$.

Choose a coordinate cut $A,B$ with $v\in A$. Put
$a=|Z\cap A|$, $b=|W\cap A|$, and $\delta=1$ if $u\in A$, otherwise $0$.
Let $C$ be the original crossing matching, $c=|C|$, $X_A,X_B$ its port sets,
and $M_A,M_B$ the internal matching restrictions. The mirror of a vertex
across this coordinate is denoted by $\bar x$.

Import the established five-direction free-root endpoint theorem for $c=0$.
For $c>0$, import the full $Q_5$ local endpoint lemma for arbitrary complete-
graph matchings with balanced $2,4,6$ holes: any free even root and any odd
target have a spanning path containing the matching with only short new
edges. Import full-cycle extensions for balanced $0,2,4,6$ holes; omit-one
extensions for hole counts $(j,j+2)$, $j=0,1,2$, at every specified majority
hole; and T44_5 for four same-parity holes, omitting any specified two.
These are the accepted A6/N14/A4, perfect-matching, and T44_5 consequences
in [EIGHT_HOLE_CONDITIONAL_REDUCTION_DRAFT.md](#proof-eight-hole-conditional-reduction-draft) Section 1 and the final
reviews cited by [EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_CLOSURE.md](#proof-eight-hole-full-closure). No higher-hole P6 theorem
is imported.

The following transfer is conditional on the exact B-side cycle theorem
specified below. In the corollary table all its local inputs are already
proved, so those cut classes are unconditional relative to the imports.

##### 1. Excess even holes in A

Suppose $1\le b\le3$ and $s=a+1-b\ge0$. Choose any $s$ members $S$ of
$Z\cap A$; this is possible because $b\ge1$. The desired B-side input is
the cycle-extension theorem for hole counts

$$ (k-a-1,\ k-b+s), $$

omitting exactly the $s$ odd holes $Y=\{\bar x:x\in S\}$.
This input must hold for the actual marked hole geometry and **every**
arbitrary complete-graph matching on its complement.

If $\delta=1$, pair $X_A\cup S$ arbitrarily into a matching $D$ and take
$r=u$. The holes of $M_A+D$ are $(b,b)$ and include $r$.
Indeed $c+s$ is even, since $c\equiv a+1+b\pmod2$.

If $\delta=0$ and $s\ge1$, choose $r\in S$ and pair
$X_A\cup(S\setminus\{r\})$ into $D$. Its cardinality is even since
$c\equiv a+b\pmod2$. The holes are again $(b,b)$ and include $r$.
There is no requirement for an even crossing port in this case.

If $\delta=0$ and $s=0$, then $b=a+1$. Shortness of $M_A$ gives
$|X_A\cap E|-|X_A\cap O|=b-a=1$. Choose an even port $r$ and pair
$X_A\setminus\{r\}$ into $D$. The completed holes are $(b,b)$.

Use the imported endpoint theorem for a spanning $r$--$v$ path in A.
Delete $D$, attach every original crossing edge, and attach the short
bridges $x\bar x$ for all $x\in S$. If $r\in S$, its bridge makes it
an interior vertex; if $r\in X_A$, its original crossing edge does so.
If $r=u$, it remains the true global endpoint. The other endpoint is $v$.
This remains true when $v$ is a crossing port or a free vertex.

Every $y\in Y$ is internally covered by $M_B$: independence excludes an
original odd hole at $y$, its even mirror $x$ is free so it is not a
crossing port, and $y\ne u$ by parity. The bridges are mutually distinct.

##### 2. Excess odd holes in A

Suppose $0\le a\le2$ and $t=b-a-1\ge1$. Choose a set $S\subset W\cap A$
of size $t$ that excludes $v$ (if free) and excludes the vertex $\bar u$
(if it lies in A). This existence is an explicit hypothesis of this branch.
It always holds for covered targets, since $b-t=a+1\ge1$; it also always
holds for free targets when $a\ge1$, since at most two vertices are excluded.

The required B-side cycle input has hole counts

$$ (k-a-1+t,\ k-b), $$

and omits exactly the $t$ even holes $Y=\{\bar x:x\in S\}$.

For $\delta=1$, take $r=u$ and pair $X_A\cup S$ into $D$.
For $\delta=0$, the port difference is $b-a=t+1>0$, so choose an even
port $r$ and pair $(X_A\setminus\{r\})\cup S$ into $D$.
The parity identities above show these sets have even size. The holes
of $M_A+D$ are $(a+1,a+1)$; $r$ is free, and $v$ remains a legal odd
target. Apply the local endpoint theorem, delete $D$, and attach crossings
and all bridges at $S$ as in Section 1.

Each $y\in Y$ is internally covered by $M_B$: independence excludes $Z$,
the choice of $S$ excludes $u$, and a free mirror excludes crossing ports.
All bridge conflicts now have even parity.

##### 3. Tagged closure and simultaneous conflict compression

In both branches all A vertices have their intended final degrees. Deleting
$D$ from one A path leaves a path forest; all attachments are at distinct
B vertices. If $u\in A$, $D$ is nonempty ($c>0$, and the pairing set has
positive even size), so the two true endpoint segments are distinct.
If $u\in B$, it has not been attached. Add a tagged artificial edge $uv$.
For $u\in A$ this joins the two different terminal segments; for $u\in B$
it extends the single terminal segment to $u$. The result remains a forest.
Compress all A-interior paths into a matching $T$ on distinct B endpoints.
Exactly one edge of $T$ carries the tag.

The only degree conflicts in $T\cup M_B$ occur at $Y$. Each $y\in Y$
has a distinct original mate $h_y$ of the opposite parity. Every $h_y$ is
outside the endpoints of $T$: it is internally covered, is not a crossing
port or the free root, and cannot be in the same-parity set $Y$. Thus the
conflict components are paths, each with an original pendant endpoint
$h_y$; they cannot be cycles. Suppress every $y\in Y$ in these components,
recording the paths and any tag, to obtain an arbitrary matching $L$ on B.

The endpoints of $T$ are exactly $X_B\cup Y$ and additionally $u$ when
$u\in B$. Consequently the holes of $L$ are precisely

$$ (H_B\setminus\{u\})\cup Y, $$

where $u$ is removed only when it belongs to B. These give the counts in
Sections 1--2. Applying the specified B theorem produces a single cycle
on $B\setminus Y$ containing $L$. Expand each suppressed conflict path,
then each transferred A path. The result is one spanning cycle on $Q_6$
containing the tag and every original matching edge. Delete the tagged
$uv$ edge to obtain the required Hamilton $u$--$v$ path. All remaining
new edges are short: artificial completion edges were deleted, and all
compressed edges were expanded. This proves the conditional transfer.

##### 4. Already available cut classes for ten and twelve holes

The following rows work for **both free and covered** odd targets.
All odd-consumption rows have $a\ge1$, so their selection condition holds.
The zero-crossing case is handled by the five-direction import.

| total holes | $(a,b)$ | A balanced holes | B hole counts; omitted holes | input |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
|10|(1,2)|(2,2)|(3,3); none|balanced six-hole cycle|
|10|(2,3)|(3,3)|(2,2); none|balanced four-hole cycle|
|10|(2,2)|(2,2)|(2,4); one odd|A6|
|10|(3,3)|(3,3)|(1,3); one odd|A4|
|10|(1,3)|(2,2)|(4,2); one even|A6 reversed|
|10|(2,4)|(3,3)|(3,1); one even|A4 reversed|
|10|(4,3)|(3,3)|(0,4); two odd|T44_5|
|10|(2,5)|(3,3)|(4,0); two even|T44_5 reversed|
|12|(2,3)|(3,3)|(3,3); none|balanced six-hole cycle|
|12|(3,3)|(3,3)|(2,4); one odd|A6|
|12|(2,4)|(3,3)|(4,2); one even|A6 reversed|

The marked T15 cases provide further **conditional geometric** entries:
ten holes $(3,2)$ or $(1,4)$, and twelve holes $(4,3)$ or $(2,5)$.
Their A hole counts are respectively $(2,2)$ or $(3,3)$ and the B counts
are $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$, omitting two majority holes. Only the already
audited marked T15 geometries may be used; unrestricted T15 is not proved.

##### 5. Remaining obligations and scope

No assertion is made that every ten- or twelve-hole geometry has a row
in this table. A complete census must account for all free/covered targets,
and any further T15 use must track the actual marked omissions. For 14--18
holes this particular table supplies no complete route. The original full
P6 objective is unchanged, and the proven eight-hole package is not edited.


</details>


<details id="proof-higher-post12-reuse-proof" class="source-doc" markdown="1">

#### Conditional sixteen/eighteen-hole reuse and positive Hall reductions

2026-11-02. ARIS proof-writer candidate; independent checking pending.

##### Exact claim and dependency boundary

Assuming the complete fourteen-hole prescribed-endpoint theorem, the
sixteen-hole problem reduces to 1,211 covered-target geometries. Assuming
the complete sixteen-hole theorem, the eighteen-hole problem reduces to
150 covered-target geometries. Both reductions leave no free-target
geometries. Neither predecessor assumption nor either full layer is proved
by this document. The finite application and exclusions also await fresh
independent verification.

The starting source streams are the already reviewed
`HIGHER_Q5_FULL_residual_h{16,18}_v{1,7,31}_{covered,free}.bin` files.
Their use as complete remaining domains has the preceding-layer condition
stated in HIGHER_Q5_FULL_NEARBALANCED.md. Records consist of sorted Z(k-1)
then W(k), with root0, 2k holes and the named opposite-parity target.

##### Reused universal local inputs

The registry is exactly the FOURTEEN_REUSE accepted registry plus the twenty
new local inputs explicitly accepted by FOURTEEN_CACHED_REVIEW. The latter
are ordinary universal local cycle inputs. Their 47,015 normalized keys
transport minority, majority and omitted vertices by one common cube map.
The old packed T26/T15/T17/T63 registries and analytical T44/T15/T63 split
routes are unchanged. The fresh reviewer must reconstruct this union from
the accepted marked inputs, not merely trust a generated lookup file.

For each original geometry, try all six target-facing cuts and all legal
source subsets. In the even row s=a+1-b, the B local hole counts are
(k-a-1,k-b+s); in the odd row s=b-a-1 they are (k-b,k-a-1+s).
The omitted vertices are the mirrors of the sources. Odd sources exclude
the root mirror and a free target. Every mirror is an originally covered
vertex. The full balanced Q5 endpoint theorem supplies the A completion,
including arbitrary artificial matching edges and prescribed endpoints.
The already accepted generic transfer then applies for each k. Forced
single-pair inputs retain all generic hypotheses, including s>=3 and root
not among the obstruction endpoints. No new root-in-obstruction route or
unreviewed local rank input is used.

Each positive record is certified by the original 32-byte witness format:
uint32 source index; uint8 cut/family; uint16 exact local ID; uint64 actual
source mask; uint32 minority/majority/omitted masks and forced endpoint
mask. The finite checker must independently check every actual projection,
lookup, root/target restriction, and complete byte partition. These
geometrical witnesses establish a route for every realizing original short
matching, with its A completion and paths allowed to depend on that matching.

##### Positive impossibility exclusions

The subsequent Hall witnesses use the 22-byte `<BBIQQ` format: target,
free-target flag, source index, S and T masks. For 2k holes, the covered
parity classes each have 32-k vertices. Each S is a nonempty subset of the
covered even class; T is its entire covered odd neighborhood, and
|T|<|S|. Any original short matching would inject S into T. Thus that input
is unrealizable. No maximal-matching search result is itself a premise.
Retained inputs carry no automatic realizability claim.

Sixteen-hole free inputs 42,846 (0/15,786/27,060) all have positive reuse
witnesses. The eighteen-hole source has zero free inputs. The sixteen-hole
total source is 2,515,014; reuse covers 2,496,814 and leaves18,200; Hall
excludes16,989 and leaves1,211. The eighteen-hole source is80,805; reuse

The generated scanners differ from the original fourteen-hole producer in

accepted registry. This is an implementation description, not a proof of

#### One marked T39 input finishes the conditional eighteen-hole step

2026-11-02. ARIS proof-writer; finite evidence pending independent review.

<summary>HIGHER_Q5_FULL_NEARBALANCED.md — Full Q5 local inputs: near-balanced cuts for the 12--18-hole layers</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_NEARBALANCED.md)。SHA-256：`964551b96288bb5f2f09bddf84f1de81e64acb09b5441d37e25e57f5417efc79`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOURTEEN_HALL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_HALL_REVIEW.json), [FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json)。

#### Full Q5 local inputs: near-balanced cuts for the 12--18-hole layers

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer producer package. The row proof is relative
to accepted local imports; the new exact census is producer evidence
pending independent review. Full 12--18-hole Q6 and full P6 remain OPEN.

##### Exact row theorem

Let M be a short matching of Q6 with 2k holes, 6<=k<=9. Fix a free root
u and any opposite-parity target v, free or covered. Normalize u=0 even,
write its other even holes as Z (size k-1) and odd holes as W (size k),
and assume Z union W is independent. Choose a coordinate face A containing
v, let B be the other face, and put a=|Z intersect A|, b=|W intersect A|.

The following cut rows suffice for a Hamilton u--v path through M with
all new edges short, relative to the stated accepted local inputs:

1. b=a with b>=1;
2. b=a+1;
3. b=a+2, provided an odd source in W intersect A exists that is neither
   the free target v nor the mirror of u across the cut.

For a covered target row3 always has a source because b>=2 and only the
root mirror can be excluded. For a free target it always has a source if
the entire hole set {u} union Z union W is independent; the root mirror
then is not a hole and only v must be excluded. Without that stronger
independence assumption one must check the source condition explicitly:
a=0,b=2 can have two different forbidden sources and is not automatic.
The row a=b=0 is deliberately excluded: its even bridge source does not
exist. No matching feasibility assumption or sampled matching is used.

##### Accepted imports and their ranges

`Q5_A10_FULL_REVIEW` accepts every arbitrary K(Q5) matching with balanced
m:m holes, m=1,...,16, from any free root to any opposite-parity target,
covered or free, with only short new edges. It accepts full cycles for
m=0,...,16. It also accepts every feasible imbalance-two avoid-one input
with holes (t-1,t+1), t=1,...,15, for every marked majority hole and both
parity orientations. Required local matching edges may be long or join
equal parities. All these ranges are part of the reviewed consequence
statement, not an extrapolation from small cases.

Use the accepted uniform-transfer construction and its explicit
five-direction free-root endpoint input for zero original crossings.
Its old numerical restrictions b<=3 or a<=2 served the former limited
A endpoint imports. The construction is replayed below with the new full
balanced-hole theorem. No complete higher-hole Q6 theorem is used to
obtain these local Q5 inputs.

##### Completion, endpoint and hole-count proof

Let C be the actual original crossing matching, c=|C|, and X_A,X_B its
distinct endpoint sets. If c=0, apply the accepted five-direction theorem.
For c>0 write delta=1 if u belongs to A, and 0 otherwise.

In row1, select one even source z from Z intersect A; in row2 select no
source. Equivalently s=a+1-b is one or zero. If delta=1, take r=u and pair
X_A plus the s sources into a matching D. If delta=0 and s=1, let r be
the source and pair X_A. If delta=0 and s=0, shortness of the original
internal matching gives one more even than odd crossing port; choose an
even port r and pair all other A ports. The endpoint pairing sets are
even by 2|M_A|+c=32-|H_A|. The completed A matching M_A union D has
exactly b holes of each parity, and r is free. In row1 b>=1, and in row2
b=a+1>=1, so the full local endpoint theorem applies. Its odd target v
is legal whether covered or free; even consumption never consumes v.

After the accepted transfer and tagging, the B matching has hole counts
(k-a-1,k-b+s). In row1 these are (k-a-1,k-a+1), and exactly the source
mirror is omitted; it lies in the majority class. The full Q5 imbalance-
two avoid-one theorem applies. In row2 both counts equal k-a-1; the full
balanced-cycle theorem applies, including zero holes/perfect matching.

In row3 choose the one legal odd source w specified in the theorem.
If delta=1 take r=u and pair X_A union {w}. If delta=0, shortness gives
two more even than odd crossing ports; choose an even port r and pair
(X_A minus {r}) union {w}. The completed A matching has a+1 holes of
each parity, includes the free even r, and still permits target v.
Use its full local endpoint theorem. The transferred B holes are
(k-a,k-a-2), with the even source mirror as the sole prescribed majority
omission. The reversed imbalance-two theorem applies. All declared B
counts are nonnegative and feasible for an actually constructed matching.
The A balanced parameter is at least one in every branch.

##### Forest, conflict and artificial-edge bookkeeping

Every selected source is originally free. Its mirror cannot be a crossing
port, because a crossing edge at that B vertex would have to use its
actual short mirror as partner in the original short M. Independence
excludes its being an original hole of the opposite parity. Even-source
mirrors have odd parity and cannot be u; the odd-source hypothesis
excludes u explicitly. Thus every mirror is internally B-covered.

Apply the local A path, delete D, attach all original crossings and the
one bridge if present. Distinct physical attachments preserve a path
forest, including a temporarily isolated crossing target. The artificial
tag uv joins the true endpoint segments when u is in A, or extends the
v segment to the previously unattached u in B. For u in A the parity
identities and c>0 make D nonempty; for u in B the D-empty boundary is
already included in the accepted tagged construction. Compress A paths.

The only B conflict is the single internally covered bridge mirror y.
Its original mate is outside every transferred endpoint: it is internally
covered, not a crossing port or free root, and has opposite parity to y.
It is a pendant endpoint in the conflict path, so no cycle is formed.
Suppress y, retaining its path and any tag. The resulting B matching has
the exact hole counts stated above, namely (H_B minus {u}) union {y} when
a bridge is present, or H_B minus {u} otherwise. Its marked y is omitted
by the B cycle theorem and restored once on expansion.

Expand every suppressed edge and transferred path and delete the unique
tag. The global graph is one Hamilton u--v path preserving every original
edge. All completion edges D were deleted, all compression edges expanded,
and the tag removed; every surviving newly introduced physical edge is
short. This proves the row theorem without the old local endpoint bounds.

##### Conditional predecessor reduction, especially free targets

Let P(k-1) be the COMPLETE preceding 2k-2-hole endpoint theorem for every
short matching, every free root of either parity and every opposite-
parity target, free or covered. The following reductions require P(k-1).

For a covered target, any short Z--W hole edge can be added without
covering u or v, and P(k-1) applies. Thus the remaining reduced domain
may assume Z union W independent; root--W adjacency is still allowed.

For a free target, suppose ANY two original holes x,y form a short edge.
If xy differs from uv, adding xy leaves at least one of u,v free. Apply
P(k-1) using that remaining free endpoint as root and the other as target,
reversing the resulting path if needed. It contains M union {xy}; the
extra xy edge is short relative to M. If xy=uv, add uv, choose a different
remaining free root r (there are at least 2k-2 free holes), and any short
neighbor s of r. P(k-1) gives a Hamilton r--s path containing the added
uv. Its endpoints are opposite-parity, and r was free in the augmented
matching. Add the short rs edge to obtain a Hamilton cycle; a path with
64 vertices cannot already contain an edge joining its two endpoints.
Delete the added uv to obtain the required Hamilton u--v path through M.
The artificial uv is not an original edge because both endpoints were
originally free. No original required edge was deleted.

Consequently the free-target reduced domain may assume the ENTIRE hole
set independent. In particular mirror(u) is never an odd source hole,
so the source exception in row3 is automatically discharged there.

The complete preceding ten-hole theorem is now final PASS in
[TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), fixed SHA-256
`72c6f693b4f8bee6376edcbd132235d7985436f6ebbad8a19dade0d5326f643d`.
Thus these predecessor reductions are available unconditionally relative
to accepted imports for the twelve-hole layer. For fourteen, sixteen and
eighteen holes they remain CONDITIONAL on the corresponding preceding
complete layer. Neither the census nor the row proof proves that missing
predecessor. The cut theorem itself holds for its explicitly independent
input geometries regardless of predecessor status.

##### Exact new producer census and raw remaining domains

[HIGHER_Q5_FULL_census.cpp](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_census.cpp) is a new source, leaving the old census frozen.
It enumerates every nonzero even Z of size k-1 and every odd W of size k
nonadjacent to Z, retaining root adjacency. For each normalized odd target
v=1,7,31 it separates free/covered status. Coordinate permutations fixing
root0 normalize all opposite-parity targets to these weights1,3,5.
For free targets, any unit vertex in W is recorded as the conditional
root-adjacent-to-predecessor branch BEFORE cut tests; all remaining free
records have fully independent holes. Then all SIX actual target-oriented
cuts are tested for b-a in {0,1,2}, excluding a=b=0. Only genuinely unhit
records are written as raw original labels, with sorted Z followed by W.

The old k>=7 eligible-only shortcut is removed. Every k=6,...,9 runs the
actual cut tests and writes all six residual files, including empty files.
The program performs no matching-realizability exclusion. Each record
has 2k-1 bytes. These are hole-geometry counts, not matching counts or
automorphism-orbit counts. A hole geometry need not be realizable by a
short original matching; no such restriction is used in this exhaustive
over-domain.

| Holes | Covered residual v1/v7/v31 | Covered total | Free residual v1/v7/v31 | Free total |
|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
|12|2364029 /2632038 /2824049|7820116|0 /80622 /107984|188606|
|14|2760900 /3125851 /3365650|9252401|0 /94182 /137860|232042|
|16|725370 /834303 /912495|2472168|0 /15786 /27060|42846|
|18|22260 /27735 /30810|80805|0 /0 /0|0|

Each output JSON records the eligible count, cut-covered count,
free-root-adjacency reduction count and residual count. Their sum is
checked. All eligible counts agree exactly with the old independent-domain
census, while the k>=7 cut filtering is new. All raw file lengths equal
the stated residual count times 2k-1. These are producer consistency
checks, not a substitute for an independent census/domain audit.

The eighteen-hole free residual being empty is a conditional statement
about this reduced domain; it is NOT a full eighteen-hole theorem while
the sixteen-hole predecessor is unproved. All four layers remain open.

##### Next shared inputs and limits

The frozen raw file naming is
`HIGHER_Q5_FULL_residual_h{12,14,16,18}_v{1,7,31}_{covered,free}.bin`.
Their SHA-256 pins, source, proof and accepted import/review hashes are
recorded in the new manifest. Counts are only the initial near-balanced
filter, before lookup of existing marked rank registries, accepted T63
split, T44 and other local inputs. They must not be described as the final
number of difficult or unproved matching cases.

For example twelve-hole rows(2,1),(0,3) require marked Q5 T37 inputs:
three minority plus seven majority holes, omitting two majority holes.
Their complement has22 endpoints, so the same matching-connectivity
rank method would require1024 legal short forests rather than2048.
Actual included holes come from original Z union W and are independent.
First reuse already accepted actual marked T26/T15/T17/T63 registries
where applicable; new T37 geometries must have their own profile and
positive certificates. No unprofiled universal local input is assumed.

All new computational evidence here is producer-only pending fresh
independent review. No full12--18-hole layer or full P6 conclusion is
asserted, and no failed search is a negative certificate.


</details>


<details id="proof-higher-q5-full-reuse-proof" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_PROOF.md — Twelve-hole residual: conservative accepted-Q5 registry reuse</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_PROOF.md)。SHA-256：`9ef66ee96fd9725120f32206eb76ece116a277c84787b26064a26f6cc726a12c`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOURTEEN_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_REUSE_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_Q5_FULL_T37_APPLICATION_REVIEW.json), [TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TWELVE_HOLE_FREE_REVIEW.json)。

#### Twelve-hole residual: conservative accepted-Q5 registry reuse

2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer producer package. The theorem below is
relative to accepted local imports; the new lookup/census needs fresh
independent review. No frozen near-balanced proof, local theorem, T26/T63
input or accepted ledger was changed. Full twelve-hole and P6 remain OPEN.

##### Exact general source-transfer theorem

Let M be a short Q6 matching with twelve holes, free even root u=0 and
any opposite-parity target v, free or covered. Its other even holes Z
have size5, its odd holes W size6, and Z union W is independent. Choose
a coordinate face A containing v, with a=|Z intersect A|, b=|W intersect A|.
Either construction suffices when the actual marked B geometry is an
accepted universal local matching input in the table below:

* Even consumption: b>=1 and s=a+1-b>=0. Choose s sources S from Z
  intersect A. B minority holes are Z intersect B, majority holes are
  (W intersect B) union Y, with Y the s short source mirrors; omit Y.
* Odd consumption: t=b-a-1>=1. Choose t sources S from W intersect A
  excluding v when free and excluding the root mirror. B minority holes
  are W intersect B, majority holes are (Z intersect B) union Y; omit Y.

The selected source set must exist. This is a statement for every original
matching realizing the geometry; it is not a favorable-matching search.

##### Replay with full balanced Q5 endpoint inputs

For zero original crossings use the accepted five-direction theorem.
Otherwise let X_A,X_B be actual distinct ports and delta indicate u in A.
In even consumption, if delta=1 choose r=u and pair X_A union S into D.
If delta=0 and s>=1 choose r in S and pair X_A union (S minus {r}).
If delta=0 and s=0, shortness gives even-port surplus1; choose an even
port r and pair the rest. The completed A matching has exactly b holes
per parity with free r. Since b>=1, the accepted FULL balanced Q5 endpoint
theorem applies, with covered or free odd target v. Even sources cannot
consume v. The old b<=3 restriction served only the old endpoint import.

In odd consumption, choose r=u and pair X_A union S when delta=1.
When delta=0 the even-port surplus is t+1>0; choose an even port r and
pair (X_A minus {r}) union S. The completed A matching has exactly a+1
holes per parity with r free. The legal source exclusions retain v.
The full endpoint theorem applies for every a, extending its former
limited a<=2 input. Pairing-set parity is the original degree-counting
identity, and arbitrary long or same-parity completion edges are allowed.

Every mirror is distinct and internally B-covered: independence excludes
opposite-parity holes, a free original short mirror excludes a crossing
port, and source choice excludes u. Delete D from the A path and attach
all crossings/bridges. When u is in A the positive-crossing parity identities
make D nonempty; when u is in B it is initially unattached. The tagged uv
closure is a forest, including D-empty and target-port boundaries already
present in the accepted uniform proof. Compress the A paths.

The only B conflicts are the same-parity mirrors Y. Each has a distinct
original internally covered pendant mate of opposite parity, outside Y,
ports, root and original holes. Conflict components therefore are paths
and cannot close a cycle, even when a transferred edge joins two mirrors.
Suppress them, retaining all path data and the tag. The resulting arbitrary
B matching has holes exactly (H_B minus {u}) union Y and omissions Y.
Apply its actual accepted marked theorem. Expand all recorded paths and
delete the tag. All original edges and prescribed endpoints are restored;
D was deleted, compressed edges expanded, and the tag removed. Every
surviving new physical edge is short. This proves the theorem for free
and covered v without extrapolating the old numerical endpoint bounds.

##### Accepted marked local inputs and their precise scope

| Family code | Actual B input |
|---:|---|
|1|Complete T44: four same-parity holes, any two prescribed omissions|
|2|T63 with actual marked2/4-hole,1/2-omission split|
|3|The exact55 T26 rank marked orbits, minority2/majority6, omit2 majority|
|4|Accepted old24 T15 cores/full split plus exact15 new T15 rank orbits|
|5|T15 short augmentation at an included majority hole to complete T44|
|6|Exact10 UNFORCED T17 rank marked inputs, minority1/majority7, omit3 majority|
|7|Exact7 additional same-parity T63 rank marked inputs and their common cube images|

All their required matchings may be arbitrary complete-graph matchings,
including the long and same-parity edges created by compression. Marked
omissions are transported together with the hole geometry. T26 lookup
normalizes either minority to0 and applies every coordinate permutation.
T15/T17 normalize their singleton minority to0. T63 rank lookup uses all
common translations and coordinate permutations, including parity reversal.
T63 split is tested in the actual five coordinates after the outer cut.

The old T15 lookup is the frozen independently generated table from
TEN_HOLE_COVERED_PARTIAL_REVIEW. No unrestricted same-face shortcut is
used. Family5 adds a short edge from the minority hole to a nonomitted
included majority hole, leaving four majority holes retaining both marked
omissions; T44 then applies. That added edge is short relative to F.

The seven CONDITIONAL forced-T17 inputs are excluded here. Original M_B
lacking their same-parity obstruction is not a proof that compressed L
lacks it. Their earlier root-not-obstruction Q6 application had a specific
ten-hole/covered-target scope, which is not silently extended by this filter.

<details id="proof-hole-range-and-completion" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>HOLE_RANGE_AND_COMPLETION.md — P6 的孔数范围与完整关闭标准</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/HOLE_RANGE_AND_COMPLETION.md)。SHA-256：`398fc807faa62a79d10c687828644b2111a0929c232e85d793c7c0f576fc9b84`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json)。

#### P6 的孔数范围与完整关闭标准

日期：2026-11-01。完整 P6 尚未证明。

##### 原问题的范围

Q6 有 64 个顶点、192 条边。一个匹配 M 每条边覆盖两个不同顶点，因此孔数为 $64-2|M|$。有指定自由根 u 的实例不可能完美，所以原问题可能涉及偶数孔数 2 至 64。每条短边各覆盖一个偶点与奇点，故孔的两个奇偶类大小相等。

##### 保持根的极大补全与安全上界

固定 u，令 $G=Q_6-\{u\}$。把 M 在 G 内不断添加两端都自由的短边，直到得到按包含关系极大的匹配 L。过程有限，且 $M\subseteq L$，u 始终未覆盖。若存在包含 L 的所需 Hamilton u—v 路径，该路径也包含 M。因此只须证明 G 内所有极大匹配的结论。“极大”不是“最大基数”，不能用最大匹配替代所有极大匹配。

G 有 $192-6=186$ 条边，最大度数为 6。极大性意味着 G 的每条边都与 L 的某条边共端点，否则可以直接添加该边。对 $ab\in L$，G 中与它共端点的边数至多

$$d_G(a)+d_G(b)-1\le11.$$

这些边的集合允许重叠，但其并覆盖 G 的全部边。因此

$$186\le11|L|,\qquad |L|\ge\lceil186/11\rceil=17.$$

另一方面，G 只有 63 个顶点，所以 $|L|\le31$。于是归约后只需考虑孔数不超过 $64-2\cdot17=30$ 的极大匹配，即候选孔数 $2,4,6,\ldots,30$。这是安全范围，不声称每个候选孔数都可实现，也不声称上界最紧。

##### 什么才算关闭整个 Q6

要对 G 内每个极大匹配 L、每个自由根 u、每个与 u 异奇偶的 v，证明存在包含 L 全部边的 Hamilton u—v 路径。允许以平移固定 u=0，以坐标置换把 v 归一化为重量 1、3、5 的三个代表，但每个代表都必须覆盖全部对应匹配，而不能只检查若干模板。

解析路线必须闭合每个归约及例外分支，并验证输入定理的全部假设。穷尽计算路线必须覆盖完整域，具有独立可复核的枚举或覆盖／UNSAT 证书。随机实例成功、超时、圈存在、自由—自由端点结果都不能替代这个全称指定端点结论。

双孔或四孔结果只是该目标的子类。即使 Z18 的完整四孔证明通过审计，仍要处理不能保持根自由而补到双孔／四孔的六孔及更多孔；也可以用一条统一定理一次关闭这些剩余情况，无须机械地逐孔数分别写定理。


</details>


<details id="proof-mixed-two-hole-transfer" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>MIXED_TWO_HOLE_TRANSFER.md — Z16：目标侧异奇偶双孔的无半层转移</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/MIXED_TWO_HOLE_TRANSFER.md)。SHA-256：`08ac55101a589c331359611a4c3315322c3070d057cd17fd97e5c59e0dd1db49`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/FOUR_HOLE_SOL_HIGH_REVIEW.json)。

#### Z16：目标侧异奇偶双孔的无半层转移

日期：2026-11-01。证明草稿，待独立审计。完整 P6 未证明。

##### 命题

设 $M$ 是 $Q_6$ 短匹配，孔为 $u,z,w,t$，$u,z$ 偶、$w,t$ 奇，目标 $v$ 奇且被覆盖。设 $z$ 不与 $w,t$ 相邻。记 $h=M(v)$，$M^*=(M\setminus\{vh\})\cup\{hu\}$。沿坐标 $i$ 切分成 $A,B$，满足 $v,z\in A$、$w,t\in B$。若 $M_A^*$ 不含半层，且 $M^*$ 有至少两条跨边，则 $M$ 有 Hamilton $u$—$v$ 延拓。

依赖 N11、N12、N14。跨边允许包含唯一的长边 $hu$；最终原匹配仍全为短边。

##### 证明

记跨边端口为 $X_A,X_B$。因为 A 有两个孔，跨边数为偶数。候选 $w\oplus e_i,t\oplus e_i$ 均不等于 $z$，且为 A 内偶点。除了原根 $u$ 外，它们原来均由 $M_A$ 覆盖，因为跨面邻点是孔。收缩只改变 $u,h$ 的伙伴：若两者同在 A，新 $hu$ 内部覆盖二者；若只有一个在 A，则至多一个候选变成跨端口；若两者都在 B，候选覆盖不变。因此至少一个候选仍由 $M_A^*$ 覆盖。

交换 $w,t$ 后令 $b=w\oplus e_i$ 是选中的候选，记 $k=M_A^*(b)$。令 $F=M_A^*\setminus\{bk\}$。它不含半层，且在 $A\setminus\{v,b\}$ 内的自由集恰为

$$Y=X_A\cup\{z,k\}.$$

这些点互异，$|Y|\ge4$ 为偶数。由于 $v,b$ 异奇偶，N12 给出 $Y$ 上配对 $W$，使 $F\cup W$ 无半层。记 $a=W(k)$，则 $a\in X_A\cup\{z\}$；令 $D=W\setminus\{ak\}$。于是 $L_A=M_A^*\cup D$ 恰有孔 $v,a$，且 N11 的压缩恰为 $F\cup W$。

N11 给出包含 $L_A$、覆盖 $A\setminus\{v\}$ 的 $a$—$b$ 路径。删除 $D$，得到非平凡顶点不交路径族，端点集恰为 $X_A\cup\{z,b\}$。$D$ 不接触两个端点 $a,b$，故无孤立点；$a=z$ 的情形也满足同一端点集公式。

给 $X_A$ 接回真实跨边，另加短边 $bw$、$zy$，其中 $y=z\oplus e_i\in B$。由于 $z$ 不邻接 $w,t$，$y$ 不等于 $w,t$；其为奇点，不等于偶点 $u,h$。原来 $y$ 不是孔，跨面邻点 $z$ 是孔，故 $y$ 由原 $M_B$ 覆盖，收缩后仍由 $M_B^*$ 覆盖。

将所得路径族缩成匹配 $R$，其覆盖集恰为 $X_B\cup\{w,y\}$。它与 $M_B^*$ 的唯一覆盖冲突是 $y$。令 $r=M_B^*(y)$、$s=R(y)$，则 $s\in X_B\cup\{w\}$。$y,r$ 原被 $M_B^*$ 覆盖，$s,t$ 不被覆盖，所以四点不同。定义

$$L_B=(M_B^*\setminus\{yr\})\cup(R\setminus\{ys\})\cup\{rs\}.$$

该匹配恰有同奇偶的两个孔 $y,t$（均奇）。N14 给出包含 $L_B$、覆盖 $B\setminus\{y\}$ 的圈。把 $rs$ 展开为 $r$—$y$ 及从 $y$ 到 $s$ 的对应转移路径，其余 $R$ 边也全部展开。$y$ 恢复一次，各 A 内点恢复一次，得到覆盖 $Q_6\setminus\{v\}$ 并包含 $M^*$ 的圈。

最后删 $hu$、在 $h$ 端接回 $hv$。原匹配全部恢复，所有辅助边消去或展开，新增边均短，得到所需 Hamilton 路径。证毕。


</details>


<details id="proof-near-perfect-extension" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>NEAR_PERFECT_EXTENSION.md — 近完美补全类的指定端点延拓</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/NEAR_PERFECT_EXTENSION.md)。SHA-256：`eefb31b2c708fdd2c2b9ebe9e86b43a83bfdecc91fd59f737782d6bdbed02257`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json)。

#### 近完美补全类的指定端点延拓

日期：2026-11-01。目标是推进 P6，不改变完整 P6 的全称范围。本稿作为从已引定理推导的结果，不声明文献新颖性。

##### 状态与依赖

**PROVABLE AS STATED（相对于列明的已知定理）**。独立同系列模型审读未发现实质性错误，接受状态为 provisional；见 NEAR_PERFECT_REVIEW.md，不代表形式化或跨系列验收。只使用用户 `2501.19029v1.pdf` 的 Theorem 1（Fink）、Theorem 6（Gregor–Novotný–Škrekovski，n≥5）和 Theorem 8（至多五方向匹配的端点路径刻画），以及 CORE_DERIVATION.md 的 D2/D3。全体 P6 仍未证明。

Theorem 6 的准确输入为 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配 P，异奇偶端点 x,y，xy不属于P。其结论是：存在包含 P、其余边全在 Q_n 的哈密顿 x–y 路径，当且仅当
R=(P\{xa,yb})∪{ab} 不含半层，其中 a=P(x)、b=P(y)。

##### 引理 N0：一般完美匹配的短边方向限制

设 P 为 B(Q_n) 的任意完美匹配，x,y异奇偶，xy不属于P。记 a=P(x)、b=P(y)，R=(P\{xa,yb})∪{ab}。若R包含一个方向i的半层，那么P中的全部立方体边至多使用三个方向。

**证明。** 用下文N1相同的S,T记半层端点集及其补集，两者的诱导立方体边都仅沿i方向，且x,y属于T。如果ab不属于半层，则半层包含于P，S全部被内部匹配，因此P的所有短边都沿i。如果ab属于半层，则半层去掉ab包含于P；只有xa,yb可能跨越S,T。P的其余短边均在S或T内、沿i方向，xa,yb即使都是短边也至多引入两个额外方向。证毕。

本引理允许P包含任意多条长边。N3只需要这个短证明。下面N1保留为单长边情形的更精确结构说明。

##### 引理 N1：单条长边时的半层刚性

设 P 为 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配，恰有一条非立方体边 f，其余边均为立方体边。给定异奇偶 x,y，xy不属于P，记 a=P(x)、b=P(y)，R=(P\{xa,yb})∪{ab}。如果 R 含半层，则 f 长度为3，并且 P\{f} 至多使用三个坐标方向。

**证明。** 设半层 H 的方向为 i，端点集为
$$S=\{z:\sum_{k\ne i}z_k=\epsilon\pmod2\},\qquad T=V(Q_n)\setminus S.$$
Q_n[S] 和 Q_n[T] 都仅含方向 i 的边。R 不覆盖 x,y，所以 x,y属于T。

**第一种情况：ab不属于H。** 此时 H⊆P，因而 P 在 T 上也是完美匹配，其唯一长边 f 的两个端点 c,d 均在 T。T 的其余顶点仅能沿方向 i 匹配。于是 c 的 i 邻点必须是 d；否则 c 的 i 邻点没有可用的短边匹配伙伴。因此 f 是方向 i 的短边，矛盾。

**第二种情况：ab属于H。** 此时 b=a⊕e_i，且 H\{ab}⊆P。S 中仅 a,b 不由这些半层边匹配，它们分别匹配到 x,y∈T。

若 f 是 xa 或 yb，则 T\{x,y} 全由方向 i 的短边匹配。故 y=x⊕e_i。结合 b=a⊕e_i 得 d(x,a)=d(y,b)，不能恰有其中一条是长边，矛盾。

所以 f 不属于 {xa,yb}，并完全位于 T\{x,y}。边 xa,yb 都是短边，可写
$$x=a\oplus e_j,\quad y=b\oplus e_k,\qquad j,k\ne i.$$
令 f=cd。T\{x,y,c,d} 全由方向 i 匹配，故四点集 {x,y,c,d} 在翻转 i 下封闭。这四点互异。如果 x⊕e_i=y，那么 c⊕e_i=d，使 f 成短边，矛盾。因此交换 c,d 的名称后，必有
$$c=x\oplus e_i=b\oplus e_j,\qquad d=y\oplus e_i=a\oplus e_k.$$
若 j=k，则 y=x⊕e_i，已被排除。所以 i,j,k 两两不同，f 的两个端点恰在这三个坐标不同，d(c,d)=3。P 的短边除 xa,yb 之外全部沿方向 i；因此只使用 i,j,k 三方向。证毕。

##### 引理 N2：包含完美匹配的路径必交替

若一条包含偶数个顶点的哈密顿路径包含完美匹配 P，那么沿路径编号0,1,…，P 的边恰连接位置(0,1),(2,3),…。

**证明。** 位置0的顶点只有一条路径边，该边必须是它的P边，故位置0与1由P匹配。位置2的P伙伴不能是已被匹配的位置1，只能是位置3。依次归纳即可。证毕。

若所有边连接二部图两侧，并从与 u 同奇偶的端点开始，则 P 中连接 u 到异奇偶 w 的边沿路径必按 u→w 的方向出现。

##### 定理 N3：近完美补全足以解决所有指定终点

设 n≥5，M⊆E(Q_n) 是匹配，u不被M覆盖。假设存在立方体匹配 L⊇M，恰好不覆盖两个顶点 u,w。那么对每个与u异奇偶的v，都存在包含M的哈密顿 u–v 路径。

**证明。** 二部图两侧各有2^(n−1)点，每条匹配边覆盖两侧各一点，所以u,w异奇偶。

1. 若 v=w，则由 D3（把人工边uw加入L，用Fink圈定理后删去它）得结论。
2. 若 d(u,w)=1，则 L∪{uw} 是短边完美匹配。M 可补成完美匹配，应用已证 D2。
3. 以下 v≠w 且 d(u,w)≥3。若 L 至多使用三个方向，则 M 也至多使用三个方向。应用原文 Theorem 8：u 未被 M 覆盖排除 C1、C2、C3，得到目标路径。
4. 以下 L 使用至少四个方向。令 P=L∪{uw}，这是 B(Q_n) 的完美匹配，唯一长边为 uw。选一个 w 的立方体邻点 x，要求 x≠P(v)。这样的点存在：w 有n个邻点，至多一个被上述条件排除。由于uw不是短边，x≠u；又x与u同奇偶，v与u异奇偶，故x≠v。于是 xv不属于P。
5. 对 P 和端点 x,v 应用 Theorem 6。若压缩匹配含半层，N0 将推出 L 只使用至多三个方向，与第4步矛盾。因此存在包含 P 的哈密顿 x–v 路径 K，其余边全为立方体边。
6. 从 x 出发，N2 保证人工边 uw 的定向为 u→w。因此删去 uw 后得到两条顶点不交且覆盖全图的路径 K[x,u] 和 K[w,v]。这两条路径所有边均为立方体边，并仍包含 L 的全部边。
7. 将第一条路径反向，再用立方体边 xw 接到第二条：
$$u\ \leadsto\ x\;—\;w\ \leadsto\ v.$$
x、w 原来属于不同分量，所以 xw 不可能已在删边后的路径中。连接后每个顶点恰出现一次，端点为 u,v，保留全部 L⊇M。证毕。

人工边在第6步被明确删除；第7步只添加已选的立方体边。因此没有把含长边路径冒充立方体路径。

##### 推论及剩余范围

- P6 的所有31边匹配均被 N3 覆盖；所有可在不覆盖u的前提下补成31边的匹配也被覆盖。
- 在 Q6−V(M) 上作二部图最大匹配。若 M 可补成完美匹配，由 D2 解决；否则残余匹配能覆盖除u及某个w外的所有顶点时，由 N3 解决。
- 不能由“|M|≤30”推出可近完美补全；极大匹配可能留下更多互不相邻的未覆盖点。
- 全部六方向问题尚剩无法在保留M的前提下进行上述补全的匹配，需要继续处理这些残余图的匹配缺陷。

##### 推论 N4：剩余问题的精确 Hall 障碍

设 F=V(Q_n)\V(M)，E 为 F 中与 u 同奇偶的点，O 为 F 中与 u 异奇偶的点。由于 M 是二部图匹配，|E|=|O|。对 S⊆E\{u}，令 N_F(S) 为 S 在残余诱导图 Q_n[F] 中的邻点集。

**等价判据。** 存在某个 w∈O，使 M 可以补成恰不覆盖 u,w 的短边匹配，当且仅当
$$|N_F(S)|\ge |S|\quad\text{对每个 }S\subseteq E\setminus\{u\}\text{成立。}$$

**证明。** 补全边必须全部在 F 内且不覆盖 u，因此恰需在二部图 (E\{u},O) 中找到饱和左侧的匹配。Hall定理给出所述充要条件。左右大小差1，饱和左侧后右侧恰剩一个w。证毕。

于是未被 N3 解决的实例都必须具有一个具体的非空集 S⊆E\{u}，满足 |N_F(S)|<|S|。这是补全路线的障碍证书，不是哈密顿路径不存在的证书。

特别地，对 Q6 的30边匹配，若未覆盖点为 {u,z,w,t}，其中 u,z 同奇偶，则 N3 适用当且仅当 z 与 w,t 中至少一个相邻。该补全路线尚不能处理 d(z,w),d(z,t) 均大于1的情形。其余已知充分条件仍可能适用。

##### 核验结果与来源

verify_near_perfect.py 对固定长边0—7的所有短边补全及所有异奇偶指定端点检查 N1：Q3 为2个补全、24个端点对；Q4 为48个补全、2688个端点对。所有半层障碍均符合N1的方向限制。这是小维数反例排查，不是六维全枚举。

construct_near_perfect.py 对16个六维31边匹配执行证明中的实际构造，分别让两未覆盖点距离为3或5；先找到允许唯一人工长边的中间路径，再按N2删边并拼接。最终16条路径全为立方体边，均通过全排列、端点和匹配包含检查。

原1152个六维样本依次按已知五方向、D2、N3、D5分类，数量为512、32、32、72，其余504个仍无这些引理的统一证明。此前剩余535个，故本轮新闭合31个此前只有逐实例证书的端点实例。这些数字仅说明原样本覆盖范围，不是全空间证明比例。

Theorem 6 的原始来源已核对：[Gregor–Novotný–Škrekovski (2018), Theorem 2](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v25i2p56/pdf/)。它允许完美匹配来自 B(Q_n)，并要求延拓添加的边来自 Q_n；没有把“短边完美匹配”条件误套到人工长边情形。

与之同名检索结果中的 [Fink–Mütze 长圈论文](https://tmuetze.de/papers/match.pdf) 是另一篇论文，其Theorem 9再次陈述这个输入定理；不能与用户的 Fink–Hotmar 五方向论文混为一篇。有限检索未认证本推论的新颖性。

##### 单跨边实验的地位

single_bridge_probe.py 对固定种子的96个六维单跨边、错误奇偶实例搜索，匹配大小27—30；全部找到恰用三条跨边的合法路径。它包含终点等于强制跨边另一端的边界例。每条见证已检查全顶点覆盖、端点、邻接、匹配包含关系。

这些实例不是全空间枚举；N1—N3 的证明不依赖实验。相反，N3 给出了独立于三跨边配对选择的统一证明入口。


</details>

<summary>Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md — Four-dimensional core certificates and an unconditional A4 split class</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md)。SHA-256：`2925b389034346000a9bd38979e451b7fac9ff4cf700600b6ea868cfdf384389`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[A4_SINGLE_GEOMETRY_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A4_SINGLE_GEOMETRY_REVIEW.json), [A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A6_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json), [A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/A8_PARTIAL_REVIEW.json), [CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.json), [EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [Q4_CORE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q4_CORE_REVIEW.json), [Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_REVIEW.json), [Q5_T63_COMPLETE_SPLIT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/Q5_T63_COMPLETE_SPLIT_REVIEW.json), [SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/SIX_HOLE_CLOSURE_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json), [T15_ALTERNATIVE_GROUP_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_ALTERNATIVE_GROUP_REVIEW.json), [T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE1_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE1_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE23_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE23_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE24_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE24_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE27_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE27_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE4_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE4_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE8_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_REVIEW.json), [TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/TEN_COVERED_Q5_ENDPOINT_REVIEW.json)。

#### Four-dimensional core certificates and an unconditional A4 split class

Date: 2026-11-01. Status: finite positive certificates plus mathematical
reductions; independent review pending at initial writing. Full Q5 A4 and P6
remain unproved. None of the claims below assumes Q5 A4 or P6.

##### Exact core claims

**N14_4.** Every matching of $K(Q_4)$ with exactly two same-parity holes has a
cycle through all vertices except either prescribed hole, preserving every
matching edge and using only short new edges.

**A4_4.** Every matching of $K(Q_4)$ with exactly four holes of parity counts
3 and 1 has a cycle through all vertices except any prescribed majority-parity
hole, preserving every matching edge and using only short new edges.

All matching edges may be arbitrary pairs of vertices, including same-parity
long edges. A short edge changes exactly one coordinate. Hamilton circles in
these statements have 15 vertices and may include the prescribed long edges.

##### Finite proof of N14_4

Translate the prescribed forbidden vertex to 0 by bitwise XOR. The other
hole is a distinct even vertex, at Hamming distance two or four. A coordinate
permutation takes it to 3 or 15 respectively. These automorphisms preserve
short edges, long prescribed edges, and the extension question.

For each representative, all perfect matchings of the other 14 vertices are
covered by a certificate file: [q4_two_hole_3.bin](research/six_directions/q4_two_hole_3.bin) or [q4_two_hole_15.bin](research/six_directions/q4_two_hole_15.bin).
There are $13!!=135135$ such matchings in each representative. Every record
contains the entire mate array and a 15-vertex cycle witnessing the assertion.

The independent checker [verify_q4_extension_certificates.py](research/six_directions/verify_q4_extension_certificates.py) checks:

1. The mate array is an involution without fixed points on exactly the
   14 prescribed covered vertices, with precisely the two prescribed holes.
2. The cycle contains all 15 required vertices exactly once, includes every
   matching edge, and has only short edges outside the matching.
3. No perfect matching is omitted or repeated. To certify this without
   depending on the generator's recursion order, compute its rank as follows.
   Remove the least remaining vertex $x$. If its mate has index $i$, starting
   at zero, in the increasing list of other remaining vertices, its rank is
   $i(2k-3)!!$ plus the recursively computed rank of the remaining matching,
   where $2k$ is the number of vertices before removing this pair. Empty
   rank is zero and $(-1)!!=1$. There are $2k-1$ disjoint equal-size blocks,
   so induction proves a bijection with $0,\ldots,(2k-1)!!-1$.
   The checker marks all these ranks and requires each exactly once.

All 270270 records pass. Thus, modulo the transparent finite certificate
verification, the two representatives and symmetry prove N14_4 completely.
This proof does not import the five-dimensional version of N14.

##### Finite proof of A4_4

Translate the minority-parity hole to $a=0$. Let $v$ be the forbidden odd
hole and $b,t$ the two remaining odd holes. If $a$ is adjacent to $b$ or $t$,
add that short edge. The resulting matching has two same-parity holes, and
N14_4 proves the required 15-cycle avoiding $v$.

Otherwise $b,t$ are distinct weight-three vertices in $Q_4$. Permuting
coordinates makes their unordered pair $\{7,11\}$. Their supports share
coordinates 0 and 1 and differ in coordinates 2 and 3. The permutations of
the two common coordinates and of the two differing coordinates preserve
this unordered pair. The six possible forbidden odd vertices have exactly
three orbits:

$$\{1,2\},\qquad \{4,8\},\qquad \{13,14\}.$$

Choose representatives $v=1,4,13$. For each, the other 12 vertices have
$11!!=10395$ perfect matchings. Files [q4_four_hole_1.bin](research/six_directions/q4_four_hole_1.bin),
[q4_four_hole_4.bin](research/six_directions/q4_four_hole_4.bin), [q4_four_hole_13.bin](research/six_directions/q4_four_hole_13.bin) contain a 15-cycle certificate
for each one. The same independent checker validates the matching, cycle,
and full rank coverage. All 31185 records pass. Together with the adjacent
branch, this proves A4_4.

The five files total 301455 certificates. The search programs' positive
outputs are independently checked; neither a numerical solver's feasibility
judgment nor the completeness of its search is needed for acceptance.

##### Derived four-dimensional path inputs

**N10_4.** Let $L$ be an arbitrary matching of $K(Q_4)$ with exactly two holes
$r,s$. For any $y\ne r$ with $p(y)=p(s)$ there is a Hamilton $r$--$y$ path
containing $L$, with all newly added edges short.

If $y$ is free, then $y=s$. Add $rs$ to make a perfect matching of $K(Q_4)$,
apply Fink's perfect-matching extension theorem, and delete $rs$ from the
resulting Hamilton circle. It yields the stated path. This is the only
external extension theorem needed here; it permits arbitrary original edges
of the complete graph and adds short edges.

If $y$ is covered, let $k=L(y)$. The matching
$L'=L-yk+kr$ has same-parity holes $y,s$. N14_4 supplies a 15-cycle avoiding
$y$ and containing $L'$. Delete $kr$ to obtain an $r$--$k$ path on all vertices
except $y$, and append the original edge $ky$. The path now contains all of
$L$ and only short edges outside $L$. The appended edge may be long, but is
an original required matching edge.

**NC_4.** If the two holes of $L$ have opposite parity, $L$ extends to a
Hamilton circle of $K(Q_4)$ with only short new edges. Choose any short
neighbor $y$ of the free root $r$, use N10_4, and close the Hamilton path by
$ry$. Such a spanning path on 16 vertices cannot already contain the edge
between its two endpoints, so this produces a simple circle.

**K4_4.** A balanced four-hole matching of $K(Q_4)$ has a Hamilton path from
any free root $r$ to any vertex $y$ of the opposite parity, preserving the
matching and adding only short edges. If $y$ is free, add the auxiliary
edge $ry$; the remaining holes are opposite, so NC_4 gives a full circle;
delete $ry$. If $y$ is covered with mate $k$, swap $yk$ to $kr$. The four
holes now have counts 3 and 1, with $y$ in the majority. Apply A4_4 avoiding
$y$, delete $kr$, append the original $ky$. Both constructions meet the
specified endpoints and restore all original matching edges.

##### S4D: a Q5 A4 class closed without assuming A4

Let $F$ be an arbitrary $K(Q_5)$ matching with holes $a,b,t,v$, where $a$
has the minority parity and the desired circle must avoid $v$. Suppose a
coordinate cut has on one side $A$ exactly the holes $v,b$, on the other
side $B$ exactly $a,t$, and at least one original $F$ edge crosses the cut.
Then the Q5 A4 conclusion holds for $F$.

Let the crossing matching be $C$, with endpoint sets $X_A,X_B$. Since
$|A|=16$ and exactly two vertices of $A$ are globally free, the equality
$2|F_A|+|C|=14$ makes $|C|$ even. Thus it is at least two. Choose any
perfect matching $D$ of the complete graph on $X_A$. Then $F_A\cup D$ has
the same-parity holes $v,b$. N14_4 supplies a cycle on $A\setminus\{v\}$
containing it, with all other edges short.

Delete $D$. Because $D$ is a nonempty matching in a simple circle, the result
is a disjoint family of nontrivial paths, with endpoints exactly $X_A$.
Attach each corresponding original crossing edge of $C$. The paths now
have endpoints $X_B$, disjoint interiors in $A\setminus\{v\}$, and together
cover that entire side. Replace each by a formal edge to get a matching $R$
on $X_B$. No restriction on the length or parity of edges in $C$ or $R$
is imposed; edges of $C$ are original required edges, not new short edges.

The matching $F_B\cup R$ of $K(B)$ has precisely the opposite-parity holes
$a,t$. NC_4 supplies its full Hamilton circle. Expand every $R$ edge into
its corresponding path. This gives a single circle through
$V(Q_5)\setminus\{v\}$, containing $F$ and with every edge outside $F$ short.
All artificial edges $D,R$ have disappeared. This proves S4D.

##### G4D: a whole hole-geometry family, with no matching restriction

Normalize $a=0$. If both masks

$$v\mathbin{\&}b\mathbin{\&}\neg t\ne0,
\qquad v\mathbin{\&}t\mathbin{\&}\neg b\ne0$$

are nonzero (all masks restricted to the five cube coordinates), then every
matching with these holes satisfies Q5 A4.

Choose a coordinate $i$ from the first mask and $j$ from the second. The
four holes have distinct $(i,j)$ patterns: $a:00$, $b:10$, $t:01$, $v:11$.
If any matching edge crosses either coordinate cut, that cut has the S4D
hole split, so S4D applies. If no edge crosses either cut, all matching
edges lie within the four 8-vertex $Q_3$ cells. Each cell has exactly one
hole and hence seven covered vertices, impossible for an internal matching.
Therefore at least one cut has crossings, proving the claim.

For normalized residual Q5 geometries ($a=0$, $b,t$ nonadjacent to $a$,
unordered $b,t$, and distinct forbidden odd $v$), there are 770 choices.
Exactly 255 have both masks nonzero, 350 only one, and 165 neither. These
are labeled geometric counts, not isomorphism counts or matching counts.
G4D closes all matchings in the first class. S4D can also close instances in
the one-mask class when a corresponding cut actually has a crossing edge.

##### Remaining obligations

The four-dimensional input A4_4 does not by itself prove five-dimensional
A4. The complete remaining transfer for hole configurations outside G4D,
including zero-crossing cases, is not supplied here. A4_4 and K4_4 are now
available for that research; they must not be invoked with an unverified
dimension or endpoint condition. The unconditional full six-hole P6 result
and all remaining 8--18-hole obligations remain open.


</details>
