For occupied mode, every negative output is $L=F_B\cup Q$. Enumerate each $m$-edge subset $J\subseteq L$ and set $F_B=J$, $Q=L-J$.

For internal mode, choose every oriented edge $kq$ of $L$ and every $(m-1)$-edge subset $J\subseteq L-\{kq\}$. Set

$$F_B=J\cup\{zk\},\qquad R_B=(L-J-\{kq\})\cup\{zq\}.$$

These are both directions of the inverses in Step 1. For a fixed actual $F_B$, the resulting family contains all possible negative boundary pairings. If $F_B$ does not occur in the inverse list, it has no negative output. No restriction on its edge lengths or on any A matching is used. The arbitrary crossing bijection only relabels boundary vertices and preserves connectedness.

[r3_boundary_blocking_3_1.json](research/six_directions/r3_boundary_blocking_3_1.json) and [r3_boundary_blocking_15_1.json](research/six_directions/r3_boundary_blocking_15_1.json) save these complete families and explicit blocking pairings. [verify_t15_core8_blockers.py](research/six_directions/verify_t15_core8_blockers.py) independently rebuilds every family from the raw negative tables, checks exact set equality, checks all matching supports, and uses graph traversal to verify that each saved blocker has disconnected union with every forbidden output. Its output is [t15_core8_blockers_verification.json](research/six_directions/t15_core8_blockers_verification.json).

For bridge $3$, the complete family counts in internal/occupied modes are $312/43$ at $c=5$, $264/52$ at $c=7$, $100/33$ at $c=9$, $12/10$ at $c=11$, and occupied $1$ at $c=13$. All have explicit blockers except one occupied $c=5$ family.

For bridge $15$, the corresponding counts are $1080/146$, $856/180$, $240/107$, $12/24$, and occupied $1$. All have explicit blockers except two occupied $c=5$ families. There is no internal mode at $c=13$.

Pull the applicable blocker back through $C$ and use it as $D$ in internal mode, or as $D'$ in occupied mode. Every forbidden output has disconnected union with it, whereas Step 1 supplies an output with connected union. Hence the supplied output is positive. This proves every $c\ge7$ case and every $c=5$ input with an internal bridge. For $c=5$ with both bridges occupied, the two null-family sets have exactly one common matching:

$$J=\{(2,4),(5,6),(9,11),(10,13)\}.$$

Its port set is $S=\{3,8,12,14,15\}$. This intersection is verified exactly, not inferred from a failed blocker search. Every other $c=5$ input has a blocker on at least one bridge. The remaining $F_B=J$ inputs are handled in Step 5.

###### Step 3. Small-crossing spectra, including occupied mirrors

For $c=3$, each bridge has four A endpoints and three possible endpoint pairings. At least two are realizable: if only $R_0$ were realizable, choose $D=R_0$ in Step 1; its two doubled edges would give two connected components, contradicting connectedness. For $c=1$ the sole two-endpoint pairing is realizable by N14.

For a fixed B input and crossing bijection, transport A ports to their B partners and the bridge endpoint to $z_B$. Add these compressed edges to $F_B$ as a multigraph. Reject a self-loop or any closed component. Otherwise trace the paths between degree-one endpoints and compress them to $L$, testing it against the balanced table. This defines B-admissibility on the same original A endpoint pairings. In particular, at an occupied mirror two endpoint labels become the same B vertex; the graph test, rather than an assumption of distinct boundary labels, handles this. For occupied $c=1$ the sole pairing can form a loop and is then rejected.

[verify_t15_core8_B.cpp](research/six_directions/verify_t15_core8_B.cpp) independently traces this multigraph and extracts negative sets from the thirteen audited raw tables and their coordinate images. It checks all $135135$ one-crossing B inputs, and all $\binom{13}{3}9!!\cdot3!=1621620$ three-crossing B/bijection inputs. Its full histograms equal the saved producer histograms.

At $c=1$, exactly twenty-two B inputs have neither bridge admissible. At $c=3$, exactly ten B partial matchings, each with all six bijections, have zero admissible pairing on both bridges; every other B/bijection input has at least two admissible pairings on some bridge. Its two-of-three admissible set intersects the at-least-two realizable A set, closing that input by Step 1.

The ten exceptional B partial matchings are exactly

$$F_B=J\cup\{e\},\qquad e\in\binom{S}{2},$$

with ports $S-V(e)$. This equality is checked directly from the complete independent exception list. It also identifies the relation between the $c=3$ and $c=5$ residuals, without assuming that proving one automatically proves the other.

###### Step 4. Exact residual input domains

The saved inputs are [t15_core8_c1_B_inputs.txt](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c1_B_inputs.txt), [t15_core8_c3_B_inputs.txt](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c3_B_inputs.txt), and [t15_core8_c5_B_inputs.txt](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c5_B_inputs.txt). Each begins with its number of B cases; each row contains its $c$ ports and its $(13-c)/2$ internal edges. For $c=1,3$ the lists equal the independently regenerated exceptions, with no duplicate B input. For $c=5$ the sole row is $J$ with ports $S$.

For each fixed B case, the A side has

$$\binom{13}{c}(12-c)!!$$

partial matchings, and there are exactly $c!$ crossing bijections. Consequently the complete residual domains have sizes:

| $c$ | B cases | A partial matchings | Bijections | Full inputs |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1|22|135135|1|2972970|
|3|10|270270|6|16216200|
|5|1|135135|120|16216200|

These are complete domains, with every original internal pairing and arbitrary crossing partner represented. They total $35405370$ original matchings.

###### Step 5. Positive certificates and independent coverage verification

[t15_core8_residual.cpp](research/six_directions/t15_core8_residual.cpp) constructs one explicit positive cycle for each residual input. It treats each original matching edge as an indivisible block and the four retained holes as singleton blocks. It joins these blocks only by short edges. Precomputed bitsets and a memo table accelerate the search; the proof uses only the saved positive cycles.

Each certificate record is exactly 56 bytes: thirteen original matching edges, followed by thirty cycle vertices. The three binary files are [t15_core8_c1_residual.bin](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c1_residual.bin), [t15_core8_c3_residual.bin](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c3_residual.bin), and [t15_core8_c5_residual.bin](research/six_directions/t15_core8_c5_residual.bin).

The separate verifier [verify_t15_core8_residual.cpp](research/six_directions/verify_t15_core8_residual.cpp) performs no search and does not reproduce the producer's enumeration order. From each record it validates that the required edges form a matching covering exactly $Q_5-H$, with the prescribed B case and exactly $c$ crossings. It computes an independent dense input index: the A port subset has a combinadic rank, the remaining A perfect matching is ranked recursively by the partner of its least unused vertex, and the crossing bijection has a permutation rank. Combining these ranks with the B case index gives a bijection onto the domain in Step 4. A bitmap rejects repeated indices; exact record count and an entirely filled bitmap prove no omission.

For each record the verifier also checks thirty distinct cycle vertices with support exactly $Q_5-\{1,2\}$, all thirteen original edges present, and Hamming distance one for every other edge. It checks exact EOF with no incomplete or trailing record. The three verification reports are `t15_core8_c<c>_residual_verification.json`.

All $35405370$ residual inputs have positive certificates, with zero UNKNOWN and zero exhausted inputs. Their exact byte sizes are $166486320$, $908107200$, and $908107200$, respectively, totaling $1982700720$ bytes. Counts, file sizes and SHA256 hashes are recorded in [T15_CORE8_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE8_FULL_CLOSURE_VERIFICATION.json) by the aggregate checker. No finite node cap contributes a negative or universal assertion: each accepted input has its own fully checked positive cycle.

###### Step 6. Conclusion

Step 2 closes all larger crossing counts except the single five-port B skeleton, which Step 5 closes. Steps 3--5 close every one- and three-crossing input. These cases exhaust every possible odd crossing count. Undo the global coordinate swap and transport by arbitrary cube automorphisms to obtain the original marked claim. All original edges survive and all new edges are short. ∎

##### Reproduction

From this directory, compile with `g++ -O3 -std=c++17`; `-march=native` is optional for the producer. Run the producer as `t15_core8_residual.exe <c> t15_core8_c<c>_B_inputs.txt t15_core8_c<c>_residual.bin t15_core8_c<c>_residual_failures.txt` for $c=1,3,5$, saving its JSON stdout. Run the verifier as `verify_t15_core8_residual.exe <c> t15_core8_c<c>_B_inputs.txt t15_core8_c<c>_residual.bin`, saving each verification JSON. Run [verify_t15_core8_B.exe](research/six_directions/verify_t15_core8_B.exe) for the B spectra, `python verify_t15_core8_blockers.py` for all inverse blockers, and `python verify_t15_core8_full_closure.py` for the aggregate package.

Initial bounded pilots checked $10000$ inputs in each residual family, all positive. After bitset optimization a $100000$-input three-crossing pilot took about 1.55 seconds on the local environment; full enumeration was chosen using this measured cost, rather than an unbounded blind run. Pilot data are not used to establish universal coverage.

##### Corrections or Missing Assumptions

None beyond the explicitly retained N14 and audited balanced-table imports. The ten three-crossing B exceptions and the common five-crossing B exception are handled as full positive-certificate domains, not discarded because both bridges fail.

##### Open Risks

A fresh independent overall proof audit is required before integrating this one core into parent counts. This candidate package does not establish the other T15 cores, full T15, the complete eight-hole layer, or P6. Previously audited core23 files and global proof status were not changed.


</details>


<details id="proof-t15-edge-prescription-reduction" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T15_EDGE_PRESCRIPTION_REDUCTION.md — An alternative T15 route through one optional edge in an A4 cycle</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T15_EDGE_PRESCRIPTION_REDUCTION.md)。SHA-256：`afd094ab2235517b1514bb9b8c439602cb74dcad572a0e7a8e0b1c4504314e8a`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json)。

#### An alternative T15 route through one optional edge in an A4 cycle

Date: 2026-11-01. New conditional reduction, independent review pending.
The edge-prescription obligation below is UNPROVED. This document does
not close T15 or any remaining Q6 endpoint instance.

##### Exact input and a geometric choice that always exists

Let F be a Q5 T15 input, with minority hole a, forbidden majority holes
x,y, and three other majority holes B={b,c,d}. Two distinct vertices of
one parity in Q5 have distance two or four. At most two majority vertices
are at distance four from BOTH x and y.

To prove this, translate x to 0. If y has weight two, a vertex z of weight
four has distance four from y exactly when its support contains one of
the two y coordinates and all three other coordinates: two choices.
If y has weight four, two four-element subsets of a five-element set
intersect in at least three coordinates, so no weight-four z has distance
four from y. Consequently among the three vertices of B, one has distance
two from at least one of x,y.

Exchange the names of the forbidden vertices if necessary and select
z in B with d(y,z)=2. There are exactly two common short neighbors p,q
of y and z, both of minority parity.

##### A sufficient prescription

Adjoin the auxiliary same-parity edge yz to F, obtaining L=F+yz.
Its four holes are a, x, and the two members of B other than z. Thus L
is an A4 input and x is its forbidden majority hole. The established A4
theorem supplies a 31-cycle on Q5-x containing L with short new edges.
What it does NOT guarantee is the following extra condition:

    There exists such a cycle C with yp or yq as an edge.

If this prescription holds, say yp is present, y has exactly the two
cycle edges yz and yp. Delete y and replace the two-edge segment p-y-z
by the short edge pz. The result is a single 30-cycle on Q5-{x,y}.
It retains every edge of F because y,z were original holes, and its only
new replacement edge pz is short. The artificial yz has disappeared.
Thus it proves precisely the T15 conclusion.

For the preprocessed T15 inputs, a is nonadjacent to every member of B,
so neither common neighbor p,q equals a. This is not needed for the
cycle deletion argument, but matters if a later proof uses coverage of
the prescribed-edge endpoints.

##### Remaining quantified obligation

A sufficient global lemma would assert the edge prescription for every
A4 matching L with a specified required same-majority-parity distance-two
edge yz and forbidden majority hole x. That is a stronger demand than
the existing A4 theorem and is not assumed true here.

An alternative, weaker sufficient demand is: for every original T15 F,
there exists at least one ordered choice of forbidden endpoint y and
nonforbidden hole z at distance two for which the prescription holds.
The geometry above proves that eligible pairs exist, but not that their
short common-neighbor edges can occur in an A4 extension. The latter
quantifier is the exact unproved step in this alternative route.

This route may handle several of the 23 orbit cores at once. It is
independent of the earlier (2,0) EP0 condition: that condition concerns
a near-perfect local Hamilton path, whereas the present one concerns
an A4 avoided cycle and a required same-parity edge.


</details>


<details id="proof-t15-prescription-analysis" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T15_PRESCRIPTION_ANALYSIS.md — T15 prescription analysis: exact equivalence and universal factors</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T15_PRESCRIPTION_ANALYSIS.md)。SHA-256：`44039b1a19d426f430455cb42011fc55849e09cfb0bb34fba7e719ad2ec47aaf`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json)。

#### T15 prescription analysis: exact equivalence and universal factors

Date: 2026-11-01. Local proof package; no project-wide status is changed.

##### Claim

The original T15 statement remains: for every matching $F$ of $K(Q_5)$
with holes $\{a,x,y\}\cup B$, where $a$ is even and $x,y$ and the three
members of $B$ are odd, there is a cycle on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ containing $F$
and having only short edges outside $F$. Original matching edges may have
arbitrary length and parity.

This package proves three narrower statements:

1. For every eligible ordered pair $(y,z)$, with $z\in B$ and
   $d(y,z)=2$, and every $p\in N(y)\cap N(z)$, the A4 cycle prescription
   is exactly equivalent to a T15 cycle with the extra prescribed edge $pz$.
2. In the preprocessed case $N(a)\cap B=\varnothing$, each one of these
   prescriptions has a spanning simple cycle factor, uniformly for all $F$.
   The factor need not be connected.
3. T44_5 gives a Hamilton $a$--$z$ path on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ for every
   $z\in B$, preserving $F$. A precisely oriented local pattern suffices to
   close one such path.

##### Status

**PROVABLE AS STATED** for Claims 1--3, relative to the explicitly imported
CF1 and T44_5 below. The universal connected prescription and full T15 are
**NOT CURRENTLY JUSTIFIED**. No strict counterexample to either is claimed.

##### Assumptions and notation

$N(v)$ denotes the five short neighbors of $v$. A cycle factor is a simple
spanning 2-regular graph, possibly disconnected. A prescribed new edge must
be short; an original edge in $F$ need not be short.

The preprocessed case is sufficient for T15: if $az$ is short for some
$z\in B$, apply T44_5 to the matching $F+az$, whose holes are the other
four odd holes, avoiding $x,y$. The added edge is short.

The roles of $x,y$ can be exchanged. The elementary geometry proved in
[T15_EDGE_PRESCRIPTION_REDUCTION.md](#proof-t15-edge-prescription-reduction) guarantees at least one eligible
ordered pair: at most two vertices of a fixed parity can be at distance
four from both $x$ and $y$, whereas $|B|=3$.

##### Proof strategy and dependency map

1. Suppress or expand one degree-two vertex to prove an exact equivalence.
2. Import CF1 from [A4_SPANNING_FACTOR.md](#proof-a4-spanning-factor), audited in
   [A4_FACTOR_REVIEW.md](#review-a4-factor-review), then apply the same suppression to its factors.
   CF1 depends on a complete 65,535-subset geometry certificate and a
   matching-independent Hall loss bound. It is a universal statement about
   arbitrary complete-graph matchings, rather than a matching sample.
3. Import T44_5 from [T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md](#proof-t44-q5-closure-draft), with its accepted scope
   recorded in [T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.md](#review-t44-q5-closure-review). Delete one auxiliary edge.

Neither the proofs below nor these dependencies import full P6.

##### Proof

###### 1. Fixed-prescription equivalence

Fix an eligible $(y,z,p)$ and put $L=F+yz$. Its four holes are $a,x$ and
the other two members of $B$. The following statements are equivalent:

* There is a 31-cycle $C$ on $Q_5-x$ containing $L$ and $yp$, with every
  edge outside $L$ short.
* There is a 30-cycle $D$ on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ containing $F$ and $pz$, with
  every edge outside $F$ short.

In the forward direction the two edges at $y$ are exactly $yz,yp$. Replace
the path $z,y,p$ by the edge $zp$. Because $C$ is one cycle of length 31,
$zp$ cannot already be an edge of $C$: otherwise $p,y,z$ would themselves
form the entire cycle. Suppression gives a simple cycle of length 30.
The edge $zp$ is short by the choice of $p$, and every edge of $F$ remains,
since $y,z$ were holes of $F$.

In the reverse direction replace $zp$ in $D$ by $z,y,p$. The new vertex
$y$ was absent from $D$, so expansion produces a simple 31-cycle. The
only newly introduced edges are the required edge $yz$ of $L$ and the
short edge $yp$. These two operations are inverse.

Thus even the fixed-$p$ strong prescription is a concrete optional-edge
extension question on the original T15 target graph. The weaker sufficient
global obligation is exactly

$$\forall F\ \exists (y,z,p)\ \exists D:
\quad z\in B,\ d(y,z)=2,\ p\in N(y)\cap N(z),\quad pz\in E(D),$$

where the ordered forbidden vertex $y$ may be either member of the
specified avoided pair. Replacing the two existential choices by universal
quantifiers is a stronger assertion, not a consequence of this reduction.

###### 2. Each fixed prescription has a simple spanning cycle factor

Assume $N(a)\cap B=\varnothing$. Fix *any* eligible $(y,z,p)$.
For $L=F+yz$, its two nonforbidden majority holes are the two members of
$B-\{z\}$, and neither is adjacent to $a$. Thus it falls in the
nonadjacent branch required by CF1. The edge $yp$ is an allowed short edge
outside $L$: $y$ is matched only to $z$ in $L$, and $p$ has opposite parity.
CF1 therefore gives a simple spanning 2-factor $J$ on $Q_5-x$ containing
$F+yz+yp$.

Here $p\ne a$, since $p$ is adjacent to $z\in B$. Consequently $p$ is
covered by $F$. It already has its $F$ edge and the edge $py$ in $J$.
There cannot be an edge $pz$ in $J$: it would give $p$ degree three,
because $pz\notin F$ as $z$ is a hole of $F$. Hence $y$ is not in a
triangle of $J$. Suppressing $y$ produces a **simple** spanning 2-factor
$J'$ on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ containing $F+pz$. It preserves the number of
components. Expansion is inverse, also on factors under these hypotheses.

This proves the universal quantification

$$\forall F\ \forall (y,z,p)\ \exists J':
\quad J'\text{ is a simple spanning 2-factor containing }F+pz.$$

It proves neither that one such factor is connected nor that an arbitrary
chosen factor can be merged. In particular Hall feasibility of the
prescribed edge is already settled; the remaining issue is connectedness.

The exclusion of a triangle above matters: without preprocessing one can
have $p=a$, which has no required $F$ edge. A general factor could then
contain the triangle $p,y,z$; suppressing $y$ would create a doubled edge.
The cycle equivalence in Step 1 is valid without preprocessing because a
31-cycle cannot have a separate triangle component.

###### 3. Exact form of the remaining completion problem

Still assume preprocessing. For any target factor $J'$ put $H=J'-F$.
The new degree is two at the four included holes $a$ and $B$, and one at
every covered vertex. These four holes are independent in the cube:
members of $B$ have the same parity, and none is adjacent to $a$.
Every component of $H$ containing a hole is therefore a two-edge path
centered at that hole. Its two ends are covered vertices and have degree
one in $H$. These four paths are disjoint. The remaining 18 covered
vertices are nine isolated edges of $H$.

Thus $H$ always consists of exactly four two-edge paths and nine single
edges, with 17 short edges in total. The completion problem can equivalently
be stated as choosing these paths and edges, disjoint from $F$, such that
$F\cup H$ is connected; under a fixed prescription, require $pz\in H$.

Contracting the 13 edges of $F$ gives a 2-regular multigraph on 17 vertices
(the 13 contracted pairs and the four holes). It has no loops, since $H$
avoids $F$, but it may have parallel edges. Connectivity of this
multigraph is exactly connectivity of $J'$. CF1 establishes that at least
one such completion exists for every eligible prescribed $pz$; it supplies
no connectivity conclusion about this multigraph.

###### 4. T44 supplies every hole-to-hole Hamilton path

Fix $z\in B$ and add the auxiliary edge $az$ to $F$. This is a matching
whose holes are the four odd vertices $x,y$ and $B-\{z\}$. T44_5 gives a
30-cycle on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ containing $F+az$. Delete $az$ to obtain a
Hamilton path from $a$ to $z$ containing $F$, with every new edge short.
The edge $az$ need not be short: it was prescribed as an auxiliary matching
edge and is deleted before the path is used. This proves the assertion for
every choice of $z$, including the preprocessed case.

For completeness, a precise one-rotation sufficient condition is as follows.
Orient such a path $P$ from $a$ to $z$. Suppose consecutive vertices $v,w$
occur in this order, $vw\notin F$, and the following adjacency conditions
hold:

$$v\in N(z),\qquad w\in N(a).$$

Then delete $vw$ and add $vz,wa$. The two resulting path components have
endpoints $a,v$ and $w,z$. The new edges join $v$ to $z$ and $w$ to $a$,
so their union is one spanning cycle. Both new edges are short and the
deleted edge is outside $F$. This closes T15 for that particular path.

The order $v,w$ is essential. If the order is $w,v$, the same operation
closes each path component separately and yields two cycles. No argument
here proves that a path with the required ordered pattern always exists.

##### Corrections or missing assumptions

There is no new universal connected-prescription proof in this package.
The exact missing lemma is that, for every preprocessed T15 matching $F$,
at least one eligible prescribed $pz$ admits a **connected** completion
$F\cup H$ of the form in Step 3. Requiring this separately for every
eligible $p$ is a potentially unnecessary strengthening.

##### Open risks

* The factor result imports CF1's complete finite geometry certificate;
  it is not presented as a purely analytic proof of that certificate.
* T44_5 is imported at its audited scope for arbitrary $K(Q_5)$ matchings.
* The ordered rotation criterion is sufficient only. Failure of this
  criterion for some chosen path would not refute T15.
* Full T15, the connected A4 optional-edge strengthening, and full P6
  retain their previous open status.


</details>


<details id="proof-t15-r3-small-crossing-progress" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md — Proof Package: r3 small-crossing kernels</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T15_R3_SMALL_CROSSING_PROGRESS.md)。SHA-256：`8218505ba8b0c8833272760aa353abb827f20bd2dfe28d68fa8d1bf235bc72f4`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE0_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE15_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE15_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE23_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE23_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE27_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE27_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE5_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE5_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_CORE8_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_CORE8_FULL_REVIEW.json)。

#### Proof Package: r3 small-crossing kernels

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer. This file supplies the complete small-crossing pieces for core 0; it does not claim full T15 or the complete eight-hole layer.

##### Claim

Consider an arbitrary complete-graph matching on two adjacent four-dimensional cube faces. In the common local labels, its uncovered vertices are $\{0,3,5\}$ in face $A$ and $\{0,7,1\}$ in face $B$. The prescribed omitted vertices are $0_A$ and $1_B$. If the matching has exactly $c\in\{1,3\}$ crossing edges, it extends to a simple cycle on the other thirty vertices using only short new edges. This is the core-0 profile.

The $c=3$ conclusion also holds for the profiles called cores 5 and 23 below. For the remaining profiles, only the explicitly stated finite reduction is proved here.

##### Status

PROVABLE AS STATED for the preceding claim, conditional on the previously imported Q4 N14 theorem and the independently audited complete balanced four-hole tables. Independent checking performed in this work is recorded in [t15_r3_small_verification.json](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_verification.json) (PASS). A fresh overall proof review remains appropriate before integration.

##### Assumptions

- Q4 N14: every arbitrary complete-graph matching with two holes of the same parity extends to a 15-cycle omitting either specified hole, with short new edges.
- The audited complete Q4 tables for holes $\{0,7,z,y\}$, omitting $z,y$, are exact. Each contains all $11!!=10395$ matchings on the other twelve vertices. See `T15_BALANCED_BRIDGE_REVIEW.md/.json` and `q4_balanced_two_avoided_*_*.bin`.
- The common local labeling preserves short edges and mirrors across the cut. No restriction is imposed on crossing partners or on the lengths of original matching edges.

##### Notation

Let $x$ be the omitted $A$ hole, let $r,s$ be its two retained holes, and let $y$ be the omitted $B$ hole. Write $F_A,F_B$ for the two internal matchings, $X_A,X_B$ for their crossing ports, and $C:X_A\to X_B$ for the arbitrary crossing bijection. Both faces have thirteen originally covered vertices. The retained $B$ holes are $0,7$. For a bridge $z\in\{r,s\}$, define $E_z=X_A\cup\{z\}$.

An $A$ pairing is a perfect matching on $E_z$ obtained by compressing the path components of a spanning path forest on $A-x$ that contains $F_A$ and uses short added edges. No cyclic component is permitted in that forest.

##### Proof Strategy

For $c=3$, every bridge has at least two realizable $A$ pairings among the three possible pairings. A complete independent finite enumeration shows that every core-0 $B$ input has a bridge permitting at least two of these pairings. The two sets intersect. For $c=1$, the same construction leaves exactly six $B$ inputs; all $6\cdot135135=810810$ complete residual inputs have explicit independently verified thirty-vertex cycles.

##### Dependency Map

1. N14 supplies the $A$ path forests and the two-of-three pairing lemma.
2. The audited balanced tables decide which compressed $B$ matchings have the required fourteen-vertex cycle.
3. [verify_t15_r3_small_B.cpp](research/six_directions/verify_t15_r3_small_B.cpp) independently enumerates every $B$ input and reconstructs each compression as a graph.
4. [verify_t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.cpp](research/six_directions/verify_t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.cpp) independently checks both exhaustive residual-input coverage and every saved positive cycle.

##### Proof

###### Step 1. Pairing abundance for three crossings

Fix a bridge $z$ and suppose $c=3$. There are exactly three perfect matchings on the four vertices of $E_z$. For any such artificial matching $D$, the matching $F_A\cup D$ has precisely the two same-parity holes $x$ and the other retained $A$ hole. N14 gives a 15-cycle omitting $x$. Deleting the two edges of $D$ produces two paths spanning $A-x$, whose endpoint pairing is some $R$ on $E_z$.

The pairing $R$ cannot equal $D$: if equal, restoring the two artificial edges would close each path separately, yielding two components instead of the N14 cycle. If the realizable pairing set were a singleton $\{R_0\}$, applying N14 with $D=R_0$ would contradict this fact. Consequently every bridge has at least two realizable pairings. This argument avoids dependence on the producer's exhaustive $A$ spectra.

For $c=1$, the endpoint set has two vertices and its unique pairing is realized by deleting the single artificial edge supplied to N14.

###### Step 2. Exact meaning of an admissible B pairing

Map each endpoint $a\in X_A$ to $C(a)\in X_B$ and map endpoint $z\in E_z$ to the mirror $z_B$. Regard each pair of $R$ as the compression of its corresponding $A$ path with the attached original crossings and the new short bridge $z_Az_B$. Unite these compressed edges with $F_B$ to obtain a multigraph $J$ on $B-\{0,7,y\}$.

Every vertex of $J$ except $z_B$ has degree one and $z_B$ has degree two. Reject a pairing if $J$ contains a closed component, including a loop at $z_B$. Otherwise its path components compress to a perfect matching $L$ on $B-\{0,7,y,z\}$. Its six pairs contain all original $B$ edges not incident to $z$, and the original edge incident to $z$, if present, is recovered by expanding the corresponding path.

Call $R$ admissible if this $L$ is positive in the audited balanced table. Expanding its fourteen-vertex cycle restores all fifteen $A-x$ vertices and $z_B$, giving a simple thirty-vertex cycle. All original matching edges survive; all added edges are short. Distinct path interiors ensure that expansion preserves simplicity.

###### Step 3. Complete independent B enumeration

The producer [t15_r3_small_spectra.cpp](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_spectra.cpp) enumerates the $B$ partial matchings, all crossing bijections, and all one or three pairings for each of the two bridges. Its implementation explicitly suppresses the degree-two vertex.

The independent checker [verify_t15_r3_small_B.cpp](research/six_directions/verify_t15_r3_small_B.cpp) reads the thirteen original binary tables directly, transforms their exact negative lists under the six coordinate permutations fixing coordinate 3, and covers all 49 marked balanced geometries. It does not read the producer's prepared negative list. It then builds the multigraph $J$, traces all paths from degree-one endpoints, rejects any unvisited closed component, and looks up the resulting endpoint matching. Thus it does not reuse the producer's suppression procedure.

For $c=1$ it checks all $13\cdot11!!=135135$ internal partial matchings. For $c=3$ it checks all $\binom{13}{3}9!!=270270$ internal partial matchings and all $3!=6$ crossing bijections, totaling $1621620$ inputs per profile. The bit positions for $c=3$ are the three pairings $01|23$, $02|13$, $03|12$ on the ordered ports followed by the bridge endpoint, first for $r$ and then for $s$.

[verify_t15_r3_small_results.py](research/six_directions/verify_t15_r3_small_results.py) checks exact equality of the complete independent and producer $B$ spectrum histograms. It also checks that each nonzero three-crossing spectrum permits at least two pairings for at least one bridge. For core 0 there are no zero three-crossing spectra. Step 1 and the elementary fact that two subsets of size at least two of a three-element set intersect now prove the entire core-0 $c=3$ case.

###### Step 4. Complete core-0 one-crossing reduction

For $c=1$, the unique $A$ pairing works whenever either bridge's corresponding $B$ pairing is admissible. The complete independent enumeration identifies exactly six $B$ inputs with neither bridge admissible. These are saved in [t15_r3_small_core0_c1_B_exceptions.txt](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_core0_c1_B_exceptions.txt); their equality with the residual search inputs [t15_r3_small_core0_c1_B_inputs.txt](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_core0_c1_B_inputs.txt) is independently asserted by [verify_t15_r3_small_results.py](research/six_directions/verify_t15_r3_small_results.py).

The six exceptional inputs, each showing its sole port followed by its six internal edges, are:

```text
3 : 2-4 5-6 8-10 9-13 11-12 14-15
3 : 2-4 5-6 8-14 9-13 10-15 11-12
3 : 2-4 5-6 8-15 9-13 10-14 11-12
5 : 2-4 3-6 8-12 9-11 10-13 14-15
5 : 2-4 3-6 8-14 9-11 10-13 12-15
5 : 2-4 3-6 8-15 9-11 10-13 12-14
```

The $A$ crossing port has thirteen possibilities, and the other twelve covered $A$ vertices have $11!!=10395$ internal matchings. Thus these six inputs leave exactly $6\cdot13\cdot10395=810810$ original Q5 matchings.

###### Step 5. Positive certificates for every residual matching

Use global labels $2v+1$ for $v_A$ and $2v$ for $v_B$. The omitted vertices are globally $1,2$, and the four retained free vertices are $0,7,11,14$. This label map is a cube isomorphism. Each residual input has thirteen required edges: six internal edges on each face and its sole crossing edge.

[t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.cpp](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.cpp) exhaustively emits a certificate for every residual input. The search treats each required edge as an indivisible block and links oriented blocks using short edges. Its finite node cap is irrelevant to acceptance because all inputs succeed: the result is $810810$ positive, zero UNKNOWN, zero exhausted negatives. The maximum visited-node count for any input is $9359$, below the cap of $2000000$.

The independent verifier reconstructs each expected input by independently enumerating all ports and all pairings of the other twelve vertices. Each 56-byte record contains its thirteen required edges followed by thirty cycle vertices. The verifier checks exact equality of the recorded required edges with the independently reconstructed input, uniqueness and exact support of the cycle vertices, presence of all thirteen required edges, and Hamming distance one of every other cycle edge. It asserts exactly $810810$ records and no trailing bytes. These checks pass.

The binary certificate file is [t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.bin](research/six_directions/t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.bin), size 45,405,360 bytes, SHA-256 `4764b5f4d0252e5bcfc1a09c87c79a8c86bd1c1c56d88a31b72b323d3c5902b6`.

Steps 1--5 prove both small-crossing cases claimed for core 0. ∎

##### Additional finite kernels

The same independent enumeration was completed on all seven requested profiles. In the table, the exceptional count is the number of $B$ partial matchings with zero admissible pairing on both bridges. For three crossings every such partial matching fails for all six crossing bijections; every other input has at least two good pairings on one bridge.

| Core | $x;r,s$ in $A$ | $y$ in $B$ | $c=1$ exceptional B | $c=3$ exceptional B |
|---:|:---|---:|---:|---:|
|0|$0;3,5$|$1$|6|0|
|5|$0;3,6$|$1$|5|0|
|8|$0;3,15$|$1$|22|10|
|15|$0;10,15$|$1$|12|1|
|23|$9;3,5$|$8$|20|0|
|26|$9;3,15$|$8$|82|24|
|27|$9;6,15$|$8$|82|24|

Hence cores 5 and 23 also have complete $c=3$ proofs by Steps 1--3. The full exact exceptional B lists are saved as `t15_r3_small_core<K>_c<C>_B_exceptions.txt`. Those residuals for other cores are not claimed solved here.

##### Reproduction

From this directory, compile the three C++ executables with `g++ -O3 -std=c++17` and run:

```powershell
./verify_t15_r3_small_B.exe | Out-File -Encoding utf8 t15_r3_small_B_independent.json
./verify_t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.exe t15_r3_small_core0_c1_B_inputs.txt t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual.bin | Out-File -Encoding utf8 t15_r3_small_core0_c1_residual_verification.json
python verify_t15_r3_small_results.py
```

The producer for any listed profile is `t15_r3_small_spectra.exe <core> <c> <prefix>`. The residual certificate producer takes the exceptional B input path, binary output path, and failure log path as its three arguments.

##### Corrections or Missing Assumptions

None for the stated small-crossing claim. This file deliberately does not assert the larger-crossing cases or full T15.

##### Open Risks

- The N14 import and the balanced-table audit are external dependencies explicitly retained in the claim.
- Core normalization and integration into the eight-hole parent count require separate review; this package proves the displayed common-label profiles.
- Other cores' exceptional B residuals remain open within this package.


</details>


<details id="proof-t15-sameface-zero-crossing" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T15_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md — T15 in Q5: all six holes in one face, zero required crossings</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T15_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md)。SHA-256：`1aec13d85973868163a2560945de84abf6a459f45382f8c8b53e35c020df0be5`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json)。

#### T15 in Q5: all six holes in one face, zero required crossings

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer/proof-checker scoped package.
Semantic assurance: **same-family / provisional**. The deterministic finite
checks are separate from this semantic assurance. No global state is changed.

##### Exact quantified claim

For every matching F of the complete graph on V(Q5), suppose its uncovered
vertices are exactly {a} union H, where |H|=5 and each member of H has cube
parity opposite to a. For every pair of distinct specified vertices v,w in H,
suppose a coordinate cut Q5=A union B has all six holes in A and no edge of F
crosses that cut. Then a simple cycle exists on exactly V(Q5) minus {v,w},
contains every edge of F, and has only short cube edges outside F.
Thus the cycle has 30 vertices. Required edges of F may be long and may join
vertices of the same parity. The claim includes either parity for a.

This is a theorem for every input satisfying this particular cut condition.
It is not the unrestricted Q5 T15 theorem and does not prove full P6.

##### Inputs, symbols, and obligations

Identify the two faces with the same Q4 by deleting the cut coordinate. A
vertex x in A corresponds to bar(x) in B, and x--bar(x) is a short Q5 edge.
Write F_A and F_B for the two restrictions. The zero-crossing hypothesis
implies that F_B is a perfect matching, while F_A has precisely the six holes.

The imported theorem T44_5 is the statement in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md,
with current PASS provenance in T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json. It says that
four holes of one parity allow omission of any prescribed two holes in a
30-cycle. Its proof and its Q4/Fink dependencies are explicit imports here;
they are not rerun in this package. The import has same-family/provisional
semantic assurance. No Q5 T15 or P6 result is used to prove a local step.

The new independent checker imports no generator or earlier checker. It
reads all four positive path files and both complete opposite-hole circle
tables directly. Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md supplies context and the name of
the triangle condition; its cycle classification is not needed as an
unproved shortcut in the path argument below.

Dependency DAG:

* Complete opposite-hole circle tables, including exhaustive negative
  complements -> perfect-matching root-endpoint bounds.
* Four T15 positive path tables + full matching coverage -> A path bounds.
* Lossless cube automorphisms + complete marked-hole geometry partition ->
  those four residual representatives cover all nonadjacent inputs.
* T44_5 -> adjacent available-hole branch.
* A and B endpoint bounds + two-bridge construction -> residual branch.

All objects are finite. There are no limit interchanges or asymptotic
uniformity assumptions. Bounds are uniform over all complete-graph
matchings of the stated vertex supports.

##### 1. Adjacent available-hole branch

If some b in H minus {v,w} is short-adjacent to a, add ab to F. Both are
holes, so this is still a matching. Its four remaining holes are H minus
{b}, all of one parity, and contain v,w. Apply imported T44_5, omitting
exactly v,w. The resulting cycle contains F union {ab}; the edge ab was
short, so relative to the original F every added edge is short as required.

##### 2. Lossless residual normalization and complete coverage

Suppose no member of H minus {v,w} is adjacent to a. Translate the common
local labels on both faces by a, putting the root at 0 in A and bar(0) in B.
The five majority holes then have odd local parity, regardless of a's
original local or global parity. Each of the three available holes is a
nonneighbor of 0, hence has Q4 weight 3. Permute coordinates, on both
faces simultaneously, so these three vertices become {7,11,13}. This is
possible because the four weight-3 vertices are the complements of the
four distinct coordinate units; any choice of three can be sent to this
choice. These transformations preserve all short edges and transport any
arbitrary matching bijectively; they also preserve the correspondence of
the two faces and the identities of the two omitted holes.

The omitted pair is now drawn from {1,2,4,8,14}. The permutations preserving
{7,11,13} fix coordinate unit 1 and permute units {2,4,8}. Their four
unordered-pair orbits have representatives

    (1,2), (2,4), (1,14), (2,14).

Independently enumerating all binomial(8,5)*binomial(5,2)=560 marked
geometries at root 0 gives 520 adjacent geometries and 40 residual ones.
The four full coordinate-permutation orbits have sizes 12,12,4,12 and are
disjoint. Every residual geometry belongs to exactly one. Translation
handles every minority root, including the parity-reversed case; there
is no assumption that an arbitrary input was already in a representative.

##### 3. Independently checked A path bounds

For each representative pair (v,w), the holes are {0,7,11,13,v,w}. The
remaining ten vertices admit exactly 9!!=945 complete-graph matchings.
The checker generates this entire matching set independently and deletes
one matching for each parsed record. At the end the set is empty. Invalid
mate arrays, duplicate inputs, missing inputs, incomplete records, and
trailing bytes all cause failure.

Each row gives a lower set S of odd endpoints q: every q in S has an
explicit 0--q path on precisely Q4 minus {v,w}. Each path has 14 distinct
vertices, retains all five required matching edges, and has only short
edges outside that matching. Distinct witnesses in a row have distinct
endpoints. No claim that S lists every possible endpoint is required.

Let N={1,2,4,8} and D3={7,11,13,14}. Define the triangle condition by

    {v,w} subset N, N minus {v,w}={p,q}, and pq in F_A.

The deterministic checks establish:

* If the triangle condition fails, S is all six allowed odd endpoints,
  namely ODD minus {v,w}.
* If the triangle condition holds, S contains all four members of D3.
  In particular these endpoints are allowed, since v,w are neighbors.

The 3780 complete matching records give 22260 positive paths. There are
210 triangular records, each with four listed endpoints; all other 3570
records have six listed endpoints. The two families with both omitted
vertices neighboring 0 have histograms {4:105,6:840}; each other family
has {6:945}. The checker also confirms the generation JSON against these
counts, but does not trust the producer's search or its failure behavior.

The triangle condition obstructs a corresponding 14-cycle through 0 in
the older classification. It does not obstruct the endpoint paths used
here: the root 0 has degree one in an A path. Its positive paths are
checked directly, including all 210 records.

##### 4. Independently checked B endpoint bounds

For every complete-graph perfect matching P on Q4 and every root r, let
G(P,r) consist of opposite-parity vertices q for which a Hamilton r--q
path contains P and uses only short additional edges. Then

    |G(P,r)| >= 4,
    G(P,r) intersects {q: d_Q4(r,q)=3}.

The package independently checks the full finite basis behind
Q4_PERFECT_ENDPOINT_ABUNDANCE.md, rather than treating the saved 4708
rows as a complete proof by themselves. At root 0, for odd endpoint y,
P(0)=y is necessarily impossible: the mandatory edge 0y would already
exhaust both endpoint degrees, leaving the remaining vertices disconnected.
Otherwise put a=P(0), b=P(y). The four vertices 0,y,a,b are distinct.
Deleting 0,y from a desired Hamilton path and adding the auxiliary edge ab
is equivalent to a 14-cycle containing

    T = P minus {0a,yb} union {ab}

on Q4 minus {0,y}. The reverse removes ab and restores the two endpoint
edges. The auxiliary edge cannot coincide with a retained P edge, and
the 14-vertex path cannot already contain ab: that would isolate its two
endpoints from its other twelve vertices. Thus both constructions give
simple paths/cycles and preserve all original required edges.

The two complete tables with omitted sets {0,1} and {0,7} each contain
135135 distinct valid matchings, exactly 13!!, which proves full coverage.
All 270166 positive circles pass direct support/edge/shortness checks.
For all 104 negatives (51 and 53), the checker exhausts complementary
short perfect matchings disjoint from T. Any required cycle must be such
a union, since T covers each surviving vertex once and a cycle covers it
twice. Every enumerated union has more than one connected component;
therefore the claimed negatives are rigorously impossible.

Coordinate permutations transport the negative tables to all eight odd
endpoints. For every negative T and every oriented edge ab in T, construct
P=T minus {ab} union {0a,yb}. These are all failed endpoint pairs other
than the exceptional trivial case P(0)=y, by the preceding equivalence.
There are 5824 labeled inverse instances and 4708 distinct candidate P.
For each candidate the checker recomputes all eight endpoints by the
forward rule, adds the trivial bad endpoint when present, and agrees with
every saved exact endpoint row. The bad-endpoint histogram is
{1:2072,2:2180,3:36,4:420}; the good distance-3 histogram is
{1:420,2:276,3:2212,4:1800}. These imply the two stated bounds within the
candidate universe. Outside it, only a possible odd partner P(0) can be
bad, giving at least seven good odd endpoints and at least three good
distance-3 endpoints. This proves the bounds for every P, without a
quantifier gap caused by inspecting only the exceptional candidates.
Translation gives every root r.

##### 5. Endpoint intersection and exact two-bridge gluing

Apply Section 4 to F_B at root bar(0), in the same local labels. Let G be
its set of good odd local endpoints. If the A record is nontriangular,
|S|=6 and |G|>=4 inside an eight-element universe, so |S intersect G|>=2.
If it is triangular, S contains D3 and G intersects D3, so again their
intersection is nonempty. Choose any q in the intersection and its two
witnessing paths R_A and R_B.

The A path goes from 0_A to q_A and visits exactly A minus {v,w}; the B
path goes from 0_B to q_B and visits all of B. Their supports are disjoint,
and q is odd while 0 is even, so each path has two distinct endpoints.
Add the two short edges

    0_A--0_B and q_A--q_B.

Starting at 0_A, traverse R_A to q_A, cross to q_B, traverse R_B backwards
to 0_B, then cross back to 0_A. This explicitly visits every retained
vertex once and gives one simple cycle, not a disconnected 2-factor.
It has 14+16=30 vertices and omits exactly v,w. Every original matching
edge is internal to a face by hypothesis and is retained by its path.
Every other path edge is short; the two bridges are also short. Undoing
the shared automorphism proves the precise claim above.

##### Reproduction and scope boundary

Run D:/anaconda/python.exe
research/six_directions/T15_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING_check.py from E:/新问题.
The dedicated JSON contains input hashes, every family count, orbit
coverage, the full negative-complement evidence, and the independent
perfect endpoint census. The review records a hash of this proof too.

This closes only the all-six-holes-in-a-coordinate-face, zero-required-
crossing T15 branch, conditional on imported T44_5 for its adjacent
subbranch. The nonadjacent subbranch is established directly from the
independently checked Q4 certificates. Inputs with required crossings,
hole sets in no common coordinate face, the remaining T15 cases, and
full P6 are not resolved here. No global closure ledger is edited.


</details>


<details id="proof-t15-single-avoided-face-closure" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_CLOSURE.md — Eight T15 hole orbits with a singleton avoided face</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_CLOSURE.md)。SHA-256：`3c85fea859c2471bfbe756294ecadb7d74eb8bb3dc31a61c7adfbb871925eae4`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_SINGLE_AVOIDED_FACE_REVIEW.json)。

#### Eight T15 hole orbits with a singleton avoided face

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer package.
Status: PROVABLE AS STATED relative to the listed Q4 finite certificates;
independent audit pending. Full T15 and full P6 remain unproved.

##### Exact claim

Let $F$ be any matching of the complete graph on $V(Q_5)$, with holes
$\{a,x,y,b_1,b_2,b_3\}$, where $a$ has parity opposite to all five other
holes. The specified omitted holes are $x,y$. For every input whose marked
hole geometry is a cube-automorphic image of any of the eight rows below,
there is a simple cycle on $Q_5-\{x,y\}$ containing $F$, with only short
edges outside $F$. The cycle has exactly $30$ vertices.

The eight rows refer to zero-based orbit IDs in
[t15_analytic_geometry.json](research/six_directions/t15_analytic_geometry.json) and are equivalently specified by the local
table below. The original minority hole is normalized to $0$ before
reading the orbit IDs. The claim is for **every** matching realizing each
geometry; required edges may be long or join equal parities.

##### Normalization, notation and dependencies

Choose the indicated cut. Its one-face $A$ contains exactly one original
hole, the omitted vertex $y$; the other face $B$ contains the other five
holes. Delete the cut coordinate and translate the common local labels by
the local label of $y$, so $y_A=0$. The corresponding vertex of $B$ has
the same local label and is joined by a short bridge. In these labels the
minority hole in $B$ is even, its other four holes are odd. Both coordinate
deletion and the common translation preserve adjacency within faces and
the correspondence across the cut.

| orbit | cut (zero-based) | B minority $a$ | B omitted $x$ | B included holes $I$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|13|1|0|1|7,11,13|
|14|1|0|1|7,11,14|
|19|2|3|2|4,8,14|
|31|3|6|7|1,11,13|
|32|3|6|7|1,8,13|
|35|3|6|7|8,11,13|
|37|0|0|7|11,13,14|
|38|4|15|14|2,4,8|

Write $F_A,F_B$ for the internal restrictions, $C$ for the original
crossing edges, $X_A,X_B$ for their endpoint sets, and $c=|C|$.
There are $15$ covered original vertices in $A$ and $11$ in $B$.
Consequently $c$ is odd and $1\le c\le11$.

Dependencies, with no use of Q5 T15 or P6:

1. Complete Q4 two-opposite-hole cycle tables, including their certified
   $51+53$ exceptions ([q4_distance1_avoided_table_verification.json](research/six_directions/q4_distance1_avoided_table_verification.json) and
   [q4_distance3_avoided_table_verification.json](research/six_directions/q4_distance3_avoided_table_verification.json)), decide the A paths below.
2. Q4 A4: holes $1:3$, omit a specified majority hole, obtain a 15-cycle
   ([Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md](#proof-q4-core-and-a4-split)).
3. Exact Q4 T15 classification ([Q4_T15_CLASSIFICATION.md](#proof-q4-t15-classification)): for holes
   $1:5$, omitting two majority holes fails precisely when both omitted
   vertices neighbor the minority and the required matching joins its
   other two neighbors. In particular it succeeds if either omitted
   vertex is not a neighbor of the minority.
4. Finite completion accounting in `t15_single_avoided_face_probe.py/.json`.
5. Positive optional-edge spectra in [t15_single_crossing_spectra.json](research/six_directions/t15_single_crossing_spectra.json),
   whose paths/cycles are independently checkable without trusting search.

Every application below specifies the resulting hole set and omitted
vertices. These are finite statements; no asymptotic or limiting argument
is used. All local degree-two contractions are expanded at the end.

##### 1. The exact A path test

Choose $d\in X_A$ and a perfect pairing $D$ on $X_A-\{d\}$.
Then $L=F_A\cup D$ is a matching on $Q_4$ with holes $0,d$.
For an odd vertex $z\ne d$, let $k=L(z)$. Define
$T_z=L-\{zk\}+\{dk\}$, a matching with holes $0,z$.

A 14-cycle on $Q_4-\{0,z\}$ containing $T_z$ is equivalent to a
15-vertex $d$--$z$ path on $A-\{0\}$ containing $L$ and using short
new edges. In the forward direction delete $dk$, then append $kz$.
In the reverse direction $zk$ must be the last edge, since $z$ is covered
by $L$ and is an endpoint; delete $z$ and add $dk$. Both graphs are simple:
$d,k,z,0$ are distinct, and adding an edge between endpoints of a
14-vertex path cannot duplicate one already in that path. The case $z=d$
is declared unavailable. Thus the complete Q4 tables give an exact test.

##### 2. Transfers for safe and occupied endpoints

Set
$$S=\{z\in O(Q_4):z\ne x,\ d(a,x)\ne1\text{ or }d(a,z)\ne1\}.$$
The three vertices in $I$ belong to $S$ in every row. Suppose Section 1
gives an A path $P$ with endpoint $z\in S$. Delete $D$, attach all original
crossings $C$, and add the short bridge $z_Az_B$.

###### 2a. Safe endpoint: $z_B\notin X_B$

This is a path forest with endpoint set $X_B\cup\{z_B\}$ and interiors
partitioning $A-\{0\}$. If $z_A$ itself is a port different from $d$,
its mandatory edge belongs to $D$ and is the last edge of $P$; deleting
it isolates $z_A$ temporarily. Its original crossing and its new bridge
restore degree two, yielding a valid path component. No original matching
edge is lost. Compress each path to obtain a matching $R$ on the endpoint
set.

If $z\in I$, the matching $F_B\cup R$ has holes
$\{a,x\}\cup(I-\{z\})$, of type $1:3$. Q4 A4 omits $x$, giving a
15-cycle. Expand $R$ to obtain the desired $15+15=30$ cycle.

Otherwise $z_B$ is internally covered, since it is neither an original
hole nor a port. Write $k=F_B(z)$ and $q=R(z)$.
The sets of internal matching endpoints and crossing ports are disjoint,
so $k\ne q$ and replacing $kz,zq$ by $kq$ creates a matching $L_B$.
Its holes are $\{a,x\}\cup I\cup\{z\}$, of type $1:5$.
At least one of $x,z$ is nonadjacent to $a$ by the definition of $S$.
The exact Q4 T15 theorem therefore gives a 14-cycle omitting $x,z$.
Expand $kq$ and the remaining compressed edges. This restores $z_B$ and
all $15$ A vertices, producing a single $14+1+15=30$ cycle.

###### 2b. Occupied endpoint: $z_B\in X_B$, $c\ge3$

Here require $d=C^{-1}(z_B)$ to be a good root for $z$ in Section 1.
Then $d\ne z$ and $D$ is nonempty. Deleting $D$ from $P$ separates its
two endpoints. Attaching the original crossings adds distinct B leaves.
The bridge $z_Az_B$ joins the two different endpoint components, because
$z_B$ was attached at $d$. It creates no cycle. If $z_A$ is also a port,
its separate crossing ends at a different B port; the temporary isolated
vertex boundary is covered by the same argument.

The resulting forest has endpoints $X_B-\{z_B\}$ and interiors precisely
$(A-\{0\})\cup\{z_B\}$. Compress it to $R$. Now $F_B\cup R$ is a
matching with holes $\{a,x\}\cup I\cup\{z\}$. Apply the same Q4 T15
theorem omitting $x,z$ and expand. The resulting cycle has $30$ vertices.
All artificial edges are deleted or expanded, so all surviving new edges
are short. Section 4 treats the excluded case $c=1$ separately.

##### 3. Complete accounting of roots and port pairings

For each odd $z$, inverse-enumerate every failing state $(d,L)$ with
$z\ne d$ from the negative Q4 table for holes $0,z$. For every such
negative matching $T$ and oriented edge $dk$ of $T$, the inverse is
$L=T-\{dk\}+\{zk\}$. Set storage removes duplicates. These inverses are
complete by Section 1; $d=z$ is handled separately in each test.

Any state failing all three fixed targets $I$ belongs to the union of
their inverse lists, since at most one target equals $d$. Test all three
conditions in that union. There are $105$ failed states for each of
orbits $13,14,31,35,37$, and none for $19,32,38$.

For fixed $c$, a partial $F_A$ has $(15-c)/2$ edges. It has exactly
$c(c-2)!!$ states $(d,F_A\cup D)$, with $(-1)!!=1$.
Count appearances of each submatching of that size in all failed states.
It is stalled exactly when the count equals $c(c-2)!!$; smaller counts
leave a successful fixed-target choice. Every stalled partial is listed
this way, including those not selected by any prior construction.

For each of the five nonempty rows the stalled counts at
$c=1,3,5,7,9,11$ are respectively $105,105,21,1,0,0$.
For each stalled partial and root $d$, there are $(c-2)!!$ pairings.
For each $z\in S$, count failed completions at that root. A root is good
exactly when $d\ne z$ and this count is smaller than $(c-2)!!$.

Let $G$ be the endpoints in $S$ with at least one good root. If $|G|>c$,
some endpoint is safe. Otherwise, failure of both transfers would require
$G\subseteq X_B$ and an injective assignment $z\mapsto C^{-1}(z_B)$
mapping every $z$ to a bad root. The finite check tests Hall's condition
on these bad-root sets and stores a deficient subset whenever no such
injection exists. For every stalled partial at $c\ge3$, there is either
a safe endpoint by $|G|>c$ or no bad-root injection. Thus Section 2 applies
to every actual crossing endpoint set and every actual crossing bijection.

For orbit $37$ the same check gives a safe endpoint also at $c=1$.
For the other four rows $13,14,31,35$, the only usable endpoint in each
$c=1$ stalled state is the following $h$:

|orbit|13|14|31|35|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|$h$|14|13|8|1|

If $X_B\ne\{h\}$, $h$ is safe and Section 2a applies.
The only remaining case is $X_B=\{h\}$, treated next.

##### 4. One crossing: two cycles and a certified common optional edge

Fix one of the four rows and one of its $105$ stalled A matchings.
The only crossing is $d_Ah_B$. The available A path $P$ goes from $d_A$
to $h_A$ through all of $A-\{0\}$. Add $d_Ah_B$ and the short bridge
$h_Ah_B$ to close a simple 16-cycle $C_A$ whose support is
$(A-\{0\})\cup\{h_B\}$. The endpoints $d,h$ are distinct.

The B matching has holes $\{a,x,h\}\cup I$ and five edges, since its
only port is $h$. Thus there are exactly $9!!=945$ possible $F_B$.
Since $h$ is not a neighbor of $a$, Q4 T15 gives a 14-cycle $C_B$ on
$B-\{x,h\}$ containing $F_B$.

It remains to choose $P,C_B$ with a common optional short edge in their
local coordinates. This is a finite positive-certificate assertion:
for each of the $105$ A matchings, retain a collection of valid $d$--$h$
paths, and for each of the $945$ B matchings retain valid 14-cycles.
Let $U_A,U_B$ be the unions of their short edges outside $F_A,F_B$.
Every one of the $105\cdot945$ pairs has $U_A\cap U_B\ne\varnothing$.
The minimum intersection sizes, by row $13,14,31,35$, are $7,5,9,6$.
The four rows comprise $396900$ pairs, with no empty intersection.

The files [t15_single_crossing_spectrum_inputs.json](research/six_directions/t15_single_crossing_spectrum_inputs.json) and
[t15_single_crossing_spectra.json](research/six_directions/t15_single_crossing_spectra.json) contain all $4200$ matching inputs and
the witnessing paths/cycles. [t15_single_crossing_spectra.py](research/six_directions/t15_single_crossing_spectra.py) checks
every witness's exact support, endpoints, matching containment and
shortness, reconstructs every stored union, and tests every pairwise
intersection. Completeness of the B matching lists is by all pairings of
their ten covered vertices; completeness of the A lists is Section 3.
Only these **lower bounds** on optional-edge unions are needed; no failed
search or assertion of maximality of a spectrum is used in the proof.

Choose $st\in U_A\cap U_B$, and choose its witnessing $P,C_B$.
Build $C_A$ from that $P$ as above. Delete $s_At_A$ from $C_A$ and
$s_Bt_B$ from $C_B$, then insert the two short bridges $s_As_B,t_At_B$.
The cycles were vertex-disjoint. The deleted edges belong to neither
original matching, and $s,t$ are distinct and avoid $0,x,h$ because
they occur in both local supports. The two opened paths joined by the
two bridges form one simple cycle on their union. It covers precisely
$Q_5-\{0_A,x_B\}$, retains $F_A,F_B,d_Ah_B$, and all added edges are
short. This resolves the last one-crossing case.

##### Conclusion and limits

Sections 2--4 exhaust all roots, pairings, crossing counts and internal
matchings for all eight displayed marked geometries, so the exact claim
follows relative to the listed finite inputs. Undo their normalizations
and any cube automorphism to cover their entire marked-hole orbits.

This does not prove all T15 geometries. It does not address Q6 EP0 or
claim full eight-hole P6. Its concrete Q6 coverage must be recomputed
against all allowed cuts before updating any remaining-parent count.
The prescribed-edge route remains a separate unproved connectivity route.


</details>


<details id="proof-t44-q5-closure-draft" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md — Four same-parity holes in Q5: avoiding any prescribed two</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T44_Q5_CLOSURE_DRAFT.md)。SHA-256：`96f8273168ddf1fbc4e9cc7cdd9c733ced8ab8cdfe868c593b10dba900b7a7d0`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/EIGHT_HOLE_FULL_REVIEW.json), [HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/HIGHER_HOLE_UNIFIED_TRANSFER_REVIEW.json), [T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T15_NEW_CONSEQUENCES_REVIEW.json), [T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T44_Q5_CLOSURE_REVIEW.json)。

#### Four same-parity holes in Q5: avoiding any prescribed two

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer draft. Proposed complete proof relative
to the specified Q4 certificates and preceding gluing lemmas. Independent
proof-checker audit pending; full P6 and full Q5 T15 remain open.

##### Claim T44_5

For every matching F of K(Q5) with exactly four uncovered vertices, all
of one parity, and every specified pair of distinct holes x,y, there is
a cycle through exactly Q5 minus {x,y}, containing F and having every
edge outside F short. Thus the cycle has 30 vertices. Original required
edges are arbitrary, including long and same-parity edges.

##### Inputs and dependency map

1. Q4 N14 (two same-parity holes, omit one) and T44_4 (four same-parity
   holes, omit two), certified in Q4_CORE_AND_A4_SPLIT.md and
   Q4_TWO_AVOIDED_TRANSFER.md with their independent reviews.
2. Q4_RICH_GLUING.md, reviewed PASS in Q4_RICH_GLUING_REVIEW.md/.json:
   two avoided Q4 cycles with opposite LOCAL forbidden parities have
   intersecting optional-new-edge unions in the stated two-hole cases.
3. T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md: all four holes in one face and no
   crossings are handled by two local paths and two short bridges.
   It uses the complete Q4 perfect-endpoint classification and the
   311850 four-hole path certificates. Its separate audit is required.
4. Complete Q4 opposite-parity two-avoided circle tables, already audited
   in CANONICAL_COMPLETION_REVIEW.md. There are 51 negative matchings
   for holes 0,1 and 53 for holes 0,7; all positives have explicit circles
   and all negatives have exhaustive complementary-short-matching checks.
5. The finite completion/root accounting of Section 5 below, independently
   checkable from those complete tables. No Q5 T15 or Q6 theorem is used.

##### 1. Reduction to two geometries

Translate the first forbidden hole to 0. The second forbidden hole is
even, so by coordinate permutations it is 3 or 15. Let s,t be the two
other holes. A coordinate splitting both the forbidden pair and {s,t}
puts two same-parity holes in each face. Such a coordinate exists exactly
when supp(x xor y) intersects supp(s xor t).

In that case the claim follows for positive crossing count by pairing
the first-face ports, using N14 there, deleting the artificial pairs,
attaching crossings, compressing on the second face, using N14 there,
and expanding. The crossing count is even because each face has two
original holes. At zero crossings, Q4_RICH_GLUING supplies common
optional edges; deleting them and adding the two corresponding short
crossings joins the two 15-cycles into the desired 30-cycle.

If the forbidden distance is four, the support of s xor t is nonempty
and has even size, hence cannot be confined to the sole coordinate
outside the forbidden difference. Thus this split always exists.

For forbidden holes 0,3 and no such split, s and t agree in coordinates
0 and 1 and differ in two of the other three. The subgroup preserving
the unordered pair {0,3} consists of translations by 0 or 3, permutations
of coordinates 0,1, and permutations of coordinates 2,3,4. Its 18 eligible
unordered pairs {s,t} fall into three orbits of size six, represented by

    {12,20}, {5,9}, {5,29}.

This finite geometric claim can also be checked by enumerating all 91
pairs of remaining even vertices, as in t15_analytic_geometry.py/.json.
For {5,9}, all four holes lie in one coordinate face. More generally any
such same-face geometry is handled as follows. At positive crossings,
pair ports in the hole face, use Q4 T44_4, delete the nonempty artificial
matching, transfer and compress onto the other face, and use Fink's
perfect-matching circle extension there. At zero crossings use input 3.

Only the representatives {0,3,12,20} and {0,3,5,29}, forbidden {0,3},
remain. Section 2 puts both into a common canonical cut description.

##### 2. The canonical one-hole/three-hole cut

In the first representative split coordinate 0 and let A be the odd
face. It has the sole hole 3, which is forbidden. Drop coordinate 0 and
translate both faces by local vector 1. In their common Q4 labels A has
sole forbidden hole 0; B has holes {1,7,11}, with 1 forbidden.

In the second representative split coordinate 0 and let A be the even
face, whose sole forbidden hole is 0. Dropping that coordinate without
translation gives B holes {1,2,14}, with 1 forbidden.

Thus it suffices to handle either target pair (f,g)=(7,11) or (2,14),
with A's sole original hole 0, B's original holes {1,f,g}, and 0_A,1_B
the prescribed forbidden vertices. The B holes are all odd in the shared
local labeling. The A forbidden hole is even locally; their global
parities agree as required. New bridges join equal local labels.

Write C for original crossing edges, X_A,X_B for their endpoint sets,
and c=|C|. Then c is odd and positive: the original matching covers 15
vertices in A. Also c<=13 because B has three holes. Required crossing
edges may connect arbitrary labels; their actual partners are retained.

##### 3. Local path availability from the complete tables

Choose d in X_A and a perfect matching D on X_A minus {d}. Put
L=F_A union D, whose holes are 0,d. For any odd z different from d, z is
covered by L; write k=L(z) and set

    T_z = L - {zk} + {dk}.

Its holes are 0,z. A 14-cycle on Q4 minus {0,z}, containing T_z and
using short new edges, yields a 15-vertex d--z path on A minus 0:
delete dk to open the cycle between d,k and append the original edge kz.
Conversely any such path ends at z via zk, since zk is its required
matching edge; removing z and adding dk gives the 14-cycle. The new edge
dk is artificial and is removed in the forward construction.

Consequently the audited Q4 tables decide exactly which (d,D,z) work.
For z=d the path with equal endpoints is disallowed. If z is one of
f,g and some choice works, the safe free-hole transfer in Section 4
already proves the canonical claim. Otherwise use the full availability
classification in Section 5.

##### 4. Safe and occupied endpoint transfers

Suppose a path P as above has been chosen with odd endpoint z != 1.
Delete D and attach all original crossing edges. Also attach the new
short bridge from z_A to z_B. All A vertices except 0 have degree two:
at d the crossing edge supplies the missing endpoint degree; at z the
bridge supplies it. If z is itself a port, deleting D removes its sole
path edge, so z is temporarily isolated; its original crossing plus
the bridge restore degree two. This boundary is included, not excluded.

###### Safe endpoint z outside X_B

The attached B vertices are distinct. The graph is a path forest with
endpoints X_B union {z_B}, and its interiors partition A minus 0.
Compress it to a matching R on that endpoint set.

If z is f or g, F_B union R is a matching with precisely two same-parity
holes, including 1. Q4 N14 omits 1 and gives a 15-cycle; expanding R
produces the required 30-cycle.

If z is not f or g, it is internally covered by F_B, since z != 1 and
z is not a port. Write k=F_B(z), q=R(z). Suppress the two-edge path
k--z--q by replacing zk,zq with kq. The resulting matching has holes
{1,f,g,z}, four odd vertices. Q4 T44_4 avoids 1,z. Expanding kq restores
z and its original matching edge together with the transfer path;
expanding all remaining R edges restores A minus 0. The result has
14+1+15=30 vertices and omits exactly 0_A,1_B.

###### Occupied endpoint z in X_B

Assume c>=3 and choose the root d to be the original A partner of z_B.
Availability in Section 3 ensures d != z. The matching D is nonempty.
Every edge of D occurs on P, so deleting D separates P's endpoints d,z
into different components, even when z is a port and becomes isolated.
After all original crossings have been attached, these components remain
different: each attachment adds a distinct B endpoint. Adding bridge
z_A z_B joins the z component to the endpoint z_B already attached at d.
It creates no cycle. If z is an A port, its separate original crossing
attaches at another B port because the crossing partners of d and z are
distinct. Thus the temporarily isolated case also gives a path, not a
closed component.

All resulting components are paths with endpoints X_B minus {z_B},
and their interiors partition (A minus 0) union {z_B}. Compress to R.
Now F_B union R has exactly the four odd holes {1,f,g,z}; apply Q4 T44_4
avoiding 1,z and expand. Again this gives the required 30-cycle.

Only c=1 is excluded from occupied transfer: D would be empty and the
two attachments would close a separate A-side cycle. Section 5 always
provides a safe endpoint when c=1.

##### 5. Complete finite coverage of choices of roots and pairings

For each odd z, inverse-enumerate the bad near-perfect states (d,L) from
the audited negative tables. Given a negative T with holes 0,z and any
oriented edge dk of T, the inverse state is

    L = T - {dk} + {zk}, with root d.

Every failed state with z != d is included, by the forward equivalence
in Section 3. Add the special failure z=d when testing availability.
To fail both fixed targets f,g, at least one of them is different from
d; therefore the union of these two inverse lists contains every possible
double-failure state. Intersecting the two failure conditions gives 256
states for (7,11) and 187 for (2,14).

For a fixed odd crossing count c, an internal partial matching F_A has
(15-c)/2 edges. Its completions are the c choices of d and the
(c-2)!! pairings D of the other ports, totaling c(c-2)!! distinct states.
The convention (-1)!!=1 applies for c=1. Each completion (d,L) contains
F_A. Enumerate every submatching of the double-failure states of the
required size and count its occurrences. It is a stalled partial
matching exactly when the count is c(c-2)!!; any partial not enumerated
or with a smaller count has a successful fixed-target completion.

The complete stalled partial counts are:

| c | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 | 11 | 13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| f,g=7,11 |256|210|42|2|0|0|0|
| f,g=2,14 |187|110|21|1|0|0|0|

For each stalled F_A and each odd z, count failed completions separately
for each root d. At a fixed d there are (c-2)!! completions; d is a good
root for z exactly when z != d and fewer than all those completions are
in the inverse negative list. This respects the necessary quantifier:
for a good root one may then select an appropriate D.

Let G be all odd z != 1 with at least one good root. If |G|>c, some
z in G is outside X_B, and the safe transfer works. This holds for all
stalled inputs with c=1.

For the remaining inputs, c>=3. If any z in G lies outside X_B we again
use the safe transfer. Otherwise G is a subset of X_B. The original
crossing partners define an injective map phi:G -> X_A. If phi(z) is a
good root for any z, the occupied transfer applies. Failure would require
an injection assigning EVERY z in G to one of its bad roots.

[t44_canonical_completion_probe.py](research/six_directions/t44_canonical_completion_probe.py) exhaustively tests this finite
injection condition for every stalled partial in the table. In every
case either |G|>c or no such bad-root injection exists. The unresolved
count is zero at every c for both target pairs. It stores all partials,
all good-root sets, exact failed-completion counts, and the injection
test outcome in [t44_canonical_completion_probe.json](research/six_directions/t44_canonical_completion_probe.json).

This checks all possible crossing endpoint sets and all partner bijections
without enumerating them: if G is not contained in X_B a safe endpoint
exists, and if it is contained there its actual partner map is one of the
injections ruled out above. No assumption of short original crossing
edges is used. No random matching test supplies a universal step.

##### Conclusion and scope

The split lemma, same-face lemma and the two canonical completion
arguments exhaust the normalized four-hole geometries, proving T44_5
relative to the stated finite certificates and gluing inputs, subject to
their independent audits. In particular the canonical occupied transfer
allows an endpoint that is itself an A port, a boundary not needed in
the earlier, more restrictive A4 canonical proof.

T44_5 gives the adjacent-hole reduction for Q5 T15: if its minority hole
is short-adjacent to a nonforbidden majority hole, add that short edge
and apply T44_5 to the remaining four majority holes, avoiding the
prescribed two. It does not prove the nonadjacent T15 core or EP0, and
does not close full eight-hole P6 or the higher 10--18-hole layers.


</details>


<details id="proof-t44-sameface-zero-crossing" class="source-doc" markdown="1">
<summary>T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md — T44 same-face zero-crossing gluing — proof draft</summary>

原件：[打开文件](research/six_directions/T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING.md)。SHA-256：`bfe89f0cb0044a847430769727bde8e731debd0cab1c59f5d516408f6b9b5e32`。

关联审计（以其实际接受范围为准）：[T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING_REVIEW.json](research/six_directions/T44_SAMEFACE_ZERO_CROSSING_REVIEW.json)。

#### T44 same-face zero-crossing gluing — proof draft

Date: 2026-11-01. ARIS proof-writer package. This closes one specified
transfer branch relative to the imported Q4 perfect-endpoint classification;
it does not claim the full T44_5 or T15 target.

##### Claim

Let $F$ be an arbitrary matching of $K(Q_5)$ with precisely four holes,
all of one parity. Let $x,y$ be two prescribed holes. Suppose some
coordinate cut $Q_5=A\cup B$ has all four holes in $A$ and no required
edge of $F$ crossing the cut. Then there is a cycle on exactly
$Q_5\setminus\{x,y\}$ containing every edge of $F$ and adding only
short edges.

The original required edges may be long or same-parity. No shortness
assumption is imposed on $F_A$ or $F_B$.

##### Status

PROVABLE AS STATED, relative to the explicitly imported finite Q4
perfect-endpoint classification and the positive path certificates
checked below. Independent review of this new proof package is requested.

The dedicated verifier completed with **PASS**: $311850$ matching
records, $2486610$ explicit positive paths, and all $216$ low-endpoint
rows passed. The endpoint-count histogram is
$\{3:180,4:36,5:10,6:1040,7:5036,8:305548\}$.

##### Notation and dependencies

Identify both coordinate faces with the same Q4, so corresponding
vertices differ by the deleted coordinate. Write $\bar v$ for the
corresponding vertex in the other face. The map $v\mapsto\bar v$
preserves Q4 distances; as a Q5 map it reverses global parity.

For a perfect matching $P$ of $K(Q_4)$ and a root $r$, let $G(P,r)$
be the set of opposite-parity endpoints of Hamilton paths starting at
$r$, containing all of $P$ and adding only short edges.

Imported input: [Q4_PERFECT_ENDPOINT_ABUNDANCE.md](#proof-q4-perfect-endpoint-abundance) proves that
$|G(P,r)|\ge4$. Its complete bad-endpoint classification, in
[q4_perfect_endpoint_abundance_check.json](research/six_directions/q4_perfect_endpoint_abundance_check.json), has 4708 exceptional
perfect matchings at root $0$, with their exact bad odd endpoint sets.
Every nonexceptional matching has at most one bad odd endpoint.

This proof uses two finite statements:

1. The exceptional bad sets contain none of the endpoint triples in
   Section 1 below.
2. The 30 normalized T44 inputs have complete positive path witnesses
   satisfying the endpoint alternative in Section 2 below.

The dedicated independent checker is
